sn.e: Two weeks later the cousin comes to my house.

sn.s: Viene solo, sin avisar, un domingo en la tarde.
sn.e: He comes alone, without warning, on a Sunday afternoon.

sn.s: Se sienta en el patio y hablamos tres horas.
sn.e: He sits down in the yard and we talk for three hours.

sn.s: Yo le contesto todo lo que me pregunta, sin adornar.
sn.e: I answer everything he asks me, without dressing it up.

sn.s: Y le digo lo que va a extrañar y no sabe todavía.
sn.e: And I tell him what he is going to miss and does not know yet.

sn.s: Le digo que va a extrañar la bulla, y él se ríe.
sn.e: I tell him he is going to miss the racket, and he laughs.

sn.s: Se ríe igual que me reí yo cuando me lo dijeron.
sn.e: He laughs the same way I laughed when they told me.

sn.s: En abril el primo se va y yo no voy a la terminal.
sn.e: In April the cousin leaves and I do not go to the terminal.

sn.s: No me toca ir, yo no soy de la familia de él.
sn.e: It is not my place to go, I am not his family.

sn.s: Pero Marcos me llama esa noche desde su casa.
sn.e: But Marcos calls me that night from his house.

sn.s: Solo para decirme que ya se fue y que llegó bien.
sn.e: Just to tell me he has gone and arrived safely.

sn.s: Marcos y yo nos conocimos hace cinco años y medio.
sn.e: Marcos and I met five and a half years ago.

sn.s: Nos conocimos en el taller, el segundo día que llegué.
sn.e: We met in the workshop, the second day I arrived.

sn.s: Él me enseñó dónde estaba el baño y dónde el agua.
sn.e: He showed me where the toilet was and where the water was.

sn.s: Y después me enseñó todo lo demás, durante cinco años.
sn.e: And then he taught me everything else, over five years.

sn.s: Aquí una amistad no se declara nunca.
sn.e: Here a friendship is never declared.

sn.s: Nadie dice somos amigos, eso no se dice.
sn.e: Nobody says we are friends, that is not said.

sn.s: La amistad se ve en lo que uno hace, no en lo que dice.
sn.e: The friendship shows in what you do, not what you say.

sn.s: Y hay una lista de cosas que hacen los amigos.
sn.e: And there is a list of things friends do.

sn.s: La primera es que uno llega sin avisar.
sn.e: The first is that you arrive without warning.

sn.s: Un amigo de verdad no llama antes de venir.
sn.e: A real friend does not call before coming.

sn.s: Llamar antes es de gente que no es de la casa.
sn.e: Calling first is for people who are not of the house.

sn.s: Marcos llega a mi casa un domingo cualquiera.
sn.e: Marcos arrives at my house any given Sunday.

sn.s: Se sienta en el patio y agarra un vaso él solo.
sn.e: He sits down in the yard and gets himself a glass.

sn.s: La segunda es que uno se aparece cuando hay problema.
sn.e: The second is that you turn up when there is trouble.

sn.s: No hay que pedirlo y no hay que avisar.
sn.e: You do not have to ask and you do not have to tell.

sn.s: Cuando el niño estuvo en el hospital dos noches.
sn.e: When the boy was in hospital for two nights.

sn.s: Marcos llegó la primera noche a las once.
sn.e: Marcos arrived the first night at eleven.

sn.s: No hizo nada, no podía hacer nada, se quedó ahí.
sn.e: He did nothing, he could do nothing, he stayed there.

sn.s: Se sentó en el pasillo conmigo hasta las cuatro.
sn.e: He sat in the corridor with me until four.

sn.s: Acompañar es el verbo entero de esa amistad.
sn.e: Acompañar is the whole verb of that friendship.

sn.s: No ayudar, no resolver, acompañar nada más.
sn.e: Not helping, not solving, just accompanying.

sn.s: Y eso es lo que aquí se espera de un amigo.
sn.e: And that is what is expected of a friend here.

sn.s: La tercera es la plata, que es la más delicada.
sn.e: The third is money, which is the most delicate.

sn.s: Entre amigos se presta y no se cobra.
sn.e: Between friends you lend and you do not chase.

sn.s: Uno presta lo que puede perder, y ya.
sn.e: You lend what you can afford to lose, and that is that.

sn.s: Si vuelve, bueno, y si no vuelve no se menciona.
sn.e: If it comes back, good, and if it does not it is not mentioned.

sn.s: Yo le he prestado a Marcos y él a mí.
sn.e: I have lent to Marcos and he to me.

sn.s: Y ninguno de los dos ha preguntado nunca.
sn.e: And neither of us has ever asked.

sn.s: La cuarta es la más rara para mí, y es la de los años.
sn.e: The fourth is the strangest for me, and it is the one about years.

sn.s: Aquí una amistad no se acaba, se apaga y se prende.
sn.e: Here a friendship does not end, it goes out and comes on again.

sn.s: Marcos tiene un amigo de la escuela que vive en León.
sn.e: Marcos has a friend from school who lives in León.

sn.s: No se ven hace nueve años y se hablan dos veces al año.
sn.e: They have not seen each other in nine years and talk twice a year.

sn.s: Y si ese hombre llega mañana, se queda en su casa.
sn.e: And if that man arrives tomorrow, he stays at his house.

sn.s: Sin preguntar cuánto tiempo y sin poner condiciones.
sn.e: Without asking how long and without conditions.

sn.s: Nueve años y la amistad está intacta, guardada.
sn.e: Nine years and the friendship is intact, kept.

sn.s: En mi país una amistad de nueve años sin verse ya no existe.
sn.e: In my country a friendship of nine years without meeting no longer exists.

sn.s: Aquí no se pierden, se dejan quietas.
sn.e: Here they are not lost, they are left still.

sn.s: En marzo Marcos me pide que sea el padrino del bautizo.
sn.e: In March Marcos asks me to be godfather at the christening.

sn.s: No de la hija grande, del último que le nació.
sn.e: Not of the eldest daughter, of the last one born to him.

sn.s: Ser padrino de bautizo no es lo mismo que de las sillas.
sn.e: Being a christening godfather is not the same as being godfather of the chairs.

sn.s: El padrino de bautizo se vuelve compadre del papá.
sn.e: The christening godfather becomes the father's compadre.

sn.s: Y compadre aquí es una palabra grande.
sn.e: And compadre here is a big word.

sn.s: Un compadre es familia sin ser de la sangre.
sn.e: A compadre is family without being blood.

sn.s: Si a Marcos le pasa algo, ese niño es problema mío.
sn.e: If something happens to Marcos, that boy is my problem.

sn.s: No de palabra, de verdad, y todos lo entienden así.
sn.e: Not in words, really, and everybody understands it that way.

sn.s: Yo le digo que sí antes de que termine de pedirlo.
sn.e: I say yes before he finishes asking.

sn.s: Y él me dice que ya sabía, que preguntó por la forma.
sn.e: And he tells me he already knew, that he asked for form's sake.

sn.s: En el bautizo la gente me dice compadre todo el día.
sn.e: At the christening people call me compadre all day.

sn.s: Y yo le digo compadre a Marcos por primera vez.
sn.e: And I call Marcos compadre for the first time.

sn.s: Después de cinco años y medio de decirle Marcos.
sn.e: After five and a half years of calling him Marcos.

sn.s: Suena raro las primeras diez veces y después no.
sn.e: It sounds strange the first ten times and then it does not.

sn.s: Doña Elena me dice que ya no me falta nada.
sn.e: Doña Elena tells me I am not missing anything now.

sn.s: Le digo que ella dijo eso también con los versos de Darío.
sn.e: I tell her she said that with the Darío lines too.

sn.s: Y con lo de la cédula, y con lo del baho.
sn.e: And with the ID card thing, and with the baho thing.

sn.s: Ella me dice que cada vez es cierto y cada vez falta algo.
sn.e: She tells me each time it is true and each time something is missing.

sn.s: Que así es esto y que no se acaba nunca.
sn.e: That that is how this is and it never finishes.

sn.s: Esa noche cuento los años que llevo aquí.
sn.e: That night I count the years I have been here.

sn.s: Cinco y medio, que no es nada, dicen todos.
sn.e: Five and a half, which is nothing, everybody says.

sn.s: Pero conté también las cosas que ya me deben.
sn.e: But I also counted the things people already owe me.

sn.s: Y las que yo debo, que son más.
sn.e: And the ones I owe, which are more.

sn.s: Un velorio al que fui, dos hospitales, tres mudanzas.
sn.e: A wake I went to, two hospitals, three house moves.

sn.s: Un techo, doscientas sillas y un bautizo.
sn.e: A roof, two hundred chairs and a christening.

sn.s: Eso no se junta en cinco años en ninguna parte.
sn.e: That is not accumulated in five years anywhere.

sn.s: Se junta cuando uno se queda en la misma cuadra.
sn.e: It is accumulated when you stay on the same block.

sn.s: En junio viajo a mi país por primera vez en cinco años.
sn.e: In June I travel to my country for the first time in five years.

sn.s: Voy solo porque los pasajes de los tres no alcanzaban.
sn.e: I go alone because the fares for the three of us were not enough.

sn.s: Voy tres semanas, que es lo que dan de vacaciones.
sn.e: I go for three weeks, which is what they give as holiday.

sn.s: El primer día allá me pasa una cosa en la calle.
sn.e: The first day over there something happens to me in the street.

sn.s: Camino tres cuadras y no saludo a nadie.
sn.e: I walk three blocks and greet nobody.

sn.s: Nadie me saluda a mí tampoco, y eso es normal allá.
sn.e: Nobody greets me either, and that is normal over there.

sn.s: Pero yo llevo cinco años saludando en cada esquina.
sn.e: But I have spent five years greeting people on every corner.

sn.s: Y el cuerpo me pide saludar y no hay a quién.
sn.e: And my body wants to greet and there is nobody to greet.

sn.s: Después está el silencio, que es lo que más me pega.
sn.e: Then there is the silence, which is what hits me most.

sn.s: Una calle a las nueve de la noche sin una sola persona.
sn.e: A street at nine at night without a single person.

sn.s: Sin música, sin perros, sin nadie en la acera.
sn.e: No music, no dogs, nobody on the pavement.

sn.s: Todo el mundo adentro de su casa con la puerta cerrada.
sn.e: Everybody inside their house with the door closed.

sn.s: Yo me acordé de la noche del campo cerca de Boaco.
sn.e: I remembered the night in the countryside near Boaco.

sn.s: Mi hermana me tiene tres semanas de comidas y visitas.
sn.e: My sister has three weeks of meals and visits lined up for me.

sn.s: Y en cada comida me preguntan por Nicaragua.
sn.e: And at every meal they ask me about Nicaragua.

sn.s: Me preguntan si es peligroso, todos, sin faltar uno.
sn.e: They ask me if it is dangerous, all of them, without fail.

sn.s: Yo les digo que no y no me creen del todo.
sn.e: I tell them no and they do not entirely believe me.

sn.s: Me preguntan si hay agua y si hay luz.
sn.e: They ask me if there is water and if there is electricity.

sn.s: Me preguntan cuándo voy a volver, y ahí está el problema.
sn.e: They ask me when I am going to come back, and there is the problem.

sn.s: Volver, dicen ellos, y quieren decir volver allá.
sn.e: Come back, they say, and they mean come back there.

sn.s: Y yo digo que en tres semanas vuelvo.
sn.e: And I say that in three weeks I am going back.

sn.s: Y ellos me dicen que no, que volver de verdad.
sn.e: And they tell me no, come back for real.

sn.s: Los dos usamos la misma palabra para dos lugares.
sn.e: We both use the same word for two places.

sn.s: Y ninguno de los dos se da cuenta al principio.
sn.e: And neither of us realises at first.

sn.s: Mi hermana lo nota como a la segunda semana.
sn.e: My sister notices it around the second week.

sn.s: Me dice que yo digo allá cuando hablo de aquí.
sn.e: She tells me I say over there when I talk about here.

sn.s: Y que digo aquí cuando hablo de Managua.
sn.e: And that I say here when I talk about Managua.

sn.s: Estando sentado en la cocina de mi mamá.
sn.e: Sitting in my mother's kitchen.

sn.s: No me di cuenta ni una vez de haberlo dicho.
sn.e: I did not notice once having said it.

sn.s: Las tres semanas se me hacen largas y eso me da culpa.
sn.e: The three weeks feel long to me and that gives me guilt.

sn.s: Es mi familia y los quiero y quiero irme.
sn.e: It is my family and I love them and I want to leave.

sn.s: Hablo con Lucía todas las noches por el teléfono.
sn.e: I talk to Lucía every night on the phone.

sn.s: Y en esas llamadas hablo español y me sale mejor.
sn.e: And in those calls I speak Spanish and it comes out better.

sn.s: Estoy hablando mi idioma todo el día con la gente.
sn.e: I am speaking my own language all day with people.

sn.s: Y las once de la noche con Lucía es cuando descanso.
sn.e: And eleven at night with Lucía is when I rest.

sn.s: Eso no se lo conté a nadie de allá.
sn.e: That I did not tell anybody over there.

sn.s: El día del regreso salgo de madrugada, con dos maletas.
sn.e: On the day of the return I leave before dawn, with two suitcases.

sn.s: Una maleta de ropa y una de cosas para la casa.
sn.e: One suitcase of clothes and one of things for the house.

sn.s: Cosas que aquí no se consiguen o son muy caras.
sn.e: Things you cannot get here or that are very expensive.

sn.s: Igual que las maletas de los que vuelven en diciembre.
sn.e: The same as the suitcases of the ones who come back in December.

sn.s: En el avión pienso en cómo se dice lo que estoy haciendo.
sn.e: On the plane I think about how you say what I am doing.

sn.s: No estoy viajando a Nicaragua, estoy volviendo.
sn.e: I am not travelling to Nicaragua, I am coming back.

sn.s: Aterrizamos a las dos de la tarde en Managua.
sn.e: We land at two in the afternoon in Managua.

sn.s: Y la puerta del avión se abre y entra el calor.
sn.e: And the door of the plane opens and the heat comes in.

sn.s: Ese calor lo odié cinco años seguidos.
sn.e: That heat I hated for five straight years.

sn.s: El primer día que llegué pensé que no iba a aguantar.
sn.e: The first day I arrived I thought I was not going to be able to stand it.

sn.s: Y esta vez el calor me entra en la cara y algo se me acomoda.
sn.e: And this time the heat hits me in the face and something settles in me.

sn.s: Me quedo parado en la escalera del avión un segundo.
sn.e: I stand on the plane steps for a second.

sn.s: Con el olor de aquí, que es de tierra y de humo.
sn.e: With the smell of here, which is of earth and smoke.

sn.s: Un olor que yo no sabía que conocía.
sn.e: A smell I did not know I knew.

sn.s: Lucía está afuera con el niño en el hombro.
sn.e: Lucía is outside with the boy on her shoulder.

sn.s: El niño no me reconoce en los primeros diez segundos.
sn.e: The boy does not recognise me in the first ten seconds.

sn.s: Tiene tres años y tres semanas es mucho tiempo.
sn.e: He is three and three weeks is a long time.

sn.s: Después me reconoce y no me suelta hasta la casa.
sn.e: Then he recognises me and does not let go of me until home.

sn.s: En el taxi hablo español sin pensarlo ni un segundo.
sn.e: In the taxi I speak Spanish without a second's thought.

sn.s: Y me doy cuenta en la mitad del camino.
sn.e: And I realise halfway along the road.

sn.s: Que no cambié de idioma, se cambió solo.
sn.e: That I did not change language, it changed on its own.

sn.s: Llegamos al barrio y el vecino tiene música puesta.
sn.e: We get to the barrio and the neighbour has music on.

sn.s: Doña Chepa me grita desde la pulpería que ya volví.
sn.e: Doña Chepa shouts at me from the shop that I am back.

sn.s: No me pregunta, me lo dice, que es distinto.
sn.e: She does not ask me, she tells me, which is different.

sn.s: Don Beto está en la acera y levanta la mano.
sn.e: Don Beto is on the pavement and raises his hand.

sn.s: No nos decimos nada porque nos vemos mañana.
sn.e: We do not say anything to each other because we will see each other tomorrow.

sn.s: Abro el portón de mi casa a las cuatro de la tarde.
sn.e: I open the gate of my house at four in the afternoon.

sn.s: Y adentro huele a la comida que hizo Lucía.
sn.e: And inside it smells of the food Lucía made.

sn.s: Ella hizo lo que yo pido siempre después de un viaje.
sn.e: She made what I always ask for after a trip.

sn.s: Gallo pinto, que es lo primero que comí en este país.
sn.e: Gallo pinto, which is the first thing I ate in this country.

sn.s: En septiembre llega un muchacho nuevo a la fábrica.
sn.e: In September a new boy arrives at the factory.

sn.s: Se llama Tom y es canadiense y tiene veinticuatro años.
sn.e: His name is Tom, he is Canadian and he is twenty-four.

sn.s: Viene con un proyecto de dos años y estudió español.
sn.e: He comes with a two-year project and he studied Spanish.

sn.s: El jefe me lo manda a mí el primer día.
sn.e: The boss sends him to me on the first day.

sn.s: Me lo manda sin decir por qué, pero yo sé por qué.
sn.e: He sends him without saying why, but I know why.

sn.s: Tom llega hablando un español muy correcto y muy raro.
sn.e: Tom arrives speaking a very correct and very strange Spanish.

sn.s: Habla como el libro que yo tenía hace cinco años.
sn.e: He talks like the book I had five years ago.

sn.s: Le dice tú a todo el mundo, sin excepción.
sn.e: He says tú to everybody, without exception.

sn.s: Le dice tú a don Emilio, que tiene setenta y tres.
sn.e: He says tú to don Emilio, who is seventy-three.

sn.s: Don Emilio no le dice nada y se voltea.
sn.e: Don Emilio says nothing to him and turns away.

sn.s: Y Tom no se da cuenta de que pasó algo.
sn.e: And Tom does not notice that something happened.

sn.s: Yo me acuerdo exactamente de esa cara de no darse cuenta.
sn.e: I remember exactly that face of not noticing.

sn.s: Esa tarde me lo llevo a comer y le explico lo del vos.
sn.e: That afternoon I take him to eat and explain the vos thing to him.

sn.s: Le digo que el tú aquí suena a telenovela mexicana.
sn.e: I tell him that tú here sounds like a Mexican soap opera.

sn.s: Que hay que decir vos, o usted, según con quién.
sn.e: That you have to say vos, or usted, depending on who.

sn.s: Él me pregunta cuál es la regla de cuándo va cada uno.
sn.e: He asks me what the rule is for when each one goes.

sn.s: Y yo abro la boca para explicársela y no puedo.
sn.e: And I open my mouth to explain it to him and I cannot.

sn.s: Porque no hay una regla, hay como veinte.
sn.e: Because there is not one rule, there are about twenty.

sn.s: Le digo lo que puedo y sé que no le va a servir.
sn.e: I tell him what I can and I know it will not help him.

sn.s: Le digo que a los viejos usted y a los del taller vos.
sn.e: I tell him usted to old people and vos to the workshop men.

sn.s: Le digo que a un jefe usted y a un compadre vos.
sn.e: I tell him usted to a boss and vos to a compadre.

sn.s: Y que hay gente que le va a decir vos primero.
sn.e: And that there are people who will say vos to him first.

sn.s: Y que ahí cambia todo y ya se puede.
sn.e: And that there everything changes and then you can.

sn.s: Tom apunta todo en un cuaderno mientras yo hablo.
sn.e: Tom writes everything in a notebook while I talk.

sn.s: Y yo me veo a mí mismo apuntando refranes hace años.
sn.e: And I see myself writing down sayings years ago.

sn.s: Le digo que el cuaderno no le va a servir de mucho.
sn.e: I tell him the notebook is not going to help him much.

sn.s: Él me pregunta qué le va a servir entonces.
sn.e: He asks me what is going to help him then.

sn.s: Y yo le digo la verdad, que es una respuesta fea.
sn.e: And I tell him the truth, which is an ugly answer.

sn.s: Le digo que le va a servir quedarse dos años.
sn.e: I tell him what will help him is staying two years.

sn.s: Que no hay otra cosa y que yo lo intenté todo.
sn.e: That there is nothing else and that I tried everything.

sn.s: Los primeros meses me busca para todo lo que no entiende.
sn.e: The first months he comes to me for everything he does not understand.

sn.s: Me pregunta por qué la gente le dice mi amor en la fritanga.
sn.e: He asks me why people call him mi amor at the fritanga.

sn.s: Me pregunta qué quiere decir ahorita, exactamente.
sn.e: He asks me what ahorita means, exactly.

sn.s: Yo le digo que ahorita no quiere decir nada exacto.
sn.e: I tell him that ahorita does not mean anything exact.

sn.s: Me pregunta por qué el jefe le dijo depende.
sn.e: He asks me why the boss said depende to him.

sn.s: Me pregunta si un vecino se enojó con él o no.
sn.e: He asks me if a neighbour got angry with him or not.

sn.s: Cada pregunta suya es una que yo hice hace años.
sn.e: Every question of his is one I asked years ago.

sn.s: Y a mí me las contestó Marcos, todas.
sn.e: And Marcos answered mine, all of them.

sn.s: Un día me oigo diciéndole a Tom una frase.
sn.e: One day I hear myself saying a sentence to Tom.

sn.s: Le digo que aquí se hace así, y no explico más.
sn.e: I tell him that here it is done this way, and I explain no further.

sn.s: Y ahí me paro, con el desarmador en la mano.
sn.e: And there I stop, with the screwdriver in my hand.

sn.s: Porque esa es la frase que a mí me daban de niño.
sn.e: Because that is the sentence they used to give me like a child.

sn.s: Y yo me enojaba, porque quería una razón.
sn.e: And I used to get angry, because I wanted a reason.

sn.s: Aquí se hace así no es una razón, es una costumbre.
sn.e: Aquí se hace así is not a reason, it is a custom.

sn.s: Y me tomó cinco años entender que es lo mismo.
sn.e: And it took me five years to understand it is the same thing.

sn.s: En diciembre invito a Tom a la casa para la gritería.
sn.e: In December I invite Tom to the house for the gritería.

sn.s: Llega a las cinco, temprano, porque yo le dije la hora real.
sn.e: He arrives at five, early, because I told him the real time.

sn.s: Le expliqué que la gritería sí empieza a la hora.
sn.e: I explained to him that the gritería does start on time.

sn.s: Y que casi nada más en este país empieza a la hora.
sn.e: And that almost nothing else in this country starts on time.

sn.s: Él se queda parado al lado del altar sin saber qué hacer.
sn.e: He stands beside the altar not knowing what to do.

sn.s: Y cuando llega el primer grupo de niños, él no grita.
sn.e: And when the first group of children arrives, he does not shout.

sn.s: Se queda callado mirando, con la boca cerrada.
sn.e: He stays quiet watching, with his mouth closed.

sn.s: Igual que yo el primer año, exactamente igual.
sn.e: The same as me the first year, exactly the same.

sn.s: Yo grito la respuesta con Lucía y con doña Carmen.
sn.e: I shout the answer with Lucía and with doña Carmen.

sn.s: Y en el segundo grupo Tom grita también, mal.
sn.e: And with the second group Tom shouts too, badly.

sn.s: Grita tarde y grita la mitad de las palabras.
sn.e: He shouts late and shouts half the words.

sn.s: Yo no lo corrijo porque no hay nada que corregir.
sn.e: I do not correct him because there is nothing to correct.

sn.s: A la cuarta casa le va a salir mejor.
sn.e: By the fourth house it will come out better.

sn.s: Y en dos años le va a salir sin pensarlo.
sn.e: And in two years it will come out without his thinking.

sn.s: Cuando se va esa noche me da la mano en el portón.
sn.e: When he leaves that night he shakes my hand at the gate.

sn.s: Y me dice gracias, en español, y se queda ahí.
sn.e: And he says thank you, in Spanish, and stays there.

sn.s: Se queda parado como esperando algo más.
sn.e: He stands there as if waiting for something else.

sn.s: Yo lo dejo ahí parado como veinte minutos.
sn.e: I leave him standing there for about twenty minutes.

sn.s: Hablando del trabajo y del calor y del bus.
sn.e: Talking about work and the heat and the bus.

sn.s: Porque una despedida en el portón se hace despacio.
sn.e: Because a goodbye at the gate is done slowly.

sn.s: Y eso no se lo voy a explicar, lo va a aprender.
sn.e: And that I am not going to explain to him, he is going to learn it.

sn.s: La pregunta llega siempre en el mismo momento.
sn.e: The question always comes at the same moment.

sn.s: Llega cuando alguien nuevo se sienta al lado mío.
sn.e: It comes when somebody new sits down beside me.

sn.s: Me pregunta de dónde soy y espera una palabra.
sn.e: He asks me where I am from and waits for one word.

sn.s: Durante cinco años yo dije el nombre de mi país.
sn.e: For five years I said the name of my country.

sn.s: Lo decía rápido, para pasar a otra cosa.
sn.e: I said it fast, to move on to something else.

sn.s: Y después venían las mismas cuatro preguntas de siempre.
sn.e: And then came the same four questions as always.

sn.s: Este año empecé a contestar de otra manera.
sn.e: This year I started answering another way.

sn.s: Ahora digo que vivo aquí y después digo de dónde vine.
sn.e: Now I say I live here and then I say where I came from.

sn.s: En ese orden, que no es el mismo orden.
sn.e: In that order, which is not the same order.

sn.s: Y la conversación se va para otro lado enseguida.
sn.e: And the conversation goes somewhere else straight away.

sn.s: Me preguntan de qué barrio y ahí ya estamos hablando.
sn.e: They ask me which barrio and there we are already talking.

sn.s: Lucía me dice que yo cambié el orden a propósito.
sn.e: Lucía tells me I changed the order on purpose.

sn.s: Y es cierto, aunque me tomó años darme cuenta.
sn.e: And it is true, though it took me years to realise.

sn.s: Lo que no cambió es lo de adentro, que sigue partido.
sn.e: What did not change is the inside, which is still split.

sn.s: Hay días en que este país me queda ajeno.
sn.e: There are days when this country feels ajeno to me.

sn.s: Son pocos y son cortos, pero no se han ido.
sn.e: They are few and they are short, but they have not gone.

sn.s: Me pasa en las conversaciones de la guerra.
sn.e: It happens to me in the conversations about the war.

sn.s: Me pasa cuando cantan el himno en la escuela del niño.
sn.e: It happens when they sing the anthem at the boy's school.

sn.s: Todo el mundo se lo sabe y yo no me lo sé.
sn.e: Everybody knows it and I do not.

sn.s: Y no me lo voy a aprender, aunque podría.
sn.e: And I am not going to learn it, though I could.

sn.s: Aprendérmelo sería estar actuando de algo.
sn.e: Learning it would be acting at being something.

sn.s: Y hay días en que mi país me queda ajeno también.
sn.e: And there are days when my own country feels ajeno too.

sn.s: Eso fue lo que no vi venir en cinco años.
sn.e: That was what I did not see coming in five years.

sn.s: Cuando fui en junio no me hallé allá tampoco.
sn.e: When I went in June no me hallé over there either.

sn.s: No me hallé en la casa donde crecí, con mi propia familia.
sn.e: I did not find myself in the house where I grew up, with my own family.

sn.s: Y de eso no se puede hablar con nadie de allá.
sn.e: And that cannot be talked about with anybody over there.

sn.s: Porque suena a que uno los está despreciando.
sn.e: Because it sounds as if you were looking down on them.

sn.s: Y no es eso, no es nada parecido a eso.
sn.e: And it is not that, it is nothing like that.

sn.s: Marcos me dijo una vez cómo se llama esto.
sn.e: Marcos told me once what this is called.

sn.s: Me dijo que es lo mismo que le pasa a Roberto.
sn.e: He told me it is the same thing that happens to Roberto.

sn.s: Que Roberto en Costa Rica es el nica.
sn.e: That Roberto in Costa Rica is the nica.

sn.s: Y que aquí ya le dicen el de Costa Rica.
sn.e: And that here they already call him the one from Costa Rica.

sn.s: Y que no hay ningún lugar donde a Roberto no le pongan algo.
sn.e: And that there is nowhere where they do not put something on Roberto.

sn.s: Yo le dije que a mí me pasa igual, con menos años.
sn.e: I told him that the same happens to me, with fewer years.

sn.s: Él me dijo que sin embargo hay una diferencia.
sn.e: He told me that even so there is a difference.

sn.s: Que Roberto se fue por hambre y yo me vine por gusto.
sn.e: That Roberto left out of hunger and I came by choice.

sn.s: Y que esa diferencia lo cambia todo aunque duela igual.
sn.e: And that that difference changes everything though it hurts the same.

sn.s: Eso me lo dijo hace dos años y yo lo pensé mucho.
sn.e: He told me that two years ago and I thought about it a lot.

sn.s: Y creo que tiene razón, aunque no en todo.
sn.e: And I think he is right, though not in everything.

sn.s: La parte de la frontera sí es distinta, es cierto.
sn.e: The border part is different, that is true.

sn.s: Yo puedo salir y volver y nadie me detiene.
sn.e: I can leave and come back and nobody stops me.

sn.s: Roberto pasa Peñas Blancas con la mano temblando.
sn.e: Roberto crosses Peñas Blancas with his hand shaking.

sn.s: Eso no es lo mismo y no voy a decir que sí.
sn.e: That is not the same and I am not going to say it is.

sn.s: Pero la otra parte, la de adentro, sí es la misma.
sn.e: But the other part, the inside one, is the same.

sn.s: Los dos tenemos una casa donde ya no encajamos entero.
sn.e: We both have a house where we no longer fit whole.

sn.s: Y otra donde encajamos casi, que es peor.
sn.e: And another where we almost fit, which is worse.

sn.s: Lucía me pregunta si me arrepiento de haberme quedado.
sn.e: Lucía asks me if I regret having stayed.

sn.s: Se lo pregunta en la cocina, un martes, sin aviso.
sn.e: She asks me in the kitchen, on a Tuesday, without warning.

sn.s: Yo le digo que no y ella me dice que piense bien.
sn.e: I tell her no and she tells me to think properly.

sn.s: Me dice que no le conteste rápido por quedar bien.
sn.e: She tells me not to answer fast just to come out well.

sn.s: Entonces lo pienso de verdad como un minuto.
sn.e: So I really think about it for about a minute.

sn.s: Y la respuesta sigue siendo que no, pero es más larga.
sn.e: And the answer is still no, but it is longer.

sn.s: Le digo que no me arrepiento y que perdí cosas.
sn.e: I tell her I do not regret it and that I lost things.

sn.s: Que perdí ver a mi mamá envejecer de a poco.
sn.e: That I lost seeing my mother grow old bit by bit.

sn.s: Que la vi de golpe, cinco años más vieja en una tarde.
sn.e: That I saw her all at once, five years older in one afternoon.

sn.s: Que eso no se recupera y nadie me lo va a devolver.
sn.e: That that is not recovered and nobody is going to give it back to me.

sn.s: Y que aun así no me arrepiento, y las dos cosas son ciertas.
sn.e: And that even so I do not regret it, and both things are true.

sn.s: Lucía no me dice nada y sigue picando cebolla.
sn.e: Lucía says nothing to me and goes on chopping onion.

sn.s: A los cinco minutos me dice que ella tampoco.
sn.e: Five minutes later she tells me she does not either.

sn.s: Y yo no le había preguntado nada a ella.
sn.e: And I had not asked her anything.

sn.s: Ella también perdió cosas por quedarse conmigo.
sn.e: She lost things too by staying with me.

sn.s: Un pasaporte de otro país que no quiso pedir.
sn.e: A passport from another country that she did not want to ask for.

sn.s: Una hermana que le dijo que se estaba equivocando.
sn.e: A sister who told her she was making a mistake.

sn.s: De eso nunca hablamos y esa tarde tampoco.
sn.e: We never talk about that and we did not that afternoon either.

sn.s: La cebolla estaba picada y ella cambió de tema.
sn.e: The onion was chopped and she changed the subject.

sn.s: Yo la dejé cambiarlo, porque ya sé cómo se hace.
sn.e: I let her change it, because I know how it is done now.

sn.s: Estoy esperando el bus en una parada del centro.
sn.e: I am waiting for the bus at a stop in the centre.

sn.s: Es un martes en la tarde y hace un calor bárbaro.
sn.e: It is a Tuesday afternoon and it is savagely hot.

sn.s: Somos como diez personas esperando la misma ruta.
sn.e: There are about ten of us waiting for the same route.

sn.s: Un señor de unos cincuenta años me habla del calor.
sn.e: A man of about fifty talks to me about the heat.

sn.s: Me dice que este año está peor que el pasado.
sn.e: He tells me this year is worse than last.

sn.s: Yo le digo que sí y le digo lo del agua en agosto.
sn.e: I tell him yes and I tell him about the water in August.

sn.s: Él me cuenta que a él se le metió también.
sn.e: He tells me it got into his place too.

sn.s: Hablamos como diez minutos de agua y de alcaldía.
sn.e: We talk for about ten minutes about water and the town hall.

sn.s: Nos quejamos los dos con las mismas frases.
sn.e: We complain, the two of us, with the same phrases.

sn.s: Él dice ni modo y yo digo que ni modo.
sn.e: He says ni modo and I say ni modo.

sn.s: Llega el bus y nos subimos y yo me siento atrás.
sn.e: The bus comes and we get on and I sit at the back.

sn.s: Y como a las cinco cuadras me doy cuenta de una cosa.
sn.e: And about five blocks later I realise something.

sn.s: El señor no me preguntó de dónde soy.
sn.e: The man did not ask me where I am from.

sn.s: No me lo preguntó ni una sola vez en diez minutos.
sn.e: He did not ask me once in ten minutes.

sn.s: Y esa es la primera vez en cinco años y medio.
sn.e: And that is the first time in five and a half years.

sn.s: Un desconocido en una parada, diez minutos de conversación.
sn.e: A stranger at a bus stop, ten minutes of conversation.

sn.s: Y ni una pregunta de dónde vengo ni por qué estoy aquí.
sn.e: And not one question about where I come from or why I am here.

sn.s: Los primeros años era la primera pregunta, siempre.
sn.e: The first years it was the first question, always.

sn.s: Antes del nombre, antes de todo, de dónde sos.
sn.e: Before the name, before everything, where are you from.

sn.s: Y siempre por el acento, no por la cara.
sn.e: And always because of the accent, not the face.

sn.s: Aquí hay cheles nicaragüenses en todas partes.
sn.e: Here there are light-skinned Nicaraguans everywhere.

sn.s: Nadie me miraba y decía extranjero por el color.
sn.e: Nobody looked at me and said foreigner because of the colour.

sn.s: Me abrían la boca y ahí sí, en la primera frase.
sn.e: I opened my mouth and there yes, in the first sentence.

sn.s: Después empezó a tardar más en pasar.
sn.e: Then it started taking longer to happen.

sn.s: Al tercer año la pregunta llegaba a los cinco minutos.
sn.e: By the third year the question came at five minutes.

sn.s: Al cuarto llegaba cuando yo decía una palabra rara.
sn.e: By the fourth it came when I said a strange word.

sn.s: Este año hay conversaciones enteras sin que llegue.
sn.e: This year there are whole conversations without it coming.

sn.s: Y hoy fue una parada y un bus y un señor cualquiera.
sn.e: And today it was a bus stop and a bus and an ordinary man.

sn.s: Yo no le hice nada especial a mi manera de hablar.
sn.e: I did not do anything special to my way of talking.

sn.s: No estaba cuidándome ni poniendo atención.
sn.e: I was not being careful or paying attention.

sn.s: Estaba hablando del agua, enojado, como cualquiera.
sn.e: I was talking about the water, annoyed, like anybody.

sn.s: Y ahí es cuando el acento se me va del todo.
sn.e: And that is when the accent leaves me altogether.

sn.s: Cuando estoy enojado o cuando estoy cansado.
sn.e: When I am angry or when I am tired.

sn.s: Cuando estoy pensando en lo que digo, ahí vuelve.
sn.e: When I am thinking about what I say, that is when it comes back.

sn.s: Lucía me lo había dicho hace como dos años.
sn.e: Lucía had told me that about two years ago.

sn.s: Me dijo que yo hablo mejor cuando no me oigo.
sn.e: She told me I speak better when I am not listening to myself.

sn.s: Se lo cuento en la noche y ella no se sorprende.
sn.e: I tell her that night and she is not surprised.

sn.s: Me dice que a ella le pasó hace tiempo con la gente.
sn.e: She tells me it happened to her a while ago with people.

sn.s: Que ella dejó de oírme el acento como al tercer año.
sn.e: That she stopped hearing my accent around the third year.

sn.s: Y que cuando alguien se lo menciona a ella le extraña.
sn.e: And that when somebody mentions it to her it surprises her.

sn.s: Que tiene que acordarse a propósito de que yo soy de afuera.
sn.e: That she has to remember on purpose that I am from outside.

sn.s: Después me cuenta una cosa que no me había contado.
sn.e: Then she tells me something she had not told me.

sn.s: Me dice que hace meses una vecina le preguntó por mí.
sn.e: She tells me that months ago a neighbour asked her about me.

sn.s: Le preguntó de qué parte del país era mi familia.
sn.e: She asked her what part of the country my family was from.

sn.s: No de qué país, de qué parte de este país.
sn.e: Not what country, what part of this country.

sn.s: Y Lucía le contestó la verdad y la vecina se sorprendió.
sn.e: And Lucía answered her the truth and the neighbour was surprised.

sn.s: La vecina llevaba dos años saludándome en la calle.
sn.e: The neighbour had spent two years greeting me in the street.

sn.s: Yo le pregunto a Lucía por qué no me lo contó antes.
sn.e: I ask Lucía why she did not tell me before.

sn.s: Ella me dice que porque yo me habría puesto a pensar.
sn.e: She tells me because I would have started thinking about it.

sn.s: Y que pensando se me nota más el acento.
sn.e: And that when I am thinking the accent shows more.

sn.s: Eso es exactamente lo mismo que hizo con lo del cansancio.
sn.e: That is exactly the same thing she did with the tiredness.

sn.s: Me lo guardó seis meses para no arruinarlo.
sn.e: She kept it from me for six months so as not to ruin it.

sn.s: Al día siguiente me pasa lo que ella dijo.
sn.e: The next day what she said happens to me.

sn.s: Ando todo el día oyéndome hablar en el taller.
sn.e: I go around all day listening to myself talk in the workshop.

sn.s: Y me sale peor que en toda la semana pasada.
sn.e: And it comes out worse than in the whole of last week.

sn.s: Wilmer me pregunta si estoy resfriado, por la voz.
sn.e: Wilmer asks me if I have a cold, because of my voice.

sn.s: Yo le digo que no y me callo el resto de la mañana.
sn.e: I tell him no and I keep quiet the rest of the morning.

sn.s: Al mediodía ya se me olvidó y hablo normal otra vez.
sn.e: By midday I have forgotten and I talk normally again.

sn.s: El que se está oyendo no está hablando, está armando.
sn.e: The one listening to himself is not talking, he is building.

sn.s: Yo pasé tres años armando cada frase antes de decirla.
sn.e: I spent three years building every sentence before saying it.

sn.s: Ahora las armo solo cuando alguien me hace acordarme.
sn.e: Now I only build them when somebody makes me remember.

sn.s: El viernes vuelvo a la misma parada del centro.
sn.e: On Friday I go back to the same stop in the centre.

sn.s: No a propósito, es la parada que me queda.
sn.e: Not on purpose, it is the stop that suits me.

sn.s: Y no está el señor, y no pasa nada especial.
sn.e: And the man is not there, and nothing special happens.

sn.s: Una muchacha me pregunta si ya pasó la ruta.
sn.e: A girl asks me if the route has gone by.

sn.s: Le digo que no, que todavía no ha pasado.
sn.e: I tell her no, that it has not gone by yet.

sn.s: Ella me dice gracias y se queda esperando al lado mío.
sn.e: She says thank you and stays waiting beside me.

sn.s: Y eso es todo lo que pasa esa tarde.
sn.e: And that is everything that happens that afternoon.

sn.s: Un sábado de agosto hay almuerzo en la casa de doña Elena.
sn.e: One Saturday in August there is lunch at doña Elena's house.

sn.s: No es por nada, no es cumpleaños ni es fiesta.
sn.e: It is not for anything, it is not a birthday or a party.

sn.s: Es un sábado y son las once y hay gente.
sn.e: It is a Saturday and it is eleven and there are people.

sn.s: Estamos como veinte entre el patio y la cocina.
sn.e: There are about twenty of us between the yard and the kitchen.

sn.s: Está Marcos con la mujer y con los cuatro hijos.
sn.e: Marcos is there with his wife and his four children.

sn.s: Está Chino y está Julio y está doña Carmen.
sn.e: Chino is there and Julio is there and doña Carmen is there.

sn.s: Está don Beto, que ya camina despacio con bastón.
sn.e: Don Beto is there, who walks slowly now with a stick.

sn.s: Está mi hijo, que tiene cuatro años y corre.
sn.e: My son is there, who is four years old and runs.

sn.s: Yo llegué a las once y media, que es la hora buena.
sn.e: I arrived at half past eleven, which is the right time.

sn.s: No a las once, que era la hora que dijeron.
sn.e: Not at eleven, which was the time they said.

sn.s: Estoy en la cocina picando cebolla con doña Elena.
sn.e: I am in the kitchen chopping onion with doña Elena.

sn.s: Ella está haciendo el arroz y yo hago lo que me manda.
sn.e: She is making the rice and I do what she tells me.

sn.s: No mide nada y yo ya no le pregunto cantidades.
sn.e: She measures nothing and I no longer ask her amounts.

sn.s: Le pongo sal a la olla con tres dedos, como ella.
sn.e: I put salt in the pot with three fingers, like her.

sn.s: Ella la prueba y me dice que le falta un poquito.
sn.e: She tastes it and tells me it needs a little bit more.

sn.s: Le pongo un poquito más y no me dice nada.
sn.e: I put a little more in and she says nothing.

sn.s: No decirme nada es lo que ella dice cuando está bien.
sn.e: Saying nothing to me is what she says when it is right.

sn.s: Afuera Chino está discutiendo de béisbol con Julio.
sn.e: Outside Chino is arguing about baseball with Julio.

sn.s: La misma discusión de siempre, que nunca se acaba.
sn.e: The same argument as always, which never ends.

sn.s: Yo salgo con la olla y me meto en la discusión.
sn.e: I go out with the pot and get into the argument.

sn.s: Interrumpo a Chino enganchando lo que estaba diciendo.
sn.e: I interrupt Chino by hooking onto what he was saying.

sn.s: Y digo una cosa de un partido de hace cuatro años.
sn.e: And I say something about a game four years ago.

sn.s: Un partido que vi yo, en el estadio, con Marcos.
sn.e: A game I watched myself, at the stadium, with Marcos.

sn.s: La mesa se ríe y Julio dice que eso no cuenta.
sn.e: The table laughs and Julio says that does not count.

sn.s: Yo le digo un refrán y Julio se queda sin respuesta.
sn.e: I say a saying to him and Julio is left with no answer.

sn.s: Es el del camarón, que sigue funcionando siempre.
sn.e: It is the shrimp one, which always still works.

sn.s: Comemos como a la una y media, en el patio.
sn.e: We eat at about half past one, in the yard.

sn.s: Yo me siento entre don Beto y mi hijo.
sn.e: I sit between don Beto and my son.

sn.s: Don Beto me cuenta otro pedazo de la historia del hermano.
sn.e: Don Beto tells me another piece of his brother's story.

sn.s: Un pedazo más, y esta vez llega casi al final.
sn.e: One more piece, and this time it gets almost to the end.

sn.s: No llega del todo, pero llega más que las otras veces.
sn.e: It does not get all the way, but further than the other times.

sn.s: Yo no le pregunto nada de lo que falta.
sn.e: I do not ask him anything about what is missing.

sn.s: Después de comer se sientan a hablar y yo también.
sn.e: After eating they sit down to talk and so do I.

sn.s: Nadie me explica nada en toda la tarde.
sn.e: Nobody explains anything to me all afternoon.

sn.s: Esa es la cosa que noto como a las cuatro.
sn.e: That is the thing I notice at about four.

sn.s: Nadie me tradujo un chiste, nadie me repitió una frase.
sn.e: Nobody translated a joke for me, nobody repeated a sentence.

sn.s: Nadie me dijo qué quería decir una palabra.
sn.e: Nobody told me what a word meant.

sn.s: Nadie bajó la velocidad para que yo entendiera.
sn.e: Nobody slowed down so that I could understand.

sn.s: Y yo tampoco lo noté hasta las cuatro de la tarde.
sn.e: And I did not notice it either until four in the afternoon.

sn.s: Como a esa hora llega una prima de Chino de visita.
sn.e: At about that time a cousin of Chino's comes visiting.

sn.s: Una muchacha de Estelí que no conoce a nadie aquí.
sn.e: A girl from Estelí who knows nobody here.

sn.s: Se sienta al lado de Lucía y hablan un rato.
sn.e: She sits beside Lucía and they talk for a while.

sn.s: Después Chino le va presentando a todo el mundo.
sn.e: Then Chino goes around introducing her to everybody.

sn.s: Este es Julio, mi hermano, y esta es doña Carmen.
sn.e: This is Julio, my brother, and this is doña Carmen.

sn.s: Este es Marcos, el compadre, y esta es su mujer.
sn.e: This is Marcos, the compadre, and this is his wife.

sn.s: Y llega a mí y no dice nada de dónde vengo.
sn.e: And he gets to me and says nothing about where I come from.

sn.s: Dice mi cuñado, y dice mi nombre, y sigue.
sn.e: He says my brother-in-law, and says my name, and moves on.

sn.s: La muchacha me da la mano y me dice mucho gusto.
sn.e: The girl shakes my hand and says pleased to meet you.

sn.s: Y sigue con el siguiente y ahí se acabó.
sn.e: And goes on to the next and that was that.

sn.s: Nadie explicó nada porque no había nada que explicar.
sn.e: Nobody explained anything because there was nothing to explain.

sn.s: Como a las seis empieza a bajar el calor.
sn.e: At about six the heat starts to drop.

sn.s: Doña Elena saca café y pan para los que quedamos.
sn.e: Doña Elena brings out coffee and bread for those of us left.

sn.s: Quedamos como ocho, que son los de siempre.
sn.e: About eight of us are left, who are the usual ones.

sn.s: Mi hijo se durmió en una silla con la boca abierta.
sn.e: My son fell asleep in a chair with his mouth open.

sn.s: Marcos dice algo de que ya son varios años.
sn.e: Marcos says something about it being several years now.

sn.s: Lo dice sin ninguna importancia, tomando café.
sn.e: He says it with no importance at all, drinking coffee.

sn.s: Doña Elena saca la cuenta en voz alta desde la puerta.
sn.e: Doña Elena does the sum out loud from the doorway.

sn.s: Dice que yo llegué el año que se casó su sobrina.
sn.e: She says I arrived the year her niece got married.

sn.s: Y que eso fue hace seis años en septiembre.
sn.e: And that that was six years ago in September.

sn.s: Seis años, dice ella, y se queda ahí en la puerta.
sn.e: Six years, she says, and stays there in the doorway.

sn.s: Después dice una cosa a nadie en particular.
sn.e: Then she says something to nobody in particular.

sn.s: Dice que este ya es de aquí, que ya no se va.
sn.e: She says this one is from here now, that he is not leaving.

sn.s: No me lo dice a mí, se lo dice al patio.
sn.e: She does not say it to me, she says it to the yard.

sn.s: Marcos dice que sí con la cabeza y sigue tomando café.
sn.e: Marcos nods and goes on drinking his coffee.

sn.s: Y nadie más dice nada porque no hace falta.
sn.e: And nobody else says anything because there is no need.

sn.s: La conversación sigue con otra cosa enseguida.
sn.e: The conversation goes on with something else straight away.

sn.s: Yo me quedo con la taza en la mano un rato.
sn.e: I stay with the cup in my hand for a while.

sn.s: Igual que me quedé con el teléfono hace años.
sn.e: The same as I stayed with the phone years ago.

sn.s: A las siete cargo a mi hijo dormido para la casa.
sn.e: At seven I pick up my sleeping son to go home.

sn.s: Empiezo la despedida a las siete y salimos a las ocho.
sn.e: I start the goodbye at seven and we leave at eight.

sn.s: Media hora de eso pasa en el portón, como debe ser.
sn.e: Half an hour of it happens at the gate, as it should be.

sn.s: Caminamos las cuatro cuadras hasta la casa.
sn.e: We walk the four blocks to the house.

sn.s: Va oscureciendo y el vecino ya tiene la música puesta.
sn.e: It is getting dark and the neighbour already has the music on.

sn.s: Lucía me pregunta si oí lo que dijo su mamá.
sn.e: Lucía asks me if I heard what her mother said.

sn.s: Yo le digo que sí, que lo oí bien.
sn.e: I tell her yes, that I heard it clearly.

sn.s: Ella me pregunta qué sentí cuando lo oyó.
sn.e: She asks me what I felt when I heard it.

sn.s: Y yo me quedo pensando las cuatro cuadras enteras.
sn.e: And I think about it for the whole four blocks.

sn.s: Le digo que no sentí nada especial, y es la verdad.
sn.e: I tell her I did not feel anything special, and it is the truth.

sn.s: Le digo que lo raro es que no me sorprendió.
sn.e: I tell her the strange thing is that it did not surprise me.

sn.s: Que hace tres años eso me habría cambiado el año.
sn.e: That three years ago that would have changed my year.

sn.s: Y que hoy fue una cosa que alguien dijo en un patio.
sn.e: And that today it was a thing somebody said in a yard.

sn.s: Lucía me dice que eso es exactamente lo que significa.
sn.e: Lucía tells me that that is exactly what it means.

sn.s: Que uno no es de un lugar el día que se lo dicen.
sn.e: That you are not from a place the day they tell you.

sn.s: Uno es de un lugar el día que ya no le hace falta oírlo.
sn.e: You are from a place the day you no longer need to hear it.

sn.s: Abrimos el portón y adentro huele a la casa.
sn.e: We open the gate and inside it smells of home.

sn.s: Acuesto al niño y me quedo un rato en el patio.
sn.e: I put the boy to bed and stay a while in the yard.

sn.s: La bandera de papel sigue pegada en la pared del cuarto.
sn.e: The paper flag is still stuck to the bedroom wall.

sn.s: Nadie me ha preguntado nunca por qué está ahí.
sn.e: Nobody has ever asked me why it is there.

scenarios.title: Buenas
scenarios.desc: Four people between you and the pulpería, and none of them can be passed in silence
scenarios.setting: It is seven in the morning and you have to walk the length of your own street.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Buenas, joven. ¿Cómo está?
steps.en: Morning, young man. How are you?

options.es: Buenas, don Beto. Bien, gracias. ¿Y usted?
options.en: Morning, don Beto. Fine, thanks. And you?
options.feedback: His name, the don, and the question back. To a man of seventy the usted is not optional.

options.en: Morning.
options.feedback: You greeted him, which is the main thing. It is short for a neighbour who has known you a month.

options.en: Hi, how are you?
options.feedback: Vos to a man that age. He will answer you anyway and he will file it away.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¡Ideay, vecino! ¿Ya comió?
steps.en: Ideay, neighbour! Have you eaten?

options.en: Not yet, doña. I am just heading out.
options.feedback: She is not really asking about breakfast. Answering the question and saying where you are going is the whole exchange.

options.en: Yes, I have eaten.
options.feedback: Perfectly fine. It closes the conversation a little faster than she wanted.

options.en: Why?
options.feedback: Nobody is checking up on you. Have you eaten is a greeting here, not an enquiry.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¿Qué pasó? ¿Para dónde va?
steps.en: What is up? Where are you off to?

options.en: To the pulpería. And you?
options.feedback: Vos back to a chavalo of twelve is exactly right, and the question back is what turns a greeting into a conversation.

options.en: I am going to the pulpería.
options.feedback: True, and a bit flat. He asked partly so you would ask him.

options.en: To the pulpería, sir.
options.feedback: He is twelve. Señor will make him laugh at you for a week.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¡Adiós!
steps.en: Hello there!

options.en: Hello there, doña Carmen!
options.feedback: Adiós shouted across a street is a greeting, not a goodbye. It is what you say to somebody you are not going to stop for.

options.en: Morning, doña!
options.feedback: Understood everywhere and never wrong. Adiós would have matched her exactly.

options.en: Goodbye. I am leaving now.
options.feedback: You heard it as a farewell and explained yourself. She was only saying hello from her door.

scenarios.title: El gallo pinto
scenarios.desc: You are fed before anybody asks your name
scenarios.setting: You have been inside doña Carmen's house four minutes and there is already a plate on the table.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Siéntese pues. ¿Come huevo?
steps.en: Sit down then. Do you eat egg?

options.en: Thank you, doña. I eat everything.
options.feedback: Como de todo is the answer that makes you easy to feed, and being easy to feed is most of it.

options.en: Yes, thank you.
options.feedback: Correct and small. She was offering more than an egg.

options.en: I am not hungry.
options.feedback: In this house that is not about food. Nobody lets a person leave without eating, and refusing is refusing her.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Aquí tiene. Gallo pinto, cuajada y tortilla.
steps.en: Here you are. Gallo pinto, cuajada and tortilla.

options.en: That looks good. Is this the cuajada?
options.feedback: You praised the plate and asked about the one thing you did not know. Both go down well at a table like this.

options.en: Thank you, doña.
options.feedback: Polite. A word about the food itself is worth more here than the thanks.

options.en: And is there no bread?
options.feedback: Asking for something else at somebody's table reads as a complaint, whatever your tone was.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¿Le sirvo más?
steps.en: Shall I serve you some more?

options.es: Un poco más, doña. Está muy rico.
options.en: A little more, doña. It is very good.
options.feedback: A second plate is the compliment. Taking a little and saying why is better than taking a lot in silence.

options.en: No, thank you. I am full.
options.feedback: Allowed, and she will ask twice more. Saying you are full is the polite version of no.

options.en: I do not want any more.
options.feedback: Flat refusal with nothing softening it. Ya no quiero is for a child who has had enough.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¿Y de dónde es usted?
steps.en: And where are you from?

options.es: De los Estados Unidos, doña. Pero aquí estoy muy bien.
options.en: From the United States, doña. But I am very happy here.
options.feedback: She waited until you had eaten to ask who you are. Answering warmly is how you tell her the meal worked.

options.en: From the United States.
options.feedback: Correct. It is an answer rather than a conversation, and she was starting one.

options.en: From very far away.
options.feedback: It sounds like you would rather not say. She asked because she is interested, not because she is checking.

scenarios.title: Aquí nadie dice tú
scenarios.desc: A boy of twelve corrects your Spanish, kindly
scenarios.setting: You are sitting on the step with Roberto and you have just used a word you learned from a book.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ideay, ¿por qué me habla así? Aquí nadie dice tú.
steps.en: Ideay, why are you talking to me like that? Nobody here says tú.

options.en: Oh, no? And how do you say it?
options.feedback: You let a child of twelve teach you. That is how nearly all of this gets learned, and he will remember that you asked.

options.en: Sorry, that is how I learned it.
options.feedback: Honest, but it closes the door. He was offering to fix it for you.

options.en: That is how you say it in Spanish.
options.feedback: You have just told a Nicaraguan how his own language works. It is also not true here.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Se dice vos. Vos tenés, vos querés, vos sos.
steps.en: You say vos. Vos tenés, vos querés, vos sos.

options.es: Vos tenés. Vos querés. Ya, así.
options.en: Vos tenés. Vos querés. Right, like that.
options.feedback: Say it back out loud. The accent is the whole difference between comés and comes, and your ear needs it more than your eye does.

options.en: Ah, I understand now.
options.feedback: Understood is not the same as said. Repeating it once now saves you a month.

options.en: It is the same thing, no?
options.feedback: It is not. Tú marks you as foreign in every sentence you say for as long as you keep it.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Pero a mi mamá no le diga vos. A ella usted.
steps.en: But do not say vos to my mother. To her, usted.

options.es: Entonces a ella usted y a vos vos.
options.en: So usted to her and vos to you.
options.feedback: That is the rule in one sentence: vos for the people beside you, usted for the people above you.

options.en: All right, usted to her.
options.feedback: Correct as far as it goes. The half you left out is the half you will get wrong.

options.en: And to don Beto?
options.feedback: Good question, and the answer is usted. Ask it out loud like that and people will keep telling you.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Dale pues, a ver. Hablame con vos.
steps.en: Go on then, let us hear it. Talk to me with vos.

options.es: ¿Vos querés ir a la pulpería conmigo?
options.en: Do you want to come to the pulpería with me?
options.feedback: Querés, not quieres, and you used it on the person who just taught it to you. That is the fastest way it sticks.

options.en: You are my friend.
options.feedback: Right form, and he will take it. He asked for a sentence, not a declaration.

options.en: How are you?
options.feedback: The verb is fine and the tú at the end undoes it. That pronoun is the tell.

scenarios.title: ¿Y es casado usted?
scenarios.desc: In four minutes they know your age, your work and whether you are married
scenarios.setting: You sat down on the patio to wait for Roberto and three women have arrived instead.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¿Y usted vive solo en ese cuarto?
steps.en: And do you live alone in that room?

options.es: Solo, doña. Con mi maleta y nada más.
options.en: On my own, doña. With my suitcase and nothing else.
options.feedback: Answer and give her one detail more than she asked for. That is what turns a question into a conversation here.

options.en: Yes, alone.
options.feedback: Fine. In a patio full of people a second word keeps it friendly.

options.en: Why do you want to know?
options.feedback: Nothing is being asked of you. Where you live, your work and your family are the first three questions anyone gets.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¿Y es casado?
steps.en: And are you married?

options.en: No, doña. Single.
options.feedback: One word and no explanation. You will be asked this by everybody you meet for the next year.

options.en: No.
options.feedback: True. Soltero is the word she was waiting for and it costs you nothing.

options.en: That is none of your business.
options.feedback: Refusing the question is far stranger here than the question. She asked because she likes you.

steps.speaker: Vecina
steps.es: ¡Ay, soltero! ¿Y no quiere una mujer nica?
steps.en: Oh, single! And you do not want a Nicaraguan wife?

options.en: Ideay, doña, what do you say?
options.feedback: She is teasing you and you played. Being teased is being included, and answering in kind ends it well.

options.en: Later, doña.
options.feedback: A calm answer to a joke. Nothing goes wrong and nothing happens either.

options.en: No, thank you.
options.feedback: You answered a joke as if it were an offer. The patio will go quiet for a second.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¿Y en qué trabaja?
steps.en: And what do you do?

options.es: Trabajo en mi casa, doña. Casi todo el día.
options.en: I work at home, doña. Most of the day.
options.feedback: Plain and concrete. Working from the house needs saying, or the whole street will wonder why you are always in.

options.en: At home.
options.feedback: Enough. Where you work matters as much as what you do, on a street where everyone sees everyone.

options.en: I do not know how to explain it to you.
options.feedback: That answer travels. By tonight nobody on the block will be sure what you do for money.

scenarios.title: Se fue la luz
scenarios.desc: The power goes out and the pulpería is dark
scenarios.setting: It is eight at night and the whole block goes dark at once. You walk to doña Chepa's pulpería with your phone in your hand.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ideay, se fue la luz otra vez. ¿Y usted qué necesita?
steps.en: Ideay, the power has gone again. And what do you need?

options.en: Evening, doña. Do you sell candles?
options.feedback: Right on both counts - you greeted her first, and candela is the word here for a candle.

options.en: Hello. I want light.
options.feedback: She will work it out, but you have asked her for light rather than for a candle.

options.en: Where is the hotel?
options.feedback: Nothing to do with the blackout. Read the moment.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Sí tengo. ¿Cuántas querés?
steps.en: I have some. How many do you want?

options.en: Give me two, please.
options.feedback: Deme is exactly how you ask for something across a counter here.

options.en: Two.
options.feedback: Understood, but bare. One word to a neighbour sounds short.

options.en: I do not know.
options.feedback: She cannot help you decide. Pick a number.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Aquí tenés. Son veinte córdobas.
steps.en: Here you go. That is twenty córdobas.

options.en: Thank you, doña. Do you know until what time?
options.feedback: Thanks first, then the one question the whole block wants answered. That is what a counter is for.

options.en: That is fine. Thank you.
options.feedback: Polite and correct. You just missed a chance to keep her talking.

options.en: Very expensive for two candles.
options.feedback: Twenty córdobas for two is normal, and complaining to a neighbour costs you more than the money.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Dicen que como a las diez. Cuidado con la vela, mijo.
steps.en: They say about ten. Careful with the candle, son.

options.es: Va pues, doña. Que pase buena noche.
options.en: Right then, doña. Have a good night.
options.feedback: Va pues is the Nicaraguan sign-off, and you wished her the night back.

options.en: All right. Goodbye.
options.feedback: Adiós sounds like forever here. Save it for somebody leaving the country.

options.es: No hay problema, yo sé cuidarme.
options.en: No problem, I can look after myself.
options.feedback: She was looking after you. Brushing it off is not the way to take it.

scenarios.title: La pila
scenarios.desc: Water comes twice a week and you have to catch it
scenarios.setting: Roberto finds you standing in the yard with an empty bucket and no idea what to do.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Chele, el agua viene hoy. ¿Ya llenaste la pila?
steps.en: Chele, the water comes today. Have you filled the tank?

options.en: Not yet. What time does it come?
options.feedback: Admits you have not, and asks the one thing you need to know. Nothing wasted.

options.en: What is the pila?
options.feedback: Fair question on day one, but you have one in your own yard and he can see it.

options.es: Yo tengo agua en la casa.
options.en: I have water at the house.
options.feedback: That is the point - today you do, tomorrow you will not.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Como a las seis. Después se va y no vuelve hasta el jueves.
steps.en: About six. Then it goes and does not come back until Thursday.

options.es: Entonces lleno todo lo que pueda.
options.en: Then I will fill everything I can.
options.feedback: Exactly the right instinct, and said in one clean sentence.

options.en: All right, thanks.
options.feedback: You have understood but not acted. Here the answer is what you are going to do.

options.en: Thursday is far away.
options.feedback: True, and there is nothing to be done about it. Fill the tank.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Agarrá el balde. Yo te lo lleno.
steps.en: Grab the bucket. I will fill it for you.

options.en: Right then. Thanks, Roberto.
options.feedback: Dale pues accepts the offer the way a neighbour would.

options.en: No, I can do it alone.
options.feedback: You can, but turning down help from a neighbour here is turning down more than help.

options.en: How much will you charge me?
options.feedback: He is not selling you anything. That question would sting.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ya está. Con esto tenés hasta el jueves.
steps.en: Done. This will see you through to Thursday.

options.es: Ya me tocará a mí, vos.
options.en: It will be my turn next.
options.feedback: Perfect. The debt is the point, and vos is exactly right with him.

options.en: Thank you very much.
options.feedback: Correct and warm, just a shade formal for a chavalo you see every day.

options.en: I do not need anything else now.
options.feedback: It closes the door on him. He was not asking whether you needed more.

scenarios.title: ¿Dónde está el baño?
scenarios.desc: Asking for the bathroom in somebody else’s house
scenarios.setting: You are at doña Carmen's house for the first time and you need the bathroom.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Pase adelante, mijo. Siéntese.
steps.en: Come in, son. Sit down.

options.en: Thank you, doña. Excuse me.
options.feedback: Con permiso is what you say stepping into somebody's house. Faultless.

options.en: Thank you.
options.feedback: Fine, but con permiso is the piece that is missing.

options.en: I am going to come in now.
options.feedback: True but strange. Announcing it is not the same as asking leave.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¿Querés agua?
steps.en: Would you like some water?

options.es: Sí, gracias. Y disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño?
options.en: Yes, thank you. And excuse me, where is the bathroom?
options.feedback: You took the drink and put a disculpe in front of the question. Both halves right.

options.en: Where is the bathroom?
options.feedback: You will get there, but you skipped both the drink and the disculpe.

options.en: I do not want anything.
options.feedback: Refusing a drink outright is colder than you mean it. Take the water.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Detrás de la cocina. Cuidado que está oscuro.
steps.en: Behind the kitchen. Careful, it is dark.

options.en: Thank you, doña. I will be right back.
options.feedback: Ya vengo is what people say leaving the room for a minute. Very natural.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: It answers her but leaves the room without a word.

options.en: Goodbye.
options.feedback: You are going four metres, not leaving the country.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Aquí te pongo el agua en la mesa.
steps.en: I will put the water here on the table for you.

options.en: Thank you very much, doña. Truly.
options.feedback: Warm and plain, which is right with a señora you have only just met.

options.en: Thanks.
options.feedback: Perfectly fine. A little thin for the trouble she went to.

options.en: There was no need.
options.feedback: It sounds like you are refusing after the fact. Take it and thank her.

scenarios.title: La ruta equivocada
scenarios.desc: The wrong bus, and an hour you do not get back
scenarios.setting: You are standing in the door of a moving bus and the ayudante is looking at you.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: ¡Suba, suba! ¿Para dónde va?
steps.en: Get on, get on! Where are you going?

options.en: Does this route go through the centre?
options.feedback: Ask before your foot leaves the ground. He is shouting the route at every corner and he will tell you straight.

options.en: To the centre.
options.feedback: He now knows where you want to go. You still do not know whether this bus goes there.

options.en: Yes, yes.
options.feedback: You answered a question he did not ask and got on a bus nobody has checked.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: No, esta va para el otro lado. Bájese en la esquina.
steps.en: No, this one goes the other way. Get off at the corner.

options.en: Ah, ideay. And which bus do I take?
options.feedback: You took the mistake without fuss and asked the only useful question. He answers these forty times a day.

options.en: All right, I will get off.
options.feedback: You are off the wrong bus, which is progress. You are also on a corner you do not know.

options.en: But I asked.
options.feedback: Arguing with the ayudante costs you the corner he was going to point at.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: La 110. En la esquina de las frutas.
steps.en: The 110. At the fruit corner.

options.es: ¿En la esquina de las frutas? Ya. Gracias.
options.en: At the fruit corner? Right. Thanks.
options.feedback: You repeated the landmark back. Managua has no street names, so the landmark is the address.

options.en: Thanks.
options.feedback: Polite. Say the landmark out loud once and you will still have it in two minutes.

options.en: And the address?
options.feedback: That was the address. The fruit lady is more use to you here than any street name.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: Va pues. Son cinco pesos.
steps.en: Off you go then. That is five pesos.

options.en: Here you are. Thanks, mate.
options.feedback: You pay on the way out, not on the way in, and joven is what you call a man his age.

options.en: I already paid you.
options.feedback: You did not. On these buses the money changes hands when you get off.

options.en: Here.
options.feedback: It works. One word more and it would have sounded like you had done it before.

scenarios.title: Donde fue el árbol
scenarios.desc: An address that names a tree cut down in 1998
scenarios.setting: You have an address written on a piece of paper and it mentions no street at all.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: ¿Anda perdido, joven?
steps.en: Are you lost, young man?

options.es: Sí, señora. Busco esta dirección: de la iglesia, dos cuadras al lago.
options.en: Yes, madam. I am looking for this address: from the church, two blocks towards the lake.
options.feedback: You read her the address as it is written. Landmark, number of blocks, direction — that is the whole system.

options.en: Yes, I am lost.
options.feedback: She will help you anyway, but she needs the paper read out before she can.

options.en: No, thank you.
options.feedback: You are standing on a corner turning a piece of paper around. She asked because it was obvious.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: Ah, sí. Del árbol de mango, una cuadra abajo.
steps.en: Ah, yes. From the mango tree, one block down.

options.es: ¿Y dónde está el árbol de mango?
options.en: And where is the mango tree?
options.feedback: Ask, because you will not find it. Half the landmarks in Managua are things that are no longer there.

options.en: All right, thank you.
options.feedback: You have half an address. The half you are missing is the one that matters.

options.en: I do not see any tree.
options.feedback: Correct, and it sounds like you are telling her she is wrong. She is not.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: El árbol ya no está, pero ahí fue. Todos saben.
steps.en: The tree is not there any more, but that is where it was. Everybody knows.

options.es: Ya. Entonces una cuadra abajo de donde estaba el árbol.
options.en: Right. So one block down from where the tree was.
options.feedback: You said it back in the past tense, which is exactly how Nicaraguans say these. Donde fue and donde estaba are addresses.

options.en: I understand, thank you.
options.feedback: Probably. Repeating a landmark out loud is what stops you losing it at the next corner.

options.es: ¿Y cómo lo voy a saber yo?
options.en: And how am I supposed to know that?
options.feedback: Fair, and useless. Everybody in the barrio does know, and by next year you will too.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: Eso. Y al lago es para el norte, ¿oyó?
steps.en: That is it. And towards the lake is north, all right?

options.es: Al lago es al norte y arriba es al este. Gracias, señora.
options.en: Towards the lake is north and up is east. Thank you, madam.
options.feedback: Four words that replace a map: al lago, al sur, arriba, abajo. Learn them once and the whole city opens.

options.en: Yes, madam. Thank you.
options.feedback: Polite. She was giving you the compass, and it was worth repeating.

options.en: Which way is north?
options.feedback: She just told you: the lake. In Managua the lake is always north and you can see where it is.

scenarios.title: La caponera
scenarios.desc: Three wheels, no doors, and a price to agree first
scenarios.setting: You are on a corner in the rain and a caponera pulls up beside you.

steps.speaker: Conductor
steps.es: ¿Para dónde, joven?
steps.en: Where to, young man?

options.es: A la parada de buses. ¿Cuánto me cobra?
options.en: To the bus stop. How much will you charge me?
options.feedback: Destination and price in one breath. Settling the fare before you get in is the whole rule.

options.en: To the bus stop.
options.feedback: The destination is right. You have left the price for afterwards, which is where it goes wrong.

options.en: I do not know, you tell me.
options.feedback: Handing him the whole decision is how you end up paying double.

steps.speaker: Conductor
steps.es: Cien pesos.
steps.en: A hundred.

options.es: Ideay, está caro. ¿En ochenta me lleva?
options.en: Ideay, that is expensive. Will you take me for eighty?
options.feedback: Ideay takes the sting out and you named a counter-price. That is haggling as it is expected here.

options.en: All right, that is fine.
options.feedback: He expected you to try. Taking the first number marks you out.

options.en: I am not paying you that.
options.feedback: Too hard. Haggling here is a game, not an accusation.

steps.speaker: Conductor
steps.es: Noventa y nos vamos.
steps.en: Ninety and off we go.

options.en: Right then, ninety.
options.feedback: You met in the middle, which is exactly how it is supposed to end.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: Agreed, and fine. Dale pues would have closed it warmer.

options.en: No. A hundred or nothing.
options.feedback: You have just argued yourself up to his price.

steps.speaker: Conductor
steps.es: Súbase pues. Agárrese que va mojado.
steps.en: Get in then. Hold on, it is wet.

options.en: Right then. Thanks.
options.feedback: Short, local, and gets you into the caponera.

options.en: Yes, thank you.
options.feedback: Correct. Slightly stiff for a man who calls you jefe.

options.en: Drive slowly.
options.feedback: He will hear it as an instruction from somebody who does not trust him.

scenarios.title: El interlocal a Masaya
scenarios.desc: Leaving Managua for the first time
scenarios.setting: You are at the interlocal terminal and everybody seems to know something you do not.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: ¡Masaya, Masaya! ¿Va para Masaya?
steps.en: Masaya, Masaya! Are you going to Masaya?

options.en: Yes, I am. How much is the fare?
options.feedback: You are on the right bus and you asked the price. Both of those are yours to ask.

options.en: Yes.
options.feedback: Enough to get you on board, but you have not asked the price and it is your right to.

options.en: Is this the bus to León?
options.feedback: He has shouted Masaya four times. Listen before you ask.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: Treinta y cinco. Súbase adelante.
steps.en: Thirty-five. Get in at the front.

options.en: Here you go. Will you let me know when we arrive?
options.feedback: Paid, and asked the man who knows. That is exactly what an ayudante is there for.

options.en: Thank you.
options.feedback: You have paid and boarded. Asking him to tell you is what a first-timer should do.

options.en: And my change?
options.feedback: You have not handed him anything yet.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: Tranquilo, yo le digo. ¿Primera vez que va?
steps.en: Relax, I will tell you. First time going?

options.es: Sí, primera vez. Voy al mercado de artesanía.
options.en: Yes, first time. I am going to the craft market.
options.feedback: Saying it is your first time costs nothing and buys you somebody watching out for your stop.

options.en: Yes.
options.feedback: True, and it closes a conversation he opened to help you.

options.en: No, I go all the time.
options.feedback: A small lie that costs you the help he was about to give.

steps.speaker: Ayudante
steps.es: Ah, entonces se baja conmigo. Yo también voy para ese lado.
steps.en: Ah, then you get off with me. I am going that way as well.

options.en: That is good. Thank you very much.
options.feedback: Warm and easy, and vos is right with somebody your own age.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: It accepts, but flatly, and he just did you a favour.

options.en: No need, I will watch out.
options.feedback: You have just turned down a guide on your first trip out of the city.

scenarios.title: El almuerzo del comedor
scenarios.desc: Midday, a counter, and no menu anywhere
scenarios.setting: It is noon, the comedor is full, and there are six pots on the counter with no names on them.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.es: Buenas. ¿Qué le sirvo?
steps.en: Afternoon. What shall I serve you?

options.en: Afternoon. What is there today?
options.feedback: There is no menu and there never will be. What is there today is the question that gets you the list.

options.en: Give me the lunch.
options.feedback: You will get a plate, and it will be whatever she decides. Some days that is the better outcome.

options.en: Do you have a menu?
options.feedback: The pots are the menu. Asking for paper marks you out before you have ordered.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.es: Hay pollo, res y pescado. Con arroz y frijoles.
steps.en: There is chicken, beef and fish. With rice and beans.

options.es: Pollo, por favor. ¿Y me da ensalada?
options.en: Chicken, please. And could you give me salad?
options.feedback: Pick one and add the thing you want. The salad is usually cabbage with vinegar and it comes for nothing.

options.en: Chicken.
options.feedback: Clear enough. She is holding the spoon over four other pots waiting for you to say more.

options.en: How is the fish?
options.feedback: There are nine people behind you. At midday the question is what, not how.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.es: ¿Le pongo tajadas o plátano maduro?
steps.en: Shall I put plantain crisps or sweet plantain on it?

options.es: Maduro, por favor. Y un fresco de calala.
options.en: Sweet plantain, please. And a passion fruit drink.
options.feedback: You answered and ordered the drink in the same breath, which is what she was going to ask next anyway.

options.en: Crisps.
options.feedback: Correct. The drink is coming whether you order it or not, so you may as well choose it.

options.en: Both.
options.feedback: She will do it and charge you for it. It is not wrong, only more lunch than one person needs.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.es: Son ochenta pesos. Siéntese, ya se lo llevo.
steps.en: That is eighty. Sit down, I will bring it over.

options.en: Thank you. Do I pay you now or afterwards?
options.feedback: It changes from place to place and asking costs nothing. In most comedores you pay when you leave.

options.en: Here you are.
options.feedback: Paying up front is never wrong. Her hands are full and she may wave you off until later.

options.en: Eighty? That is expensive.
options.feedback: A comedor lunch has a fixed price and nobody haggles over it. That is for the market, not for food on a plate.

scenarios.title: En la ferretería
scenarios.desc: Buying a thing whose name you do not know
scenarios.setting: You need a specific bolt and you do not have the word for it in any language.

steps.speaker: Vendedor
steps.es: Buenas. ¿En qué le sirvo?
steps.en: Afternoon. How can I help you?

options.es: Buenas. Ando buscando una cosa, pero no sé cómo se llama.
options.en: Afternoon. I am looking for something, but I do not know what it is called.
options.feedback: The honest opening. Half of what a ferretería sells is the name of the thing.

options.en: I need a screw.
options.feedback: If it really is a screw, good. If not, you have sent him to the wrong drawer.

options.en: Nothing, I am just looking.
options.feedback: You came in for something. Now you have to start again.

steps.speaker: Vendedor
steps.es: Dígame cómo es y yo se lo busco.
steps.en: Tell me what it is like and I will find it for you.

options.es: Es de metal, redondo, y va en la pila para el agua.
options.en: It is metal, round, and goes on the tank for the water.
options.feedback: Material, shape, and where it goes. That is enough for anybody behind that counter.

options.en: It is small and metal.
options.feedback: Half the shop is small and metal. Say where it goes.

options.en: It is like the other one.
options.feedback: He has not seen the other one. Describe this one.

steps.speaker: Vendedor
steps.es: Ah, ya sé cuál es. ¿De media pulgada o de una?
steps.en: Ah, I know which one. Half an inch or one inch?

options.es: No sé, la verdad. ¿Me puede enseñar los dos?
options.en: I do not know, look. Can you show me both?
options.feedback: Fíjese buys you a second and admits what you do not know. He offered - take the offer.

options.en: The bigger one.
