options.feedback: A guess. He offered to show you and you turned it down.

options.en: Yes.
options.feedback: He asked you to choose between two, not a yes or no.

steps.speaker: Vendedor
steps.es: Este es el que le sirve. Lleve dos, mejor.
steps.en: This is the one you want. Take two just in case.

options.en: You are right. Give me two then.
options.feedback: You took the advice of the man who knows, which is the whole point of the shop.

options.en: Just one is fine.
options.feedback: It might be. Around here the second one saves the second trip.

options.en: I know what I need.
options.feedback: You came in without the word for it. He was helping.

scenarios.title: Una recarga
scenarios.desc: Phone credit, bought across a counter, said out loud
scenarios.setting: Your phone has been showing no saldo since yesterday and the pulpería is the shop.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Buenas. ¿Qué le doy?
steps.en: Afternoon. What can I give you?

options.en: Afternoon, doña. Do you do Claro top-ups?
options.feedback: Every pulpería does them and none of them advertise it. Ask by the company name and she will reach for her phone.

options.en: I need credit.
options.feedback: She will understand. She still needs to know whether you are on Claro or Tigo.

options.en: Do you sell cards?
options.feedback: Nobody has sold a scratch card here in years. It goes from her phone to yours.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Sí. ¿De cuánto?
steps.en: Yes. How much for?

options.en: A hundred, doña.
options.feedback: De cien, de cincuenta, de veinte. The de is how the amount is said and it will come back at you all day.

options.en: A hundred pesos.
options.feedback: Understood. De cien is what she asked for and what everybody else says.

options.en: The biggest one.
options.feedback: There is no biggest one. You name the number and she sends exactly that.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Deme su número.
steps.en: Give me your number.

options.es: Ocho, siete, cuatro, dos... ¿se lo repito?
options.en: Eight, seven, four, two... shall I say it again?
options.feedback: Digit by digit and offer to repeat it. Numbers said in pairs are what everybody gets wrong in a second language.

options.es: Ochenta y siete, cuarenta y dos...
options.en: Eighty-seven, forty-two...
options.feedback: That is how a Nicaraguan says it and it is faster than she can type. Slower is safer while your ear is new.

options.en: I will write it down for you.
options.feedback: It works, and it skips the only useful part of this errand, which is saying the numbers out loud.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ya está. Ya le llegó, ¿verdad?
steps.en: Done. It has arrived, has it not?

options.en: It has arrived. Thank you, doña.
options.feedback: Check before you walk off and say so. She wants to hear it landed as much as you do.

options.en: I think so.
options.feedback: Look at the phone. If it has not arrived she can fix it now and cannot fix it tomorrow.

options.en: I will check later.
options.feedback: Later means coming back and arguing about a message neither of you can find.

scenarios.title: Un mandado
scenarios.desc: Being sent for tortillas, which means you are trusted
scenarios.setting: Doña Carmen is at the stove and she has not turned around to ask you.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Mijo, ¿me hace un favor? Vaya a traer tortillas.
steps.en: Love, will you do me a favour? Go and fetch some tortillas.

options.en: Of course, doña. How many?
options.feedback: Yes first, question second. A mandado is not really a request, and being asked is good news.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: You are going, which is what she needed. You will be back on the doorstep asking how many.

options.en: Right now?
options.feedback: The word for right now is going. Asking whether she means now reads as looking for a way out.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ocho. Dígale a doña Chepa que son para mí.
steps.en: Eight. Tell doña Chepa they are for me.

options.es: Ocho, y que son para usted. Va pues.
options.en: Eight, and that they are for you. Right then.
options.feedback: You repeated the order back. Saying whose they are matters: doña Chepa will pick the good ones.

options.en: Eight tortillas. I will be right back.
options.feedback: The number is right and you left out her name, which was half the instruction.

options.es: ¿Y por qué le tengo que decir eso?
options.en: And why do I have to tell her that?
options.feedback: Because names carry weight in a barrio. You do not need the reason to carry the message.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¿Ocho? ¿Y esas para quién son?
steps.en: Eight? And who are those for?

options.es: Para doña Carmen. Me mandó ella.
options.en: For doña Carmen. She sent me.
options.feedback: Me mandó ella is the sentence. It tells her whose house you are in and where you stand in it.

options.en: For the house.
options.feedback: She will guess right. Naming doña Carmen would have got you the tortillas off the top of the stack.

options.en: For me.
options.feedback: Eight tortillas for one man will be talked about on this street until Thursday.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Gracias, mijo. Coma una, que está caliente.
steps.en: Thank you, love. Eat one, it is hot.

options.en: Thank you, doña. It is properly hot.
options.feedback: The tortilla is the wage. Taking it closes the errand properly.

options.en: Thank you.
options.feedback: Fine. Eating it in front of her would have been better than thanking her for it.

options.en: No, doña, they are for you.
options.feedback: Refusing the one she held out turns a favour into a transaction, which is the opposite of what happened.

scenarios.title: Los mangos
scenarios.desc: Fruit falls on the roof for a month
scenarios.setting: A mango hits your roof at six in the morning. Don Beto is on the pavement laughing at you.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Ideay, chele, ¿te despertó el mango?
steps.en: Ideay, chele, did the mango wake you up?

options.es: Me despertó, don Beto. Pensé que era un ladrón.
options.en: It woke me up, don Beto. I thought it was a thief.
options.feedback: You took the joke and added to it. He will be telling that one for a week.

options.en: Yes, it woke me up.
options.feedback: True and clear. You let a joke go by without giving anything back.

options.en: That tree is a problem.
options.feedback: To him that tree is fruit for free. You have complained about a gift.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Ya vas a ver. Todo abril es así.
steps.en: You will see. All April is like that.

options.es: ¿Y qué hace uno con tanto mango?
options.en: And what does one do with so many mangos?
options.feedback: The useful question. April gives you more mango than anybody can eat and everyone has an answer.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: You have taken the news and dropped the conversation.

options.en: I am going to cut down the tree.
options.feedback: Say that on this street and you will be remembered for it.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Se come verde con sal. Probá.
steps.en: You eat it green with salt. Try it.

options.en: Green? I have never eaten it like that.
options.feedback: Surprise, honestly said, which invites him to teach you. That is what he was after.

options.en: All right, I will try it.
options.feedback: Willing, which is the main thing. A little flat.

options.en: Mango is eaten ripe.
options.feedback: Where you come from. Here green with salt is half the point of April.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Con sal y vinagre. Vas a ver que te gusta.
steps.en: With salt and vinegar. You will see that you like it.

options.es: Si usted lo dice, don Beto, yo le creo.
options.en: If you say so, don Beto, I believe you.
options.feedback: Warm, respectful, and it hands him the last word, which is his by age.

options.en: I will try it tomorrow.
options.feedback: Fine. He was offering now.

options.en: I do not like vinegar.
options.feedback: You have closed off the whole thing over one ingredient.

scenarios.title: Pinolillo
scenarios.desc: Drink it and you belong to them now
scenarios.setting: Don Beto has handed you a jícara of something the colour of wet earth and is watching your face.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Tómeselo. Eso es pinolillo, hecho de maíz y cacao.
steps.en: Drink it. That is pinolillo, made of maize and cacao.

options.es: ¿De maíz? A ver. Gracias, don Beto.
options.en: Made of maize? Let us see. Thank you, don Beto.
options.feedback: Curiosity and then the drink. He is not offering you a drink, he is offering you the country.

options.en: Thank you.
options.feedback: Take it and drink it. The thanks matters less than the first swallow, which he is waiting for.

options.en: And what is in that?
options.feedback: He just told you. Asking again sounds like you are looking for a reason not to.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: ¿Y entonces? Diga la verdad.
steps.en: Well? Tell the truth.

options.es: Está bueno. Un poco espeso, pero está bueno.
options.en: It is good. A bit thick, but it is good.
options.feedback: Honest and warm at once. He asked for the truth and thick is the truth, so say it and then say you like it.

options.en: It is delicious.
options.feedback: He will take it. He asked for the truth because he expected a face.

options.en: It is strange.
options.feedback: It is his childhood in a cup. Raro is not the word to reach for first.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Es que hay que batirlo bien. Si no, se va todo al fondo.
steps.en: The thing is you have to stir it well. If you do not, it all goes to the bottom.

options.es: Ah, por eso. ¿Y usted lo hace en la casa?
options.en: Ah, that is why. And do you make it at home?
options.feedback: You took the correction and asked him about his own. That is how an old man's afternoon opens up.

options.en: I see.
options.feedback: Correct. He had another twenty minutes on this subject and you did not ask for them.

options.es: En mi país no se toma esto.
options.en: In my country nobody drinks this.
options.feedback: True and beside the point. He is telling you how it is made here, not asking about there.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Por eso decimos que somos pinoleros. Del pinol, pues.
steps.en: That is why we say we are pinoleros. From pinol, you see.

options.en: So I am half a pinolero now.
options.feedback: The joke he was waiting for. Pinolero is what Nicaraguans call themselves, and claiming a bit of it is allowed once you have drunk it.

options.en: Ah, how nice.
options.feedback: Polite and a little cold for a man who has just explained where his name for himself comes from.

options.en: And what does that mean?
options.feedback: He said it in the same sentence: del pinol. Listening to the end is half of this.

scenarios.title: Me caés bien
scenarios.desc: One verb between a friendship and a declaration
scenarios.setting: You have been trying to tell Roberto you like him for a full minute and his face has changed.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¿Cómo que yo te gusto? Ideay, maje.
steps.en: What do you mean you fancy me? Ideay, maje.

options.es: No, no. Quise decir que me caés bien.
options.en: No, no. I meant that I like you.
options.feedback: Caer bien is liking a person. Gustar with a person is wanting them, and there is no soft version of that mistake.

options.en: That you are a good sort.
options.feedback: True and it changes the subject. The word you actually needed was caer.

options.en: Yes, I fancy you.
options.feedback: You have now said it twice. Whatever happens next, this is the story he tells for the rest of the year.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ah, que te caigo bien. Eso es otra cosa, maje.
steps.en: Ah, that you like me. That is a different thing entirely, maje.

options.en: A very different thing, yes.
options.feedback: Take the correction and laugh at it. Nothing fixes a mistake here faster than agreeing it was funny.

options.en: Sorry, I still get it wrong.
options.feedback: Honest. There was nothing to apologise for and he had already forgiven it.

options.en: In English it is the same.
options.feedback: It is not, and explaining your own language is a slow way out of a joke.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¿Y quién más te cae bien de aquí?
steps.en: And who else around here do you like?

options.es: Doña Chepa me cae muy bien. Habla con todo el mundo.
options.en: I like doña Chepa a lot. She talks to everybody.
options.feedback: You used it about somebody else straight away. The second time you say a word is when it becomes yours.

options.en: Everyone, honestly.
options.feedback: Safe. He was hoping for a name and something about them.

options.en: I fancy doña Chepa.
options.feedback: Doña Chepa is sixty and this street has a very fast postal service.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ya pues, vos también me caés bien.
steps.en: Right then, I like you too.

options.es: Qué bueno, porque no me pienso ir.
options.en: Good, because I am not planning on leaving.
options.feedback: He said the thing he does not say often. Answering warmly without making it heavy is exactly the right size.

options.en: Thanks, Roberto.
options.feedback: Fine, and slightly formal for a friend who has just spent ten minutes teasing you.

options.en: I already knew that.
options.feedback: You did not, and he has just said something he meant. Take it.

scenarios.title: Pase adelante
scenarios.desc: Being invited in and not being able to refuse
scenarios.setting: You knock to return a borrowed tool. Doña Carmen opens the door and the tool is suddenly beside the point.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¡Chele! Pase adelante, pase.
steps.en: Chele! Come in, come in.

options.es: Solo vine a dejarle esto, doña.
options.en: I only came to drop this off for you, doña.
options.feedback: Says why you came without refusing her. It leaves her room to insist, which she will.

options.en: Thank you, I will come in for a moment.
options.feedback: Accepting is right. The moment will not be a moment.

options.en: I cannot, I am in a hurry.
options.feedback: A flat no at the door is heard as a refusal of her, not of the time.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ay, no, entre un ratito. Ya hice café.
steps.en: Oh no, come in for a little while. I have just made coffee.

options.en: All right, a little while then. Thank you.
options.feedback: She insisted once, which is the signal. You accepted at exactly the right point.

options.en: All right, one coffee.
options.feedback: Accepted, if a little transactional. It is not really about the coffee.

options.en: I really cannot.
options.feedback: Turning down a second offer needs a reason she can carry to somebody else.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Siéntese pues. ¿Cómo va el trabajo?
steps.en: Sit down then. How is work going?

options.es: Ahí va, doña. Con calor pero ahí va.
options.en: It is going, doña. Hot, but it is going.
options.feedback: Ahí va is the answer people here actually give, and you kept the heat in it.

options.en: Well, thank you.
options.feedback: Correct. Ahí va is what people here actually answer.

options.en: Very bad, everything is bad.
options.feedback: Too much for the first minute. Save that for the gate on the way out.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Aquí siempre tiene su casa, mijo.
steps.en: You always have a home here, son.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Eso lo tomo en serio.
options.en: Thank you, doña. I take that seriously.
options.feedback: You heard that it was not a formula, and you said so.

options.en: Very kind.
options.feedback: Polite, but it answers a courtesy rather than what she actually said.

options.en: All right, I am leaving now.
options.feedback: She said something large. Leaving on top of it is the one wrong move.

scenarios.title: Ahorita
scenarios.desc: One word, four meanings, and a whole afternoon
scenarios.setting: Marcos said he would come by ahorita. That was two hours ago.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Aló? Ideay, ya voy saliendo.
steps.en: Hello? Ideay, I am on my way out now.

options.en: Right. About how long will you be?
options.feedback: You accepted and asked for a number. That is the only way ahorita ever becomes a time.

options.en: All right, I will wait here.
options.feedback: Patient and pleasant. You have also agreed to wait an unknown amount of time.

options.en: You said ahorita two hours ago.
options.feedback: True, and it lands as a complaint about something nobody here counts as broken.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Como en veinte minutos, pues.
steps.en: About twenty minutes, then.

options.es: ¿Veinte minutos tuyos o veinte de verdad?
options.en: Twenty of your minutes or twenty real ones?
options.feedback: The joke Nicaraguans make about their own word. Making it yourself is the move.

options.en: All right, I will wait for you.
options.feedback: Fine. You have missed the joke that was sitting right there.

options.en: So you will arrive at five.
options.feedback: Sharp rather than funny. It reads as a telling-off.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Jaja, vos ya aprendiste. Veinte de verdad.
steps.en: Ha, you have learned. Twenty real ones.

options.en: I am getting the hang of it.
options.feedback: Light, self-deprecating, and it accepts the compliment without making a thing of it.

options.en: Yes, I know how it is.
options.feedback: True. A shade smug where the other one was warm.

options.es: Es que ustedes nunca llegan a la hora.
options.en: The thing is you people never arrive on time.
options.feedback: Ustedes turns a joke between two friends into a verdict on a country.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ahorita nos vemos pues.
steps.en: See you in a bit, then.

options.en: In a bit, then.
options.feedback: You gave him his own word back. That is exactly how the call should end.

options.en: See you.
options.feedback: Correct and normal. It just leaves his joke unanswered.

options.en: Really in a bit, please.
options.feedback: The please turns it into a request, and now it is a small argument.

scenarios.title: Que cumplás muchos más
scenarios.desc: A birthday in the patio, and a piece of cake you did not expect
scenarios.setting: Roberto is thirteen today, the whole street has arrived uninvited, and the pastel is in the middle of the table.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¡Ideay, viniste! ¿Y eso qué traés ahí?
steps.en: Ideay, you came! And what have you got there?

options.es: Felicidades, Roberto. Es una gorra, a ver si te gusta.
options.en: Congratulations, Roberto. It is a cap, let us see if you like it.
options.feedback: Felicidades first and then the present. A gorra is the safest gift there is for a chavalo of thirteen, and it will not come off his head all night.

options.en: A present for you.
options.feedback: Fine. The word everybody says as they hand it over is felicidades, and you skipped it.

options.en: It is nothing.
options.feedback: You came to his birthday with something in your hand. Talking it down on the doorstep is a foreign habit.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Que cumplás muchos más, chavalo. Dígale usted también.
steps.en: May you have many more, lad. You say it to him as well.

options.en: May you have many more, Roberto.
options.feedback: That is the sentence. It is what everybody says at a birthday here, it is the vos form, and nobody will explain it to you twice.

options.en: Happy birthday.
options.feedback: Understood everywhere and it is on the cake. Don Beto handed you the local one and you used the international one.

options.en: I already told him.
options.feedback: You said felicidades, which is not the same phrase. Don Beto was teaching you something, not checking up on you.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¡Mírelo! Le empujaron la cara en el pastel. Eso se hace siempre, mijo.
steps.en: Look at him! They pushed his face into the cake. That is always done, love.

options.es: ¿Y eso se lo hacen a todos? Ideay.
options.en: And they do that to everyone? Ideay.
options.feedback: You laughed and asked instead of judging. The answer is yes, to everybody, and Roberto is laughing harder than anyone.

options.en: Oh, I was not expecting that.
options.feedback: Honest and warm. Doña Chepa was inviting you to ask about it.

options.en: Poor lad.
options.feedback: He is thirteen and delighted. Feeling sorry for him marks the custom as cruel, which is not how anybody in the patio sees it.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: El primer pedazo para la abuela. Y el segundo para usted, que viene de más lejos.
steps.en: The first piece for the grandmother. And the second for you, who has come the furthest.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Eso no me lo esperaba.
options.en: Thank you, doña. I was not expecting that.
options.feedback: The order of the pieces is the ranking of the room: the oldest, then the visitor who travelled furthest. Being second is being placed.

options.en: Thank you, doña.
options.feedback: Enough. Something was just said about where you stand in that patio and it deserved a word.

options.en: Let the children eat first.
options.feedback: It sounds generous and it undoes what she just did. She chose the order in front of everybody.

scenarios.title: Primero Dios
scenarios.desc: Every plan anybody makes has a condition attached to it
scenarios.setting: You are agreeing a time with doña Chepa and she keeps adding two words to the end.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Mañana le traigo el queso, primero Dios.
steps.en: I will bring you the cheese tomorrow, God willing.

options.es: Primero Dios, doña. Aquí la espero.
options.en: God willing, doña. I will wait for you here.
options.feedback: Say it back. It is not a religious statement so much as the way a plan is closed here, and leaving it out sounds abrupt.

options.en: All right, tomorrow.
options.feedback: Agreed and fine. You answered the plan and not the phrase.

options.en: And if God does not want to?
options.feedback: It is a joke you can make in year three, not in month five. Right now it lands as making fun of her.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Si Dios me da vida, le hago un quesillo también.
steps.en: If God grants me life, I will make you a quesillo as well.

options.es: Que Dios le dé mucha, doña.
options.en: May He grant you plenty, doña.
options.feedback: You answered inside her own words. That is worth more here than any compliment you could have invented.

options.en: Thank you, doña.
options.feedback: Warm and safe. There was an opening there and you walked past it.

options.en: You are in good health.
options.feedback: She was not asking for a medical opinion. Si Dios me da vida is a formula, not a worry.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¿Y usted va a misa el domingo?
steps.en: And are you going to mass on Sunday?

options.es: Casi no voy, doña, pero respeto mucho.
options.en: I hardly go, doña, but I have a lot of respect for it.
options.feedback: Honest and not dismissive. Nobody needs you to believe, and everybody notices if you sneer.

options.en: Sometimes.
options.feedback: Vague enough to end it. She was making conversation, not counting attendance.

options.en: I do not believe in that.
options.feedback: In a country this Catholic that is a sentence with a lot of weight in it, said to a woman who feeds you.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ay, mijo. Bueno, nos vemos mañana, si Dios quiere.
steps.en: Oh, love. Well, see you tomorrow, God willing.

options.es: Si Dios quiere, doña. Que le vaya bien.
options.en: God willing, doña. Take care.
options.feedback: Two formulas, both hers, both returned. This is what fluency actually looks like from the outside.

options.en: See you, doña.
options.feedback: Perfectly normal. You have now heard the phrase four times and not used it once.

options.es: Entonces mañana a las tres en punto.
options.en: Tomorrow at three o'clock sharp, then.
options.feedback: Nailing it to a minute is exactly what her two words exist to avoid. Nothing here is agreed that firmly, and pretending otherwise only sets you up to be annoyed.

scenarios.title: El mes de la patria
scenarios.desc: September, and the flags go up on everything
scenarios.setting: Blue and white is on every pole and every bus. Roberto is painting a paper flag at your table.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¿En tu país también hacen esto en septiembre?
steps.en: Do they do this in your country in September too?

options.es: No así. Aquí se ve en todas partes.
options.en: Not like this. Here you see it everywhere.
options.feedback: An honest comparison with no verdict attached. He can carry that anywhere.

options.en: No.
options.feedback: True, and it stops a conversation he opened to include you.

options.en: It is too much.
options.feedback: Said out loud in September that is not an opinion, it is an insult.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Es que ganamos la independencia en septiembre.
steps.en: It is because we won independence in September.

options.es: ¿Y qué hacen en la escuela ese día?
options.en: And what do you do at school that day?
options.feedback: You turned his fact into his story. That is how a conversation stays open.

options.en: Ah, how interesting.
options.feedback: Polite, and it lands like a tourist. Ask him something.

options.en: I know that, I read it.
options.feedback: You have taken the story out of his mouth.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Desfile. Todo el colegio, con tambores.
steps.en: A parade. The whole school, with drums.

options.es: ¿Vos vas a desfilar? Yo quiero ver eso.
options.en: Are you going to march? I want to see that.
options.feedback: You asked whether he is in it and said you want to see it. That is an acceptance before the invitation.

options.en: It must be nice.
options.feedback: Warm enough. You have still not said you will come.

options.en: Parades are long.
options.feedback: They are, and it is his parade. Keep that one to yourself.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Vení pues. Es a las ocho, en la calle grande.
steps.en: Come then. It is at eight, on the main street.

options.es: Ahí nos vemos. No me lo pierdo.
options.en: See you there. I will not miss it.
options.feedback: A time, a place, and a promise. That is how an invitation is answered here.

options.en: I will try to go.
options.feedback: Trying is what people say when they mean no. He will hear it that way.

options.en: Another day.
options.feedback: That is the polite no, and he will understand it perfectly.

scenarios.title: El día de la madre
scenarios.desc: May 30, and it is not negotiable
scenarios.setting: It is the twenty-ninth. Marcos finds out you have made no plan at all.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Y vos qué vas a hacer mañana?
steps.en: And what are you doing tomorrow?

options.en: Tomorrow? I had nothing planned.
options.feedback: Honest, and it hands him the opening to tell you. Better than pretending you knew.

options.en: Nothing, I am going to rest.
options.feedback: Honest. Tomorrow is the thirtieth and resting is not one of the options.

options.en: Work, like always.
options.feedback: Nobody is at work on the thirtieth. Ask him why he is asking.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Es treinta de mayo, hombre. Día de la madre.
steps.en: It is the thirtieth of May, man. Mother's day.

options.es: Puchica, se me pasó. ¿Qué se hace?
options.en: Damn, it slipped past me. What does one do?
options.feedback: Puchica is the right size of oh-no, and the useful question comes straight after it.

options.en: Ah, right.
options.feedback: You have caught up. Now ask what is expected of you.

options.en: My mother is not here.
options.feedback: True, and beside the point. There are three mothers in this street who count you as theirs.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Se le lleva algo a la mamá. Aunque sea una flor.
steps.en: You take something to her mother. Even just a flower.

options.es: ¿Y a doña Carmen también? Ella me ha cuidado mucho.
options.en: And to doña Carmen as well? She has looked after me a lot.
options.feedback: You thought past the obligation to the person. That is the answer that gets remembered.

options.en: All right, I will take her flowers.
options.feedback: Correct and enough. You thought of one of the two.

options.en: She is not my mother.
options.feedback: Say that tomorrow and you will spend a year repairing it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ideay, ya estás pensando como de aquí.
steps.en: Ideay, you are thinking like somebody from here now.

options.en: I am learning, with help.
options.feedback: Takes the compliment, credits him, and closes it without a fuss.

options.en: Thank you.
options.feedback: Fine. It answers the words rather than what he meant by them.

options.en: It is logical, is it not?
options.feedback: It was not logical to you thirty seconds ago.

scenarios.title: La Gritería
scenarios.desc: December 7, and the shouting arrives at your door
scenarios.setting: It is six in the evening on the seventh and fifteen children are already at your gate.

steps.speaker: Niños
steps.es: ¿Quién causa tanta alegría?
steps.en: Who causes such joy?

options.en: The Conception of Mary!
options.feedback: The one answer there is, and you had it ready. Nobody here will forget that you did.

options.en: The virgin!
options.feedback: You know what it is about, but the call has a fixed answer and this is not it.

options.en: Good evening!
options.feedback: A greeting where a response goes. The whole street will hear the gap.

steps.speaker: Niños
steps.es: ¡Feliz día! ¿Y las gorras?
steps.en: Happy day! And the gorras?

options.es: Ya voy, ya voy. Traigo gofio y rosquillas.
options.en: Coming, coming. I have gofio and rosquillas.
options.feedback: The gorras are the little gifts handed out at the door, not hats. Naming what you are bringing is half the fun.

options.en: Yes, wait a moment.
options.feedback: Fine, and they will wait. Naming what you are bringing is half the fun.

options.en: I do not have anything.
options.feedback: On the seventh of December this is the one sentence you cannot say at your own door.

steps.speaker: Niños
steps.es: ¡Ideay, hay caña también!
steps.en: Ideay, there is sugar cane as well!

options.es: Uno para cada uno, no peleen.
options.en: One each, do not fight.
options.feedback: Said like somebody who has done this before, which is the impression you want.

options.en: Yes, take them.
options.feedback: It works. Twelve children and no rule is how it all ends up with four of them.

options.en: The cane is for later.
options.feedback: There is no later. The next house is waiting for them.

steps.speaker: Niños
steps.es: ¡Gracias! Ya nos vamos a la otra casa.
steps.en: Thank you! We are off to the next house.

options.en: Go carefully! And have a good night.
options.feedback: Sending them off with a word is what a neighbour does, and they are running to the next gate.

options.en: You are welcome.
options.feedback: Correct Spanish, and flat for a doorway with fifteen children in it.

options.en: There is nothing left.
options.feedback: They were saying goodbye, not asking for more.

scenarios.title: Yo invito
scenarios.desc: Reaching for your share and getting it badly wrong
scenarios.setting: There are four empty bottles on the table and you have just put your hand in your pocket.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Qué hacés? Guardá esa plata, hombre.
steps.en: What are you doing? Put that money away, man.

options.en: Ideay, at least let me chip in.
options.feedback: You are still splitting the bill. It is friendly, and it is not how a round works here.

options.es: Está bien. Entonces la otra la pago yo.
options.en: All right. Then the next one is on me.
options.feedback: That is the answer. You do not divide a bill here, you take the next one, and everybody keeps count without a word.

options.en: No, everyone pays their own.
options.feedback: Said out loud at a table of friends, that is close to an insult. It tells them tonight was a transaction.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Eso. Hoy yo invito. ¿Otra Toña?
steps.en: That is it. Today it is on me. Another Toña?

options.es: Dale pues, una más y ya.
options.en: Go on then, one more and that is it.
options.feedback: Accept and set your own limit in the same sentence. Nobody minds when you stop, only how you stop.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: The bottle is coming. Saying how many more you want is the part that saves you at midnight.

options.en: No, I do not want anything else.
options.feedback: Cutting it off flat while he is buying reads as leaving. Una más y ya does the same job warmly.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Salud pues. Por los amigos.
steps.en: Cheers then. To friends.

options.es: ¡Salud! Por los amigos y por Nicaragua.
options.en: Cheers! To friends and to Nicaragua.
options.feedback: Answer a toast with a toast and add one thing. That is the whole form and it never fails at this table.

options.en: Cheers.
options.feedback: Correct. A second clause costs nothing and it is what everybody else adds.

options.en: Thanks.
options.feedback: He raised a bottle, not a favour. Thanking a toast leaves his arm in the air.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Y vos por qué querías pagar la mitad?
steps.en: And why did you want to pay half?

options.es: Porque en mi país se hace así. Ya aprendí.
options.en: Because that is how it is done where I am from. I have learned now.
options.feedback: Name the difference, say you have got it, move on. That answer ends the subject and keeps the evening.

options.en: I do not know, habit.
options.feedback: True enough. He asked because he was curious about where you come from, not to tell you off.

options.es: Porque no me gusta deber nada.
options.en: Because I do not like owing anybody anything.
options.feedback: Here you are supposed to owe people. A favour that is never repaid is what a friendship is made of.

scenarios.title: No seás malo
scenarios.desc: The first time you are teased, and the first time you answer
scenarios.setting: Chino has been going at you all afternoon about the way you say one word.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: ¡Ideay! Repetilo otra vez, decilo.
steps.en: Ideay! Say it again, go on.

options.es: Ya, ya. Vos tampoco hablás tan bonito.
options.en: All right, all right. You do not talk so beautifully either.
options.feedback: Given back at the same size, and vos and hablás are exactly right with him.

options.en: I do not say it wrong.
options.feedback: A defence. Defending is what makes the teasing last another hour.

options.en: That is enough, seriously.
options.feedback: En serio changes the tone, and the table will change with it. Only use that when you mean it.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Jaja, ¡miren al chele contestando!
steps.en: Ha, look at the chele answering back!

options.en: I learned it from you, did I not?
options.feedback: You handed the joke back with his own name on it. That is the whole game.

options.en: I am learning.
options.feedback: True and pleasant. It does not land, but nothing is lost.

options.en: Do not call me chele.
options.feedback: Chele is not an insult here, and objecting to it makes it your nickname forever.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Este ya no se deja. ¿Quién te enseñó?
steps.en: This one does not take it any more. Who taught you?

options.es: Tu hermana, que es peor que vos.
options.en: Your sister, who is worse than you are.
options.feedback: Sharp, funny, and inside the line - family is fair game, mothers are not.

options.en: Nobody, it just came out.
options.feedback: A fine answer that leaves the ball on the ground.

options.en: Your mother.
options.feedback: The one place nobody goes. That stops being a joke instantly.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: ¡Uuuh! Ese estuvo bueno.
steps.en: Ooh! That was a good one.

options.en: Right then, now you.
options.feedback: You kept the round going instead of standing on your win. That is how you get invited back.

options.en: Thanks.
options.feedback: It accepts the compliment and quietly ends the game.

options.en: I won.
options.feedback: Nobody wins these. Saying it out loud is how you get taken apart next Sunday.

scenarios.title: Extraño mi casa
scenarios.desc: Admitting it out loud, and getting an answer you did not expect
scenarios.setting: It is the second evening in a row you have not gone out, and doña Carmen has noticed.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¿Y usted por qué anda tan callado, mijo?
steps.en: And why are you so quiet, love?

options.es: Es que extraño mi casa, doña. Nada más.
options.en: It is that I miss home, doña. That is all.
options.feedback: Say it plainly. Extrañar is the word, and this is a house where somebody is always missing somebody.

options.en: I am tired.
options.feedback: She will let it go and she will not believe it. There is no cost here to saying the true thing.

options.en: It is nothing.
options.feedback: She asked because she could see it was something. Nothing closes a door that was opened for you.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ay, mijo. Mi hijo mayor tiene ocho años de estar en Costa Rica.
steps.en: Oh, love. My eldest son has been in Costa Rica for eight years.

options.es: No sabía, doña. ¿Y lo ha podido ver?
options.en: I did not know, doña. And have you been able to see him?
options.feedback: She did not say that to compare. She said it because almost every house on this street is missing somebody, and now you know which one hers is.

options.en: That is hard, doña.
options.feedback: Kind and short. A question would have let her keep talking, which is what she was doing.

options.en: But he can come back.
options.feedback: Eight years says he cannot, for reasons nobody in the room needs explained.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Una vez. Ya tiene dos hijos que no conozco.
steps.en: Once. He has two children now that I have never met.

options.en: How sad, doña. Truly.
options.feedback: Nothing else is required. She was not looking for advice and there is none to give.

options.en: And can you not go?
options.feedback: A fair question with an obvious answer. She will explain the money to you kindly.

options.es: Con el celular ya casi es igual.
options.en: With the phone it is nearly the same now.
options.feedback: It is not the same and she knows exactly how much it is not.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Por eso, mijo. Aquí usted tiene casa. Coma con nosotros.
steps.en: That is why, love. You have a home here. Eat with us.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Se lo digo de verdad.
options.en: Thank you, doña. I mean that.
options.feedback: She has just told you that missing your family is the ordinary condition of the whole street, and that you belong to hers now. Take it as it was given.

options.en: Thank you, doña.
options.feedback: Enough, and small for what was just said to you.

options.en: I do not want to be a bother.
options.feedback: She offered you a place at her table and you argued with it. That is not modesty here, it is a refusal.

scenarios.title: El alquiler
scenarios.desc: A house, a price, and a handshake instead of a contract
scenarios.setting: You are standing in the patio of a small house three blocks away, and don Beto has come with you.

steps.speaker: Dueño
steps.es: Cuatro mil al mes, sin el agua.
steps.en: Four thousand a month, not counting the water.

options.es: ¿Y la luz? ¿Esa también la pago yo?
options.en: And the electricity? Do I pay that too?
options.feedback: Ask about every service one by one before you agree a number. What is and is not included decides what four thousand actually costs you.

options.en: Four thousand is fine.
options.feedback: You have agreed to a number you do not yet understand. Don Beto is looking at the roof and saying nothing.

options.en: That is a lot for this house.
options.feedback: That is don Beto's line to say, not yours. He came precisely so that the foreigner would not have to.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Está caro para este barrio, don. Tres mil quinientos.
steps.en: That is dear for this neighbourhood, don. Three thousand five hundred.

options.es: Yo confío en lo que diga don Beto.
options.en: I trust whatever don Beto says.
options.feedback: Let him do it. He knows the barrio prices, the landlord knows he knows, and neither of them wants you in the middle of it.

options.es: Tres mil quinientos me parece justo.
options.en: Three thousand five hundred seems fair to me.
options.feedback: You backed him up, which is harmless. The strongest thing you can do here is stay quiet.

options.es: Yo puedo pagar los cuatro mil.
options.en: I can pay the four thousand.
options.feedback: You have just undone the man who came here for you, in front of him. That will be remembered longer than the money.

steps.speaker: Dueño
steps.es: Tres mil ochocientos y hay trato. Un mes de depósito.
steps.en: Three thousand eight hundred and we have a deal. One month deposit.

options.es: ¿El depósito me lo devuelve al final?
options.en: Do I get the deposit back at the end?
options.feedback: Ask it now, out loud, with a witness standing next to you. That is what a witness is for when there is no paper.

options.en: Right then, three thousand eight hundred.
options.feedback: Agreed. The deposit is a month of your money and you did not ask a single question about it.

options.en: And the contract?
options.feedback: You can ask, and often there is none. Around here the handshake and the neighbour standing beside you do that job.

steps.speaker: Dueño
steps.es: Se lo devuelvo si deja la casa como está. ¿Estamos?
steps.en: You get it back if you leave the house as it is. Are we agreed?

options.en: We are. Thank you, don.
options.feedback: Estamos closes it, and you shake his hand on it. That handshake is the contract and everyone in the patio treats it as one.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: Agreed, and flat. Estamos is the word that answers the question he actually asked.

options.en: We will think about it and I will let you know.
options.feedback: Don Beto has just spent his own standing getting you a price. Walking away now spends it for nothing.

scenarios.title: El recibo está malo
scenarios.desc: A bill that is wrong, and the man who cannot fix it
scenarios.setting: The water bill says four times what you used. You are at the window with the paper in your hand.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.es: Buenos días. ¿En qué le ayudo?
steps.en: Good morning. How can I help you?

options.es: Buenos días. Fíjese que este recibo me llegó muy alto.
options.en: Good morning. The thing is, this bill came to me very high.
options.feedback: Fíjese warns him a problem is coming without making him the problem. That is how a counter complaint opens here.

options.en: This bill is wrong.
options.feedback: Clear, and it puts the fault on the paper straight away. He will get defensive before you finish.

options.en: You people overcharged me.
options.feedback: Ustedes makes him the company. Now he is defending it instead of helping you.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.es: A ver. ¿Cuánto pagó el mes pasado?
steps.en: Let us see. How much did you pay last month?

options.es: Trescientos. Aquí traigo el recibo anterior.
options.en: Three hundred. I have the previous bill here.
options.feedback: A number and the proof. That is the whole argument won in one sentence.

options.en: About three hundred, I think.
options.feedback: Close enough to be believed, weak enough to be argued with. Bring the paper next time.

options.en: I do not remember.
options.feedback: Now there is nothing to compare it with and no case to make.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.es: Ah, sí. Aquí hay un error. Pero yo no lo puedo cambiar.
steps.en: Ah, yes. There is a mistake here. But I cannot change it.

options.es: Entiendo. ¿Y con quién tengo que hablar?
options.en: I understand. And who do I have to talk to?
options.feedback: You took the no and asked for the next door. He will open it for you now.

options.en: And so what do I do?
options.feedback: Fair, and it hands him a problem instead of a question he can answer.

options.es: Entonces para qué está usted ahí.
options.en: Then what are you sitting there for.
options.feedback: One sentence and you have lost the only person in the building who was on your side.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.es: Tiene que ir a la oficina central. Lleve los dos recibos.
steps.en: You have to go to the head office. Take both bills.

options.es: Va pues. Muchas gracias por la ayuda.
options.en: Right then. Thank you very much for the help.
options.feedback: He did help, and thanking him is what makes the next window easier.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: It accepts. He went and found the error for you and got nothing for it.

options.en: Another trip.
options.feedback: True, and he heard it. That trip was going to happen either way.

scenarios.title: Otra vez mañana
scenarios.desc: Being told to come back, and coming back
scenarios.setting: Third day at the same office. The same woman, the same folder, a new missing paper.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Le falta la copia de la cédula.
steps.en: You are missing the copy of your ID card.

options.es: Ideay, si eso me lo pidieron ayer y aquí lo traje.
options.en: Ideay, but they asked me for that yesterday and I brought it.
options.feedback: Ideay carries the frustration without an accusation in it. She can look again without losing face.

options.en: I handed that in yesterday.
options.feedback: True, and flat. It sounds like her word against yours, which is a fight you cannot win at a window.

options.es: Esta es la tercera vez que vengo.
options.en: This is the third time I have come.
options.feedback: She knows. Counting the trips out loud makes you the problem in the room.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Déjeme ver otra vez. ¿Cómo se llama usted?
steps.en: Let me look again. What is your name?

options.es: Con mucho gusto. Se lo repito despacio.
options.en: Gladly. I will say it again slowly.
options.feedback: Foreign surnames get written wrong at every window in this country. Offering to repeat it slowly saves the fourth trip.

options.en: My name is what it says there.
options.feedback: Unhelpful. If it is spelled wrong there, that is exactly the problem.

options.es: Ya se lo dije dos veces.
options.en: I have already told you twice.
options.feedback: You have, and saying so buys you nothing but a slower search.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Ah, aquí está. Estaba en otro expediente.
steps.en: Ah, here it is. It was in another file.

options.en: That is good. Thank you for looking.
options.feedback: She found her own office's mistake. Thanking her is cheap and it will be remembered.

options.en: Just as well.
options.feedback: Honest relief. It also lands a little like an accusation.

options.en: I thought as much.
options.feedback: Smug, and she is the person who has to stamp it.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Se lo entrego el viernes. Aquí a las nueve.
steps.en: I will hand it to you on Friday. Here at nine.

options.es: El viernes a las nueve. Aquí estaré.
options.en: Friday at nine. I will be here.
options.feedback: Repeating the day and the time back is how an appointment becomes real. It also puts it on the record.

options.en: All right, thank you.
options.feedback: Accepted. Without repeating it back, Friday can quietly become the following week.

options.en: And what if it is not ready?
options.feedback: You have just told her you expect her to fail. She will remember it on Friday.

scenarios.title: Acordamos ochenta
scenarios.desc: The price doubles at the end of the journey
scenarios.setting: You are standing at the open door of the taxi and the number he has just said is not the number you agreed.

steps.speaker: Taxista
steps.es: Son ciento veinte, jefe.
steps.en: That is a hundred and twenty, boss.

options.en: We agreed eighty.
options.feedback: Four words, no heat, no explanation. This is the sentence and you are going to say it again in a moment.

options.es: Pero usted me dijo ochenta antes de subir.
options.en: But you told me eighty before I got in.
options.feedback: True, and longer than it needs to be. Every extra word is a door he can push on.

options.en: What do you mean a hundred and twenty?
options.feedback: You asked him a question, so now he gets to answer it. Do not hand him the floor.

steps.speaker: Taxista
steps.es: Es que había mucho tráfico, hombre.
steps.en: The thing is there was a lot of traffic, man.

options.en: We agreed eighty.
options.feedback: The same sentence, in the same tone. Repeating it is what wins this, and arguing about the traffic is what loses it.

options.es: El tráfico no era mi culpa.
options.en: The traffic was not my fault.
options.feedback: Reasonable, and you have started discussing the traffic. That is the conversation he wanted.

options.es: Todos los taxistas hacen lo mismo.
options.en: All taxi drivers do the same thing.
options.feedback: Now it is personal and he has something to defend. This was about eighty córdobas thirty seconds ago.

steps.speaker: Taxista
steps.es: Deme cien y quedamos bien.
steps.en: Give me a hundred and we are square.

options.en: Eighty, as we agreed. Here you are.
options.feedback: Hold the number and put the money in his hand at the same time. The transaction ends while he is still deciding.

options.en: All right, a hundred.
options.feedback: You paid twenty for the lesson. He will try it on the next foreigner because it half works.

options.es: No le voy a dar nada.
options.en: I am not giving you anything.
options.feedback: You owe him eighty and you agreed to it. Refusing the whole fare turns you into the one in the wrong.

steps.speaker: Taxista
steps.es: Ideay. Está bien pues.
steps.en: Ideay. Fine then.

options.es: Gracias, hombre. Que le vaya bien.
options.en: Thanks, man. Take care.
options.feedback: You won and you closed it warmly, which costs nothing. Nobody here needs the other person to feel beaten.

options.en: Thanks.
options.feedback: Fine. A second half to that sentence would have taken the edge off the whole exchange.

options.es: Así debió ser desde el principio.
options.en: That is how it should have been from the start.
options.feedback: You had already won. Saying so out loud is the only thing left that can go wrong.

scenarios.title: Me prestás
scenarios.desc: Somebody asks you for money
scenarios.setting: Chino catches you on the pavement on the fifteenth. He has never asked you for anything before.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Ideay, vos. ¿Andás con algo suelto?
steps.en: Ideay, you. Have you got any spare cash?

options.en: Depends what for, tell me.
options.feedback: Depende buys you the time to hear it, and contame says you are willing to listen.

options.en: How much do you need?
options.feedback: Straight to the number. It works, but you have skipped the part where he explains.

options.en: I have not got anything.
options.feedback: A door closed before he even said what for. He will not ask twice, about anything.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Es para la medicina de mi mamá. Te lo pago el treinta.
steps.en: It is for my mother's medicine. I will pay you back on the thirtieth.

options.es: Está bien. ¿Cuánto es lo que falta?
options.en: All right. How much is missing?
options.feedback: You accepted before asking the amount. That order matters more here than the number does.

options.en: And you will definitely pay me back?
options.feedback: Fair to ask, and it tells him you are counting. That is not how it is done between two of you.

options.en: I do not lend money.
options.feedback: A rule where a person was standing. He will hear the rule and remember the person.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Quinientos. Ya tengo el resto.
steps.en: Five hundred. I have the rest.

options.es: Aquí están. Y no andés apurado con eso.
options.en: Here they are. And do not be in a rush about it.
options.feedback: Handed over and the pressure taken off in the same breath. That is what makes it a favour and not a loan.

options.en: Here you are. The thirtieth then.
options.feedback: Fine, and it names the date. A shade more like a contract than it needs to be.

options.en: I will give you three hundred only.
options.feedback: Half a favour reads as half trust. Either do it or say you cannot.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Vos sos gente, de verdad.
steps.en: You are all right, you really are.

options.en: That is what we are here for.
options.feedback: The exact answer. It refuses the thanks and keeps the two of you level.

options.en: No problem.
options.feedback: Correct and warm enough. It answers the words rather than what he meant.

options.es: Ya sabés que me lo tenés que pagar.
options.en: You know you have to pay me back.
options.feedback: He just said something large. Answering it with the debt is the coldest thing available.

scenarios.title: Con el mecánico
scenarios.desc: Something is broken and you cannot name it
scenarios.setting: The bike has been making a noise for a week. You are standing over it with a man who is waiting for you to explain.

steps.speaker: Mecánico
steps.es: A ver, ¿qué le pasa?
steps.en: Let us see, what is wrong with it?

options.es: Hace un ruido cuando voy despacio. No sé de dónde sale.
options.en: It makes a noise when I go slowly. I do not know where it comes from.
options.feedback: What it does, when it does it, and an honest gap. That is everything he needs.

options.en: It is making a strange noise.
options.feedback: A start. Without the when, he has to guess twice.

options.en: I think it is the engine.
options.feedback: Guessing at a part you cannot name sends him to the wrong place and costs you an hour.

steps.speaker: Mecánico
steps.es: ¿Y cuándo empezó?
steps.en: And when did it start?

options.es: Como hace una semana, después de la lluvia grande.
options.en: About a week ago, after the big rain.
options.feedback: You gave him a time and an event. Half of what he knows comes from what happened just before.

options.en: A little while ago.
options.feedback: Vague. A week and a month send him looking in different places.

options.en: It has always been like that.
options.feedback: If that were true you would not be here. He will believe you and stop looking.

steps.speaker: Mecánico
steps.es: Déjemela media hora y le digo.
steps.en: Leave it with me half an hour and I will tell you.

options.es: Va pues. Aquí en la esquina lo espero.
options.en: Right then. I will wait for you on the corner here.
options.feedback: Accepted and you stayed nearby, which is what everybody does. Leaving entirely is how a half hour becomes Thursday.

options.en: All right, I will be back in a bit.
options.feedback: Fine. Ahorita from you is now the same word it is from him.

options.en: And how much is it going to cost me?
options.feedback: He has not looked at it yet. That question now says you expect to be cheated.

steps.speaker: Mecánico
steps.es: Era un tornillo suelto nada más. No le cobro.
steps.en: It was just a loose screw. I am not charging you.

options.es: Ideay, deje al menos le doy para un fresco.
options.en: Ideay, at least let me get you a cold drink.
options.feedback: Refusing to be given something free, once, is the polite move. He will take it or he will not.

options.en: Thank you very much.
options.feedback: Correct and enough. Offering something back is what turns him into your mechanic.

options.en: Perfect, so nothing then.
options.feedback: You took the free work and closed the door. He will remember the next time it is a real repair.

scenarios.title: No lo perdiste
scenarios.desc: A phone gone, and a grammar that puts the blame nowhere
scenarios.setting: You got off the bus with an empty pocket and you are telling Marcos about it badly.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Qué pasó, hombre? Traés una cara.
steps.en: What happened, man? Look at your face.

options.es: Me robaron el celular en el bus.
options.en: They stole my phone on the bus.
options.feedback: Me robaron, with no subject at all. Spanish tells this whole story without ever naming who did it.

options.en: I lost my phone.
options.feedback: You did not lose it. Marcos is about to correct you, and the correction is worth more than the phone.

options.en: Somebody took my phone.
options.feedback: Understood, and constructed like English. Nobody here says it that way.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: No lo perdiste, maje. Te lo robaron. No es lo mismo.
steps.en: You did not lose it, maje. It was stolen from you. Not the same thing.

options.es: Cierto. Se me olvida esa diferencia.
options.en: True. I keep forgetting that difference.
options.feedback: And listen to what you just said: se me olvida. The language keeps doing it to you, which is exactly the point he is making.

options.en: Ah, you are right.
options.feedback: Fine. He was opening a door onto a whole piece of grammar and you closed it politely.

options.es: Es igual, ya no lo tengo.
options.en: It is the same, I do not have it any more.
options.feedback: Not to him. Here the bad things happen to you, and the words are arranged to say so.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Aquí las cosas malas le pasan a uno. Se me cayó, se me perdió, se me olvidó.
steps.en: Here the bad things happen to you. It fell on me, it got lost on me, it slipped my mind.

options.es: Entonces se me quedó la bolsa en la casa.
options.en: So my bag got left at the house on me.
options.feedback: You built one yourself out of a different verb. That is the moment a pattern stops being a rule and starts being yours.

options.en: I see how it works now.
options.feedback: Probably. Saying one of your own out loud is what makes it true.

options.en: It sounds like an excuse.
options.feedback: It is not an excuse, it is how the language is built. A dropped glass has no culprit in Spanish.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Y ahora qué vas a hacer?
steps.en: And what are you going to do now?

options.es: Nada. Se me fue y ya. ¿O vos qué harías?
options.en: Nothing. It is gone and that is that. Or what would you do?
options.feedback: Se me fue, again with no culprit, and then you asked the man who lives here. He will tell you what people actually do, which is mostly nothing.

options.en: I am going to buy another one tomorrow.
options.feedback: Practical. He was asking a slightly bigger question than that.

options.es: Voy a buscar al que me lo robó.
options.en: I am going to go looking for whoever stole it.
options.feedback: In a bus with forty people in it there is nobody to look for. Marcos will spend ten minutes talking you out of this.

scenarios.title: Arrecho
scenarios.desc: One word, two opposite meanings, and only the tone to go on
scenarios.setting: Marcos said the word twice in five minutes and meant something different each time.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ese carro está arrecho, maje.
steps.en: That car is brilliant, maje.

options.en: Arrecho good or arrecho angry?
options.feedback: Ask straight out. Everybody has to have this explained once, and the answer is that the tone decides.

options.en: Yes, it is nice.
options.feedback: You guessed right from his face. Guessing works until the day it does not.

options.es: ¿Y por qué está enojado el carro?
options.en: And why is the car angry?
options.feedback: A joke that only works if you already know the word. Right now it just looks like you have lost the thread.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: No, hombre. Ahí quiere decir que está bueno. Depende del tono.
steps.en: No, man. There it means it is great. It depends on the tone.

options.es: Siempre depende del tono en este país.
options.en: It always depends on the tone in this country.
options.feedback: You have noticed the pattern behind the word, which is the actual lesson. Half of Nicaraguan Spanish is carried by how it is said.

options.en: Ah, right.
options.feedback: Understood. He gave you a rule that covers dozens of other words and you took it as one fact.

options.en: That is very hard.
options.feedback: It is, and saying so ends the explanation early. He was about to give you the other half.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Pero si yo te digo estoy arrecho con vos, ahí sí cuidado.
steps.en: But if I say to you I am arrecho with you, then watch out.

options.es: Entonces con alguien es enojo. Sin nadie es bueno.
options.en: So with somebody it is anger. With nobody it is good.
options.feedback: You worked out the rule from two examples and said it back. Estar arrecho con alguien is the version nobody says lightly.

options.en: I see, with you it is worse.
options.feedback: Half of it. The half you have is the half that will get you in trouble.

options.en: I never get angry.
options.feedback: Everybody does, and saying you do not is the kind of claim that gets tested at a table like this.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ya la sabés, pues. Usala, pero con cuidado.
steps.en: You have got it now. Use it, but carefully.

options.es: Va pues. Ese carro sí está arrecho.
options.en: Right then. That car really is arrecho.
options.feedback: Straight into the good meaning, on something harmless. That is exactly how you try out a word with two edges.

options.en: I will use it.
options.feedback: Say one now, while he is here to tell you if the tone was wrong.

options.en: Better if I do not use it.
options.feedback: It is one of the most Nicaraguan words there is. Leaving it on the shelf keeps you sounding foreign.

scenarios.title: Fijate que no
scenarios.desc: Saying no without ever saying it
scenarios.setting: A workmate you barely know invites you to something you have no intention of going to.

steps.speaker: Compañero
steps.es: Vaya, ¿venís el domingo al culto con nosotros?
steps.en: So, are you coming to the service with us on Sunday?

options.es: Qué bueno que me tomás en cuenta.
options.en: How good of you to think of me.
options.feedback: Every no here starts with the thanks. It buys you the whole rest of the sentence.

options.en: No, thank you.
options.feedback: Clear, and clean, and about twice as cold as you mean it.

options.en: I do not believe in that.
options.feedback: He invited you somewhere, not to a debate. This one will get around the workshop.

steps.speaker: Compañero
steps.es: Es a las diez. Va a estar bueno.
steps.en: It is at ten. It is going to be good.

options.es: Fijate que ese domingo andamos donde la familia de ella.
options.en: The thing is, that Sunday we are at her family's.
options.feedback: Fijate plus a reason that is not about him. Nobody loses anything.

options.es: Es que ese día no puedo.
options.en: The thing is I cannot that day.
options.feedback: The right shape. A no with nothing named behind it sounds like what it is.

options.en: On Sundays I do not do anything.
options.feedback: You have just told him you are free. Now the no has to be a real one.

steps.speaker: Compañero
steps.es: Ah, va. ¿Y otro domingo?
steps.en: Ah, right. And another Sunday?

options.en: Let me know when it is, and we will see.
options.feedback: The door stays open without a promise in it. Everybody here reads that correctly.

options.en: Maybe later.
options.feedback: The polite no, and he will hear it as one. That is fine if you meant it.

options.en: Yes, next Sunday I will come.
options.feedback: A yes you do not mean costs more than a no. Next Sunday will arrive.

steps.speaker: Compañero
steps.es: Dale pues. Ahí te aviso.
steps.en: Right then. I will let you know.

options.en: Right then. Thanks, honestly.
options.feedback: Closed warmly, and the de verdad makes the thanks real rather than a formula.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: It ends it. He put himself out and got one word.

options.es: No te preocupés, no voy a ir.
options.en: Do not worry, I am not going to go.
options.feedback: You just said the no out loud after both of you had carefully avoided it.

scenarios.title: Perdón
scenarios.desc: Apologising so that it lands
scenarios.setting: You said something in front of five people that you should not have. It is the next morning.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Y vos qué andás haciendo aquí tan temprano?
steps.en: And what are you doing here so early?

options.es: Vine a hablar con vos. Sobre lo de ayer.
options.en: I came to talk to you. About yesterday.
options.feedback: Naming why you came, straight away, before the coffee. That is the shape an apology takes here.

options.en: I was passing by.
options.feedback: Nobody passes by at seven. He knows why you are here and now you both have to pretend.

options.en: Nothing, I came to say hello.
options.feedback: The one thing that makes an apology worse is arriving without it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ah. Ya.
steps.en: Ah. Right.

options.es: Me pasé. Lo siento, de verdad.
options.en: I went too far. I am sorry, honestly.
options.feedback: Short, no explanation attached. A long apology turns into an excuse and both of you know it.

options.en: Sorry if I offended you.
options.feedback: The si makes it conditional, as though it might not have happened. It did.

options.es: Es que yo no sabía nada de eso.
options.en: The thing is I did not know anything about that.
options.feedback: That is a defence, not an apology. Do the apology first, if at all.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Está bien, hombre. Ya pasó.
steps.en: It is all right, man. It is over.

options.es: Gracias. No lo vuelvo a hacer.
options.en: Thank you. I will not do it again.
options.feedback: Accepted without arguing that it was nothing. The promise is short enough to be believed.

options.en: Yes, it is over.
options.feedback: Agreed. He offered you the door and you walked out without saying anything.

options.en: So you were not angry then.
options.feedback: Making him say it again is asking him to do the hard part twice.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Querés café?
steps.en: Do you want coffee?

options.es: Dale. ¿Cómo va lo de la casa?
options.en: Right. How is the house thing going?
options.feedback: He offered coffee instead of forgiveness, which is how it is done, and you moved to something ordinary. That is the repair finished.

options.en: Yes, thank you.
options.feedback: Accepted. Leaving the silence there means one of you has to fill it with the same subject again.

options.en: So we are all right now, are we not?
options.feedback: The coffee was the answer. Asking for it in words takes it back apart.

scenarios.title: Con las manos vacías
scenarios.desc: A year of doing something wrong, and the day somebody finally says so
scenarios.setting: You are on your way out to Marcos's house and doña Carmen has stopped you at the gate.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¿Y usted va así? ¿Sin llevar nada?
steps.en: And you are going like that? Without taking anything?

options.en: How do you mean, doña? What should I take?
options.feedback: She has finally said it. Ask, because you are about to learn something you have been getting wrong since the day you arrived.

options.en: It is only Marcos, though.
options.feedback: It makes no difference whose house it is. She is not going to let you out of the gate on that.

options.es: En mi país no se lleva nada.
options.en: Where I am from you do not take anything.
options.feedback: She knows. That is exactly why she has waited a year to mention it, and defending the habit wastes the moment.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Algo, mijo. Aunque sea una gaseosa. Aunque sea pan.
steps.en: Something, love. Even a fizzy drink. Even bread.

options.es: Ya. Entonces paso por la pulpería primero.
options.en: Right. Then I will stop at the pulpería first.
options.feedback: Fix it immediately and out loud. A bag of bread from the pulpería on the corner does the whole job.

options.en: Next time I will take something.
options.feedback: Next time is not today, and today you are already at the gate with your hands empty.

options.es: Marcos no va a decir nada.
options.en: Marcos will not say anything.
options.feedback: Nobody ever says anything. That is precisely how you have managed to do it for a year.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Eso.
steps.en: That is it.

options.es: ¿Y por qué no me lo había dicho antes, doña?
options.en: And why had you not told me before, doña?
options.feedback: Ask her. The answer is the real lesson, and it is not about bread.

options.en: Thank you, doña.
options.feedback: Warm and it ends there. There was one more thing she was ready to tell you.

options.en: You should have told me before.
options.feedback: She did you a kindness. Turning it into a complaint against her is a poor way to receive it.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Porque usted era visita. A la visita no se le corrige.
steps.en: Because you were a guest. You do not correct a guest.

options.en: So I am not a guest any more.
options.feedback: That is what she just told you. Being corrected is the promotion, and she waited a year to give it to you.

options.en: Ah, I see.
options.feedback: You have the rule. The thing she was actually saying about you went past.

options.es: Yo prefiero que me corrijan siempre.
options.en: I would rather always be corrected.
options.feedback: That is not on offer. Correction here is a sign of where you stand, not a service you can request.

scenarios.title: Una seña
scenarios.desc: Reading a signal you are not sure is one
scenarios.setting: Lucía has laughed at three things that were not funny. Marcos is watching you miss it.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Y vos siempre venís los jueves?
steps.en: And do you always come on Thursdays?

options.es: Casi siempre. ¿Por qué, vas a estar?
options.en: Almost always. Why, are you going to be here?
options.feedback: You answered and handed the question back. That is exactly the size of step this moment takes.

options.en: Yes, almost always.
options.feedback: True. It closes a door she opened, and she opened it on purpose.

options.en: I do not know, it depends on work.
options.feedback: Depende is a fine word and a terrible answer to this particular question.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Puede ser. Depende.
steps.en: Maybe. It depends.

options.es: Ah, entonces ahí nos vemos, si Dios quiere.
options.en: Ah, then see you there, God willing.
options.feedback: You gave her back her own hedge with a smile in it. Nobody has committed to anything and everybody knows what is happening.

options.en: All right, hopefully.
options.feedback: Warm and correct. It does not quite play the game she just started.

options.en: Depends on what?
options.feedback: Asking a hedge to explain itself is asking somebody to say the thing out loud. Not yet.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Y vos por qué preguntás tanto?
steps.en: And why do you ask so much?

options.es: Porque me gusta hablar con vos.
options.en: Because I like talking to you.
options.feedback: Said plainly, once, without a joke to hide behind. That is the moment and you took it.

options.en: The thing is I am curious.
options.feedback: A safe answer. She will accept it, and nothing will happen.

options.en: I do not ask that much.
options.feedback: Arguing with the observation loses the thing the observation was for.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Ideay. Qué directo el chele.
steps.en: Ideay. Very direct, the chele.

options.es: Aquí me enseñaron a dar la vuelta. Esta vez no quise.
options.en: Here they taught me to go the long way round. This time I did not want to.
options.feedback: It shows you understand how the country talks and that you chose otherwise. That is the best possible answer.

options.en: Sorry, was that too much?
options.feedback: Backing away from something that landed well. Do not apologise for it.

options.en: That is how I am.
options.feedback: A shrug where the moment wanted an answer.

scenarios.title: Te quiero
scenarios.desc: Two words for one thing, and the bigger one said first
scenarios.setting: You are on the phone with Lucía at night and she has just said something soft.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Me gusta cuando hablás así, gordo.
steps.en: I like it when you talk like that, gordo.

options.en: I love you, Lucía.
options.feedback: Te quiero is the everyday one and it is the one people actually say. It is not the small version, whatever the dictionary suggests.

options.en: Me too.
options.feedback: Safe. She left you an opening the size of a door and you stood in it.

options.en: I love you.
options.feedback: Te amo is enormous here and belongs in songs. A lot of Nicaraguans go a whole life without saying it once, and she has gone quiet.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Ideay. ¿Y por qué me decís así de repente?
steps.en: Ideay. And why are you saying that all of a sudden?

options.es: Porque de verdad lo pienso. Nada más.
options.en: Because I really do mean it. Nothing more.
options.feedback: Plain and short. Explaining it further would make it into a speech, and a speech is not what she asked for.

options.en: Sorry, did I say it too soon?
options.feedback: Honest. Apologising for it half takes it back, and she was not asking for an apology.

options.es: Así se dice en mi país.
options.en: That is how we say it where I am from.
options.feedback: You have turned a moment into a translation problem. She was not asking about your country.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Es que aquí eso casi no se dice. Mi papá nunca se lo dijo a mi mamá.
steps.en: It is just that here that is hardly ever said. My father never said it to my mother.

options.en: And how did she know, then?
options.feedback: The right question, and the answer is everything else: who cooks, who waits up, who is still there. Words are not the main channel here.

options.en: How sad.
options.feedback: She was not telling you a sad story. She was telling you how her parents' marriage worked.

options.es: Entonces yo se lo voy a decir siempre.
options.en: Then I will say it to you always.
options.feedback: Sweet, and it talks over what she just told you about her own house.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Yo también te quiero, tonto. Pero decímelo despacio.
steps.en: I love you too, silly. But say it to me slowly.

options.en: All right then. I love you, Lucía.
options.feedback: She asked for the smaller word said properly, and she gave you hers first. Do exactly what she asked.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: She just said it back to you. That deserved more than two words.

options.en: Slowly how?
options.feedback: It was not an instruction about speed. Asking her to explain it is the surest way to end the evening.

scenarios.title: Gordo
scenarios.desc: Affection that arrives sounding like an insult
scenarios.setting: Lucía has called you gordo twice this week and Roberto has explained why you must not be offended.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Qué hacés, gordo?
steps.en: What are you up to, gordo?

options.en: Here, waiting for you, negra.
options.feedback: Answer in the same currency. Gordo, negra, flaco: they all sound like insults and none of them are, and using one back says you have understood.

options.en: Nothing much. And you?
options.feedback: Perfectly normal. She used the affectionate word and you did not, which she will notice without saying so.

options.en: Do not call me gordo.
options.feedback: That is the nicest thing she has said to you all week. Refusing it tells her the door is closed.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Ay, mirá vos. ¿Y quién te enseñó eso?
steps.en: Well, look at you. And who taught you that?

options.es: Roberto, que se rió de mí media hora.
options.en: Roberto, who laughed at me for half an hour.
options.feedback: Telling her you had to be taught is funnier and warmer than pretending you knew. Nobody expects a chele to arrive knowing this.

options.en: I am learning.
options.feedback: True and a little pleased with itself. The story of how you learned it is the better answer.

options.en: Nobody, I always knew it.
options.feedback: You went silent for two hours the first time she said it. She will find that out eventually and it will be better if she hears it from you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: La primera vez no me contestaste en dos horas, gordo.
steps.en: The first time you did not answer me for two hours, gordo.

options.es: Es que en mi país eso se toma feo. Ya aprendí.
options.en: It is that where I am from that is taken badly. I have learned now.
options.feedback: Name the difference once, say you have got it, and let it go. Here affection is said backwards on purpose, and that is precisely what makes it affection.

options.en: Sorry about that.
options.feedback: Fine. She was teasing rather than complaining, and an explanation would have been better than an apology.

options.es: Es que fue un poco fuerte.
options.en: It was a bit strong, though.
options.feedback: You are still arguing that she was rude. She was not, and you have already been told so by two different people.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Vení a la casa el domingo. Mi mamá quiere conocerte bien.
steps.en: Come to the house on Sunday. My mother wants to get to know you properly.

options.en: I will be there. What shall I bring?
options.feedback: You said yes and asked the only question that matters. Arriving at doña Elena's house with your hands empty is not a mistake you get to make twice.

options.en: Right, I will be there.
options.feedback: You are going, which is the main thing. What you carry through that door is half of what she is judging.

options.en: And do I have to go?
options.feedback: It was not really an invitation. Her mother wanting to see you is the next step and there is no version where you decline it.

scenarios.title: Conocé a mi mamá
scenarios.desc: Meeting doña Elena for the first time
scenarios.setting: You are at the door with your hands empty and Lucía half a step ahead of you.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Con que vos sos el chele del que tanto hablan.
steps.en: So you are the chele they all talk about.

options.es: Mucho gusto, doña Elena. Gracias por recibirme.
options.en: Pleased to meet you, doña Elena. Thank you for having me.
options.feedback: Her name, the doña, and thanks for the invitation. All three land in one sentence.

options.en: Pleased to meet you.
options.feedback: Correct and small. This is a doorway you only walk through once.

options.en: Hello, how are you?
options.feedback: The vos-level greeting to a suegra you have never met. She will not say anything, and she will notice.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Pase. Siéntese ahí. ¿Ya comió?
steps.en: Come in. Sit there. Have you eaten?

options.es: Todavía no, doña. Huele muy bien.
options.en: Not yet, doña. It smells very good.
options.feedback: The right answer is no, whatever the truth is, and you complimented the kitchen without being asked.

options.en: Yes, I have eaten, thank you.
options.feedback: Refusing the plate at a first meeting is refusing more than the plate.

options.en: I am not hungry.
options.feedback: The one sentence that cannot be said at that table.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¿Y usted qué hace? ¿En qué trabaja?
steps.en: And what do you do? What is your work?

options.es: Trabajo en un taller, doña. Arreglando cosas.
options.en: I work in a workshop, doña. Fixing things.
options.feedback: Plain, exact, no decoration. She is not testing your job, she is testing whether you dress it up.

options.en: I work near here.
options.feedback: Vague where she asked for specific. She will ask again in a month.

options.es: Es un poco complicado de explicar.
options.en: It is a bit complicated to explain.
options.feedback: That answer means one of two things and neither of them is good.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Ajá. ¿Y sus papás saben de mi hija?
steps.en: I see. And do your parents know about my daughter?

options.es: Todavía no, doña, pero se lo voy a decir.
