options.en: Not yet, doña, but I am going to tell them.
options.feedback: Honest about where things stand and clear about the intention. That is the whole question she asked.

options.en: Yes, they know something.
options.feedback: Softening it will not help. She will ask Lucía afterwards and find out anyway.

options.en: That is my business.
options.feedback: In this house, from today, it is not.

scenarios.title: Los cuñados
scenarios.desc: Her brothers, and the test that is not called one
scenarios.setting: Julio and Chino have put a beer in your hand and pulled up a third chair.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: Sentate pues. Vos jugás béisbol, ¿o no?
steps.en: Sit down then. You play baseball, right?

options.en: Terribly, but I play.
options.feedback: Getting in first with your own weakness leaves them nothing to open with. It is the strongest move at that table.

options.en: Yes, a little.
options.feedback: Fine. It hands them the next line and they will use it.

options.en: Quite well, actually.
options.feedback: You have just written the whole afternoon for them.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Uy, ¿malísimo? Peor que Julio no creo.
steps.en: Ooh, terrible? Worse than Julio I doubt.

options.es: Eso lo vemos el domingo pues.
options.en: We will see about that on Sunday then.
options.feedback: You took the joke and turned it into a plan. Now there is a Sunday.

options.en: Maybe.
options.feedback: Safe. It lets the joke fall on the floor between the three of you.

options.en: I did not say that.
options.feedback: Correcting the record in a vacilón is how you tell everybody you cannot take one.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: ¿Y qué son tus planes con nuestra hermana?
steps.en: And what are your plans with our sister?

options.es: Serias. Se lo dije a ella y se lo digo a ustedes.
options.en: Serious ones. I told her and I am telling you.
options.feedback: One word, then the reason it is credible. They were not looking for a speech.

options.en: It is still early for that.
options.feedback: Honest, and it is the answer that keeps this conversation going another twenty minutes.

options.es: Eso es entre ella y yo.
options.en: That is between her and me.
options.feedback: In this family it is not, and you have just told two men that they do not count.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Ideay, respondió sin miedo.
steps.en: Ideay, he answered with no fear at all.

options.es: Ustedes preguntaron derecho, yo contesté derecho.
options.en: You asked straight, I answered straight.
options.feedback: It names what just happened and gives them the credit for it. That is the end of the test.

options.en: Thanks.
options.feedback: Fine, and it treats a verdict like a compliment.

options.es: No tenía por qué tener miedo.
options.en: I had no reason to be afraid.
options.feedback: True and hard. The moment was warm until you made it a competition.

scenarios.title: Estoy celoso
scenarios.desc: Jealousy, out loud, before it goes bad
scenarios.setting: Somebody put an arm around her at a party and you have not spoken for an hour.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Qué te pasa? Andás raro desde la fiesta.
steps.en: What is wrong with you? You have been odd since the party.

options.es: Sí, ando raro. Me puse celoso y no sé qué hacer con eso.
options.en: Yes, I have. I got jealous and I do not know what to do with it.
options.feedback: Named, owned, and handed to her without an accusation. That is the version of this that ends well.

options.en: It is nothing.
options.feedback: She can see that it is something. Now she has to drag it out of you, and that is its own argument.

options.es: Vos sabés muy bien qué me pasa.
options.en: You know perfectly well what is wrong with me.
options.feedback: That sentence starts a fight about whether she knows, which is not the subject.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Celoso de quién? ¿De Erick?
steps.en: Jealous of who? Of Erick?

options.es: De él y de no saber quién es.
options.en: Of him, and of not knowing who he is.
options.feedback: Honest about the real thing, which is not him. Very hard to argue with.

options.en: Yes, of him.
options.feedback: True as far as it goes. It puts a man in the middle of something that is not about him.

options.es: De todos los que te tocan.
options.en: Of everybody who touches you.
options.feedback: Todos turns one moment into an accusation about her whole life.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Erick es mi primo. Crecimos juntos.
steps.en: Erick is my cousin. We grew up together.

options.es: Ah, puchica. Ya me siento tonto.
options.en: Ah, damn. Now I feel stupid.
options.feedback: Taking the hit lightly and out loud is what stops it from becoming a week.

options.en: All right, I understand now.
options.feedback: Accepted. It is a little short for how much you just put her through.

options.es: Y por qué no me lo dijiste.
options.en: And why did you not tell me.
options.feedback: You are now blaming her for not answering a question you never asked.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Tonto no. Pero preguntame antes.
steps.en: Not stupid. But ask me first.

options.es: Te lo prometo. Prefiero preguntar que andar así.
options.en: I promise. I would rather ask than go around like this.
options.feedback: A promise, and a reason for it that is about you and not about her.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: Accepted. She said something worth answering properly.

options.es: Si no me das razones, no pregunto.
options.en: If you do not give me reasons, I will not ask.
options.feedback: That puts the condition on her. It undoes the whole conversation.

scenarios.title: La plata
scenarios.desc: An argument about money that is not about money
scenarios.setting: There is not enough this fortnight and you have both known it since Tuesday.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: No alcanza. Otra vez no alcanza.
steps.en: It is not enough. Again it is not enough.

options.es: Ya sé. Sentémonos a ver los números juntos.
options.en: I know. Let us sit down and look at the numbers together.
options.feedback: You agreed and made it a thing the two of you do. That takes the accusation out of the room before it forms.

options.en: Yes, it is a hard month.
options.feedback: True, and it agrees without doing anything. She was not reporting the weather.

options.en: I work every day.
options.feedback: A defence to something that was not a charge. That is how this becomes the other argument.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Es que se nos fue en cosas que no eran.
steps.en: The thing is it went on things that were not necessary.

options.en: Which ones? Say it straight.
options.feedback: You asked her to drop the indirect. Between the two of you that is the right moment to ask for it.

options.en: All right, we have to be more careful.
options.feedback: Agreeing with the general is how the specific never gets said.

options.es: Ah, ya sé para dónde va esto.
options.en: Ah, I know where this is going.
options.feedback: You just told her that whatever she says next will not be heard.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: La bomba del carro. Eso podía esperar.
steps.en: The pump for the car. That could have waited.

options.es: Tenés razón. Eso lo compré sin preguntarte.
options.en: You are right. I bought that without asking you.
options.feedback: Conceded the point and named the real problem, which was the asking and not the money.

options.en: It was cheap, honestly.
options.feedback: Arguing the price argues the wrong half. She said it could have waited.

options.es: Y las cosas de tu mamá qué.
options.en: And what about your mother's things.
options.feedback: Bringing the suegra into a money argument is lighting the second fire while the first one is going.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Solo quiero que hablemos antes.
steps.en: I only want us to talk about it first.

options.es: De acuerdo. Nada de cien pesos para arriba sin decirnos.
options.en: Agreed. Nothing over a hundred without telling each other.
options.feedback: You turned it into a rule that applies to both of you. That is a fix instead of an apology.

options.en: All right, I will tell you.
options.feedback: Accepted. Only one of you is bound by it, which she will notice in a month.

options.en: You do not tell me everything either.
options.feedback: Perhaps true. Said now, it is only there to stop the sentence she was finishing.

scenarios.title: Tu familia o la mía
scenarios.desc: Whose house you go to, and what it stands for
scenarios.setting: It is the twenty-third of December and both mothers are expecting you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Mi mamá ya contó con nosotros para el veinticuatro.
steps.en: My mother has already counted on us for the twenty-fourth.

options.es: Va. ¿Y qué hacemos con doña Carmen entonces?
options.en: Right. And what do we do about doña Carmen then?
options.feedback: Accepted her mother, then asked about yours in the same breath. Nobody has been chosen over anybody.

options.en: And you already told her yes?
options.feedback: The question underneath is fair. Asked like that, it is about permission rather than the plan.

options.en: It is always your mother first.
options.feedback: Siempre turns one December into every December. Now you are arguing about the last four years.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Podemos pasar por donde ella temprano.
steps.en: We can go by hers early.

options.es: Eso me parece bien. Yo le aviso hoy mismo.
options.en: That sounds good to me. I will tell her today.
options.feedback: Accepted and you took the job of telling her. That half is yours and doing it fast is what keeps it small.

options.en: All right, if there is time.
options.feedback: A yes with a way out already in it. She will hear the way out.

options.es: Temprano no le sirve a ella.
options.en: Early is no good for her.
options.feedback: Perhaps not. Now there is no plan at all and it is your turn to make one.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Vos creés que se va a poner brava?
steps.en: Do you think she will get upset?

options.es: Un poco, pero se le pasa. Prefiero decírselo yo.
options.en: A little, but she will get over it. I would rather tell her myself.
options.feedback: Honest about the cost and you take it on yourself. That is the whole answer.

options.en: I do not think so.
options.feedback: Comfortable, and probably wrong. She asked because she thinks so.

options.en: She always gets upset.
options.feedback: Said about your own mother to your wife, it will be remembered by both of them.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Gracias. Yo sé que no es fácil.
steps.en: Thank you. I know it is not easy.

options.es: Ninguno de los dos tiene familia de sobra.
options.en: Neither of us has family to spare.
options.feedback: It puts the two of you on the same side of a thing that has no clean answer. Nothing else needed saying.

options.en: It is not that hard.
options.feedback: It waves away something she just acknowledged. She was being kind.

options.en: You never have to choose.
options.feedback: That is the argument you avoided all afternoon, arriving at the end anyway.

scenarios.title: Pedir la mano
scenarios.desc: Asking her family, in a room with everybody in it
scenarios.setting: Sunday afternoon, doña Elena's front room, and the television is off for the first time in years.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Bueno. Aquí estamos. Usted dirá.
steps.en: Right. Here we are. Go ahead.

options.es: Doña Elena, vine a pedirle la mano de Lucía.
options.en: Doña Elena, I came to ask you for Lucía's hand.
options.feedback: The whole sentence, her name in front, no run-up. This is the one moment where the long way round is wrong.

options.es: Vine a hablarles de algo importante.
options.en: I came to talk to you about something important.
options.feedback: Everybody in the room knows what it is. Making them wait is making them work.

options.es: Bueno, ustedes ya saben para qué vine.
options.en: Well, you all know what I came for.
options.feedback: They do. It has to be said out loud by you, and that is the point of the afternoon.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¿Y usted con qué la va a mantener?
steps.en: And what are you going to keep her on?

options.es: Con lo que gano en el taller. No es mucho, pero es seguro.
options.en: On what I earn at the workshop. It is not much, but it is steady.
options.feedback: Honest and unpolished. Steady is the word that matters in that room, not the amount.

options.en: We will manage.
options.feedback: A phrase with nothing in it. She asked a real question and deserves a number or a name.

options.en: She works too.
options.feedback: True, and it answers a question about you with a fact about her.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: ¿Y si un día se quiere ir para su país?
steps.en: And what if one day you want to go back to your country?

options.es: Si nos vamos, nos vamos los dos, y sería decisión de ella también.
options.en: If we go, we both go, and it would be her decision too.
options.feedback: The fear is that you will take her away. You answered the fear rather than the words.

options.en: I have no plans to leave.
options.feedback: True today. It leaves the fear exactly where it was.

options.en: I cannot know that.
options.feedback: Honest, and in this room it is heard as a maybe. That is the wrong answer to that question.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Está bien. Pero aquí la boda se hace como Dios manda.
steps.en: All right. But here the wedding is done properly.

options.es: Como usted diga, doña. Yo aprendo lo que haya que aprender.
options.en: As you say, doña. I will learn whatever needs learning.
options.feedback: You gave her the yes and the authority in one sentence, which is what the sentence was asking for.

options.en: Yes, of course.
options.feedback: Agreement without the deference. It is the deference she was checking for.

options.en: We want something simple.
options.feedback: Perhaps you do. Five minutes after a yes is not when that gets said.

scenarios.title: La boda
scenarios.desc: Your own wedding, and forty people with opinions
scenarios.setting: Two weeks out. Doña Elena has the list, Lucía has the dress, and somebody has to say something about the money.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Van a ser como ciento veinte personas.
steps.en: It is going to be about a hundred and twenty people.

options.es: Ciento veinte. ¿Y quiénes son los padrinos?
options.en: A hundred and twenty. And who are the godparents?
options.feedback: You did not flinch at the number and you went straight to who is paying for what. That is the real question.

options.en: A hundred and twenty? That is a lot.
options.feedback: Honest. It also sounds like the first move in an argument about cutting the list.

options.es: Nosotros no conocemos a tanta gente.
options.en: We do not know that many people.
options.feedback: You do not. Her family does, and the wedding belongs to more people than the two of you.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Hay padrino de pastel, de música y de las sillas.
steps.en: There is a godparent of the cake, of the music and of the chairs.

options.es: Ah, entonces no lo paga una sola familia.
options.en: Ah, so one family does not pay for it all.
options.feedback: You understood the whole system in one sentence. That is the answer she was waiting to hear.

options.en: All right, that helps.
options.feedback: True, and it treats the padrinos as a discount rather than as people.

options.en: I would rather pay for it all myself.
options.feedback: It sounds generous and it is an insult. You would be shutting her family out of their own wedding.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: A usted le toca hablar con el padre.
steps.en: It falls to you to talk to the priest.

options.es: Va. ¿Qué es lo que tengo que llevar?
options.en: Right. What do I need to take?
options.feedback: Accepted the job and asked for the list. Nothing else was needed.

options.en: And why me?
options.feedback: Because it is yours. Asking why turns a task into a negotiation.

options.es: Que vaya Lucía, ella lo conoce.
options.en: Let Lucía go, she knows him.
options.feedback: She does. The point is that the priest meets the man.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Y no se me ponga nervioso el día.
steps.en: And do not go getting nervous on me on the day.

options.es: Nervioso voy a estar, doña. Pero ahí voy a estar.
options.en: I will be nervous, doña. But I will be there.
options.feedback: Admitted the first half and promised the second. That is exactly the right size of answer.

options.en: Do not worry.
options.feedback: Reassuring and empty. She was not really asking about nerves.

options.en: I never get nervous.
options.feedback: In two weeks, in front of a hundred and twenty people, that will not survive contact.

scenarios.title: La serenata
scenarios.desc: Midnight on the twenty-ninth of May, three musicians, and a woman pretending to be surprised
scenarios.setting: It is five to twelve at night, you are standing in the street outside doña Elena's door, and Julio has paid the musicians.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: A las doce en punto empiezan. Vos cantás con nosotros, cuñado.
steps.en: They start at twelve on the dot. You sing with us, brother-in-law.

options.es: Yo canto muy mal, pero canto.
options.en: I sing terribly, but I will sing.
options.feedback: So do her three sons, every year. Singing badly in the street at midnight is the entire point of a serenata.

options.es: Yo no me sé la canción.
options.en: I do not know the song.
options.feedback: Nor does half the street. Stand with them and move your mouth.

options.en: Better if I just listen.
options.feedback: You are her daughter's husband standing in the street at midnight. There is no version of tonight where you watch.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¡Ay, Dios mío! ¿Y esto qué es? ¡A esta hora!
steps.en: Oh my goodness! And what is this? At this hour!

options.en: Happy Mother's Day, doña Elena!
options.feedback: She knew. She has known since March, she is standing at the door in her dressing gown, and everybody pretends every year. Play it straight.

options.en: It is your serenade, doña.
options.feedback: Obviously. Explaining it takes the air out of the surprise she is performing.

options.en: You already knew, doña.
options.feedback: Of course she knew. Saying so is the one thing that can spoil the twelve minutes she waits all year for.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Pasen, pasen. Voy a hacer café.
steps.en: Come in, come in. I will make coffee.

options.es: Con permiso, doña. Yo le ayudo con las tazas.
options.en: Excuse me, doña. I will help you with the cups.
options.feedback: Half past midnight and she is making coffee for eight people. Getting up to help is worth more to her than the song was.

options.en: Thank you, doña.
options.feedback: Fine. Everyone else has already sat down and she is on her feet.

options.es: No se moleste, doña, ya nos vamos.
options.en: Do not trouble yourself, doña, we are going now.
options.feedback: Nobody is going anywhere. The coffee at one in the morning is the second half of the serenata.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Y usted, mijo. Gracias por venir con ellos.
steps.en: And you, son. Thank you for coming with them.

options.es: Es lo menos que puedo hacer, doña. Y con mucho cariño.
options.en: It is the least I can do, doña. And gladly.
options.feedback: That is the right register and it is not a cold one here. She has just called you mijo, which is the thing that actually happened tonight.

options.en: Not at all, doña.
options.feedback: Polite. She said something to you that she does not say lightly and you answered a formula.

options.en: Julio told me to come.
options.feedback: True and disastrous. You have just told her you came because you were told to.

scenarios.title: La casa poco a poco
scenarios.desc: A Sunday, a bag of cement, and nobody charging anybody
scenarios.setting: It is eight in the morning on a Sunday and four men you are related to by marriage are standing on your bit of land.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: Ideay, cuñado. Trajimos los bloques. ¿Por dónde empezamos?
steps.en: Ideay, brother-in-law. We brought the blocks. Where do we start?

options.es: Por el primer cuarto. Con techo y puerta y ahí vivimos.
options.en: With the first room. With a roof and a door and we live in that.
options.feedback: One room first, live in it, and the rest can take ten years. Almost every house on the street was built exactly like this.

options.en: Wherever you say.
options.feedback: They will decide and it will be fine. It is your house, and having a plan for it is worth saying out loud.

options.es: Yo quería hacerla toda de una vez.
options.en: I wanted to build the whole thing at once.
options.feedback: Nobody has the money to build a whole house at once, and everybody has a house. Saying that out loud reads as showing off or as not understanding.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Venga, le enseño a mezclar. Arena, cemento y agua, pero no de un solo.
steps.en: Come here, I will show you how to mix. Sand, cement and water, but not all at once.

options.es: Enséñeme, don Beto. Yo nunca he hecho esto.
options.en: Show me, don Beto. I have never done this.
options.feedback: He is seventy-two and he has come on a Sunday to teach you. Admitting you cannot do it is the whole reason he is enjoying himself.

options.en: I sort of know already.
options.feedback: You do not. He will let you get it wrong once and then show you, which takes longer for everybody.

options.en: Better if you do it.
options.feedback: It is your house. Standing back while other men work on it for nothing is the one thing you cannot do today.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Aquí nadie cobra, cuñado. Pero a mediodía queremos comer.
steps.en: Nobody charges here, brother-in-law. But at midday we want to eat.

options.es: Ya está todo listo. Comida y cerveza a las doce.
options.en: Already sorted. Food and beer at twelve.
options.feedback: That is the payment and everybody knows it. A man who feeds the people who came is a man they will come back for next Sunday.

options.en: I will pay for lunch, of course.
options.feedback: Right idea. It sounds better as food you have arranged than as money you are handing over.

options.es: Les puedo dar algo por el día.
options.en: I can give you something for the day.
options.feedback: Offering your wife's brothers a wage for coming to help turns family into labour. Chino just told you the price and it was lunch.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: El otro domingo venimos otra vez. Vamos a ir levantando poco a poco.
steps.en: We will come again next Sunday. We will get it up bit by bit.

options.es: Poco a poco, pues. Aquí los espero.
options.en: Bit by bit, then. I will be waiting for you.
options.feedback: Poco a poco is not resignation here, it is the method. Say it back and you are agreeing to the next ten Sundays.

options.en: Thank you, truly.
options.feedback: Warm. Thanks are slightly beside the point for something they consider ordinary.

options.en: And when do you think it will be finished?
options.feedback: It does not finish. That is why half the roofs on this street have iron rods sticking out of them, waiting for a second floor.

scenarios.title: El bautizo
scenarios.desc: Being asked to be a godparent
scenarios.setting: Marcos has been circling something for twenty minutes and has now put down his cup.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Fíjate que te quería preguntar algo.
steps.en: The thing is, I wanted to ask you something.

options.en: Go on then.
options.feedback: Two words that open the door without rushing him. That is all he needed.

options.en: Of course, what is it?
options.feedback: Fine. Qué pasó suggests something has gone wrong, which is not the tone.

options.en: Do you need money?
options.feedback: Guessing wrong at the wrong moment, and it says what you assume of him.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Queremos que seás el padrino del chavalito.
steps.en: We want you to be the boy's godfather.

options.en: Yes. Yes, of course.
options.feedback: No hesitation and no questions first. Anything else in that gap would have been heard.

options.en: Are you sure?
options.feedback: He has been working up to it for twenty minutes. He is sure.

options.en: Let me think about it.
options.feedback: An honest answer that will land as a no, and he will never ask again.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Es un compromiso, vos. No es solo la fiesta.
steps.en: It is a commitment. It is not just the party.

options.es: Ya sé lo que es. Por eso dije que sí.
options.en: I know what it is. That is why I said yes.
options.feedback: You told him you understood the weight and had already accepted it. That is the whole conversation done.

options.en: Yes, I understand.
options.feedback: Correct. He was checking, and the check deserved more than agreement.

options.es: ¿Y qué es lo que tengo que hacer?
options.en: And what is it I have to do?
options.feedback: Asked after saying yes, it is fine. Asked here it sounds like you are looking for the size of the bill.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Entonces ya somos compadres.
steps.en: Then we are compadres now.

options.es: Compadre, entonces. Se oye raro todavía.
options.en: Compadre, then. It still sounds strange.
options.feedback: You used the word for the first time and admitted it is new. Both things are true and he will like both.

options.en: Yes, compadres.
options.feedback: Correct and warm. It says the word without noticing that it changed.

options.en: Same as before, then.
options.feedback: It is not the same as before, and saying so takes something away from him.

scenarios.title: Le tocaba a alguien
scenarios.desc: The suegra asks you, and not her own sons
scenarios.setting: Doña Elena phones the house at nine on a Tuesday. Lucía is bathing the baby and you answer.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Ah, es usted. Fíjese que tengo un problema con un papel del banco.
steps.en: Ah, it is you. The thing is I have a problem with a bank document.

options.en: Tell me, doña. What does the paper say?
options.feedback: You took it as yours before asking whether it was. That is the whole test and it is over in one line.

options.en: Do you want me to tell Lucía?
options.feedback: Helpful, and it hands the call back. She rang the house and got you, which is not an accident.

options.en: She is coming, hold on.
options.feedback: You have just passed your mother-in-law to somebody else in her own phone call.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Es un trámite que no entiendo. ¿Usted podría acompañarme?
steps.en: It is paperwork I do not understand. Could you go with me?

options.es: Claro que sí. ¿Qué día le queda bien?
options.en: Of course. What day suits you?
options.feedback: Yes first, logistics second. Any gap between those two would have been the answer.

options.en: Yes, I will go when I can.
options.feedback: A yes with no day in it. Here that reads as a maybe.

options.en: And can Julio not?
options.feedback: He can. She did not ask him.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: El jueves, si se puede.
steps.en: Thursday, if possible.

options.es: El jueves entonces. Yo paso por usted.
options.en: Thursday then. I will come by for you.
options.feedback: Fixed the day and took the travel off her. A woman of sixty-two should not be finding the bank on her own.

options.en: Thursday is fine.
options.feedback: Agreed. She still has to get herself there.

options.es: Nos vemos allá a las ocho.
options.en: See you there at eight.
options.feedback: Meeting her at the door of a bank she does not understand is half a favour.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Bueno pues. Hasta el jueves.
steps.en: All right then. Until Thursday.

options.es: Hasta el jueves, doña. Que descanse.
options.en: Until Thursday, doña. Sleep well.
options.feedback: Closed it the way you would close it with your own mother. That is what she rang to find out.

options.en: Goodbye, doña.
options.feedback: Adiós still sounds like forever. Hasta el jueves was right there.

options.en: I will let you know.
options.feedback: You just agreed on Thursday. Now it is uncertain again.

scenarios.title: ¿Cómo sigue?
scenarios.desc: Nobody in the house will say the word out loud
scenarios.setting: Don Beto has not got out of bed in a week and his house is full of people you have never met.

steps.speaker: Doña Rosa
steps.es: Pase, mijo. Está delicado.
steps.en: Come in, love. He is delicate.

options.en: And how is he getting on, doña?
options.feedback: Cómo sigue, not cómo está. One asks after a person over time and the other asks for a fact, and everybody who walks through that door asks the first.

options.en: How is he?
options.feedback: Understood, and it sounds like a form being filled in. Cómo sigue is what the room is saying.

options.en: Is it serious, doña?
options.feedback: Nobody says grave out loud. She said delicado, which is how it is said, and saying the other word feels like calling it down on him.

steps.speaker: Doña Rosa
steps.es: Ahí va. Anoche durmió un poco.
steps.en: He is getting there. Last night he slept a little.

options.es: Qué bueno, doña. Primero Dios se compone.
options.en: That is good, doña. God willing he will pick up.
options.feedback: Take the small good news and add the formula. In a house like this nobody is asking you for a prognosis, only for hope said correctly.

options.en: Hopefully he gets better soon.
options.feedback: Kind and correct. Componerse is the verb people use for coming back from an illness like this one.

options.en: And what exactly did the doctor say?
options.feedback: She has been avoiding that sentence all week on purpose. Asking for the detail asks her to say the thing nobody is saying.

steps.speaker: Doña Rosa
steps.es: Siéntese un rato. Está lleno de gente pero él la oye.
steps.en: Sit down for a while. It is full of people but he can hear it.

options.es: Aquí me quedo un rato, doña.
options.en: I will stay a while, doña.
options.feedback: That is the whole visit. Nobody comes to say anything clever, they come to be in the house and to be counted.

options.en: I only came to say hello.
options.feedback: Nobody only comes to say hello here. Staying half an hour costs you nothing and is noticed.

options.es: No quiero molestar con tanta gente.
options.en: I do not want to be in the way with so many people.
options.feedback: The point is the number of people. An empty house at a time like this is the thing everybody is working to prevent.

steps.speaker: Doña Rosa
steps.es: ¿Y usted quiere pasar a verlo?
steps.en: And do you want to go in and see him?

options.es: Si él puede, sí. Solo un momento.
options.en: If he is able, yes. Only for a moment.
options.feedback: Yes, and short. You leave the decision with her and you do not sit at the bed for an hour.

options.en: Whatever you say, doña.
options.feedback: Respectful. She asked because she wanted an answer, not the decision back.

options.en: Better not, so as not to tire him out.
options.feedback: She offered because he would want to see you. Refusing spares him nothing and it is the one thing he will hear about.

scenarios.title: Se puso malo
scenarios.desc: A hospital corridor at eleven at night
scenarios.setting: Chino's father-in-law was brought in at nine. There are eleven people in the corridor and nobody is leaving.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Ideay, vos. No tenías que venir.
steps.en: Ideay, you. You did not have to come.

options.en: I know. Here I am, then.
options.feedback: The exact answer. It refuses the excuse without making a speech out of showing up.

options.en: I wanted to see how you all were.
options.feedback: Warm and true. Slightly more explanation than the moment wants.

options.en: I came in case you needed anything.
options.feedback: Well meant, and it makes your being here conditional. It is not.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Está en cirugía. No sabemos nada todavía.
steps.en: He is in surgery. We do not know anything yet.

options.en: I will stay. Have you all eaten anything?
options.feedback: The two useful sentences in a corridor: I am staying, and food. Nobody in that hallway has eaten.

options.en: I hope it all goes well.
options.feedback: Kind, and it is what everyone else has already said four times.

options.es: Todo va a estar bien, ya vas a ver.
options.en: Everything is going to be fine, you will see.
options.feedback: You cannot know that, and he knows you cannot. It closes him down.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: No, nadie ha comido.
steps.en: No, nobody has eaten.

options.es: Voy a la esquina y traigo café para todos.
options.en: I will go to the corner and bring coffee for everybody.
options.feedback: Small, concrete, immediate. In a hospital corridor that is worth more than anything you could say.

options.en: You should all eat something.
options.feedback: True. Advice in a corridor is a job you have handed to somebody else.

options.en: I am not hungry either.
options.feedback: Now nobody eats. You were the one person free to fix it.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Vos sos el único que no es de la familia aquí.
steps.en: You are the only one here who is not family.

options.es: Puede ser. Pero aquí estoy igual.
options.en: Maybe. But I am here all the same.
options.feedback: You did not argue with him and you did not leave. Both halves matter.

options.en: Well, almost.
options.feedback: Light. He was not making conversation.

options.en: I am family too.
options.feedback: Claiming it out loud in that corridor is the one way to not be.

scenarios.title: El novenario
scenarios.desc: Nine nights in somebody else’s house
scenarios.setting: A neighbour has died. Lucía tells you the rosary is at seven and that you are going every night.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Vas a venir todas las noches?
steps.en: Are you going to come every night?

options.es: Sí. ¿Qué se hace, solo estar ahí?
options.en: Yes. What does one do, just be there?
options.feedback: The yes came first and the question second. That order is the whole thing.

options.es: Voy a ir hoy por lo menos.
options.en: I will go today at least.
options.feedback: Going once is better than not going. Everybody counts the nights.

options.en: I hardly knew him.
options.feedback: Nobody is there because they knew him. They are there because the family is.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Estar ahí. Y llevá algo para el café.
steps.en: Be there. And take something for the coffee.

options.es: Va. Llevo azúcar y pan, ¿está bien?
options.en: Right. I will take sugar and bread, is that all right?
options.feedback: Named the thing and checked. Nine nights of coffee is a real cost to that house and this is how it gets shared.

options.en: All right, I will take something.
options.feedback: Fine. Naming it means nobody ends up with four bags of sugar.

options.en: Do you have to take something?
options.feedback: She has just said so. Asking again sounds like looking for a way out.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Y no hablés mucho. Ahí se está callado.
steps.en: And do not talk much. There you stay quiet.

options.es: Entendido. Yo saludo y me quedo atrás.
options.en: Understood. I will greet people and stay at the back.
options.feedback: You took the instruction and turned it into a plan. That is somebody who has understood what a wake is for.

options.es: Está bien, voy a estar callado.
options.en: All right, I will be quiet.
options.feedback: Correct. Quiet is not the same as absent, and the greeting matters.

options.en: And what does one talk about then?
options.feedback: Nothing. That is the answer, and asking makes the silence sound like a problem.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: La novena noche es distinta. Esa es más grande.
steps.en: The ninth night is different. That one is bigger.

options.es: Entonces esa noche pido permiso en el trabajo.
options.en: Then that night I will ask for time off work.
options.feedback: Nobody asked you to. Doing it without being asked is what gets remembered in that family for years.

options.en: I will be there for that one too.
options.feedback: A promise, and a good one. Saying how you will manage it makes it real.

options.en: Nine nights is a lot.
options.feedback: It is. Everybody in that house knows exactly how many it is.

scenarios.title: Los difuntos
scenarios.desc: November 2, and a grave that is not yours
scenarios.setting: You are at the cemetery with doña Elena, carrying a bucket, a brush and a bag of yellow flowers.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Aquí está. Este es el papá de Lucía.
steps.en: Here it is. This is Lucía's father.

options.en: Pleased to meet you, don Rafael.
options.feedback: Greeting the grave is exactly what people do here, and it is the warmest thing you could have said.

options.en: The grave looks nice.
options.feedback: Kind, and it comments on the stone rather than on the man.

options.en: How long has he been here?
options.feedback: A fact question at the wrong moment. She will answer it and something will close.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Ayúdeme a limpiar, mijo. Ahí está el cepillo.
steps.en: Help me clean it, son. The brush is there.

options.es: Deme el balde, doña. Yo lo lleno.
options.en: Give me the bucket, doña. I will fill it.
options.feedback: You took the heavier half without being asked. That is the entire job description of a yerno today.

options.en: Yes, I will help you in a bit.
options.feedback: Ahorita on your knees in a cemetery is a strange thing to say. Start now.

options.en: You tell me what to do.
options.feedback: She has just told you. Waiting to be directed twice is not helping.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Él nunca lo conoció a usted.
steps.en: He never met you.

options.es: No, pero usted me habla de él. Con eso algo lo conozco.
options.en: No, but you talk to me about him. That way I know him a little.
options.feedback: It gives her the credit for keeping him alive and it is true. She will remember that sentence.

options.en: How sad.
options.feedback: Kind, and it closes the subject she just opened.

options.es: Sí, qué se le va a hacer.
options.en: Yes, what can you do.
options.feedback: Ni modo is for a broken drain. Not here, not to her, not today.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Bueno. Ya está. Vámonos antes del sol.
steps.en: Right. That is done. Let us go before the sun.

options.en: Let us go. Shall we come back next year?
options.feedback: Asking to be included next year is asking to keep the place you have just been given.

options.en: Yes, it looks nice now.
options.feedback: Fine. It ends the morning on the stone rather than on the two of you.

options.es: Al fin, ya me estaba asando.
options.en: At last, I was roasting.
options.feedback: True, and there are three hours of her morning in that grave.

scenarios.title: Te lo agradezco
scenarios.desc: Thanking somebody so that it counts
scenarios.setting: Don Beto sat up two nights in the corridor with you and has never mentioned it since.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: ¿Y cómo salió el chavalo?
steps.en: And how did the boy come out?

options.es: Bien, don Beto. Gracias a Dios y gracias a usted.
options.en: Well, don Beto. Thank God and thank you.
options.feedback: The two thanks in the order they are said here, and yours is the second one on purpose.

options.en: He came out fine, thank you.
options.feedback: True and pleasant. It thanks him for asking rather than for the two nights.

options.en: Well. And how are you?
options.feedback: Turning it back so fast is a way of not saying it at all.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Qué bueno. Eso era lo que había que saber.
steps.en: That is good. That was the thing that needed knowing.

options.es: Usted estuvo dos noches ahí conmigo. Eso no se me olvida.
options.en: You were there two nights with me. I will not forget that.
options.feedback: Named the thing plainly. Around here that is said once, out loud, and then never again.

options.en: I am grateful for the hospital business.
options.feedback: The right idea, wrapped in a phrase. Say what he actually did.

options.en: Sorry for bothering you so much.
options.feedback: Apologising for it takes the gift back off him.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Ideay, no diga nada. Uno hace lo que tiene que hacer.
steps.en: Ideay, do not say anything. One does what one has to do.

options.es: Igual se lo digo, don Beto.
options.en: I am telling you anyway, don Beto.
options.feedback: He deflected, as he had to, and you said it anyway once. That is the correct number of times.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: You let him wave it away. He will assume it did not weigh much.

options.en: Yes, anybody would have done it.
options.feedback: Nobody else did.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Cuando le toque a usted, hágalo y ya.
steps.en: When it is your turn, do it and that is all.

options.es: Así va a ser. Se lo prometo.
options.en: That is how it will be. I promise you.
options.feedback: He turned the thanks into an instruction, which is the local exchange rate, and you accepted it.

options.en: Hopefully I will be able to.
options.feedback: Softer than the moment. He did not say ojalá when it was his turn.

options.en: I hope I do not have to.
options.feedback: True, and it dodges the one thing he asked for.

scenarios.title: Qué tuani
scenarios.desc: A word you learned from a teenager, said to a grandmother
scenarios.setting: Doña Chepa's shop, Saturday morning, and there is an eighty-year-old woman buying bread beside you.

steps.speaker: Señora
steps.es: ¿Y cómo le va aquí en Managua, mijo?
steps.en: And how are you getting on here in Managua, son?

options.es: Muy bien, señora. Aquí muy contento.
options.en: Very well, señora. Very happy here.
options.feedback: Plain, warm, and pitched at her age. That is all this question ever wanted.

options.en: All good, thanks.
options.feedback: Correct. Señora would have cost you nothing and bought a lot.

options.en: Everything is deacachimba.
options.feedback: The word is not wrong. In front of a woman of eighty, out of a married man's mouth, it is the wrong word.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Bueno... aquí tiene su pan, doña Julia.
steps.en: Well... here is your bread, doña Julia.

options.es: Que le vaya bien, doña Julia.
options.en: All the best, doña Julia.
options.feedback: You caught the name and used it. The room was awkward and you made it ordinary again.

options.en: Goodbye.
options.feedback: Adiós to somebody walking out of a shop still sounds bigger than it is.

options.en: Never mind, ignore that.
options.feedback: Drawing attention to it in front of her is worse than the word was.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Mijo. Esa palabra es de chavalos.
steps.en: Son. That word is for kids.

options.es: Puchica. ¿Y con quién sí se puede decir?
options.en: Damn. And who can it be said with, then?
options.feedback: Took the correction and asked the useful follow-up. That is how the rest of the slang gets learned safely.

options.en: Ah, sorry.
options.feedback: Fine, and it ends the lesson she was about to give you for free.

options.es: Roberto la dice todo el tiempo.
options.en: Roberto says it all the time.
options.feedback: He is seventeen. That is the entire point she is making.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Entre amigos sí. Con una señora mayor no.
steps.en: Among friends yes. With an older lady no.

options.en: Understood. Tuani I can use, right?
options.feedback: You checked the neighbouring word instead of guessing. That is exactly the habit to build.

options.es: Ya no la voy a decir.
options.en: I am not going to say it any more.
options.feedback: Safe, and it throws away a good word instead of learning where it lives.

options.es: Es que ustedes son muy delicados.
options.en: You people are very sensitive.
options.feedback: Ustedes, and a verdict, thirty seconds after being helped.

scenarios.title: Semana Santa
scenarios.desc: Six days when the whole country stops and nobody warned you
scenarios.setting: You have just told Lucía you are thinking of travelling next week and she has put her cup down.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿La otra semana? Gordo, es Semana Santa. Ni lo intentés.
steps.en: Next week? Gordo, it is Semana Santa. Do not even try.

options.en: Ideay, is it that bad? Tell me.
options.feedback: Ask before you argue. Six days when nobody in the country works is not a long weekend with extra traffic.

options.en: But it is only a few days.
options.feedback: It is six, and they are the six when every bus in Nicaragua is already full.

options.es: Yo saco pasaje temprano y ya.
options.en: I will buy a ticket early and that is that.
options.feedback: Early was February. From the Saturday before, there is no seat to anywhere at any price.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Desde el sábado no hay pasaje para ningún lado. Todo el mundo va a la playa.
steps.en: From Saturday there are no tickets anywhere. Everybody goes to the beach.

options.es: Entonces vamos a la playa nosotros también.
options.en: Then we go to the beach as well.
options.feedback: The only sensible answer. If the whole country is going to Pochomil or Poneloya, the week is much better spent with them than against them.

options.es: Va pues, me quedo en la casa.
options.en: All right then, I will stay home.
options.feedback: Restful and slightly sad. Managua in Semana Santa is the emptiest you will ever see it.

options.es: No entiendo por qué todos salen el mismo día.
options.en: I do not understand why everybody leaves on the same day.
options.feedback: Because it is the only week of the year nobody works. There is nothing to understand and nothing to fix.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Pero el viernes en la mañana no. El viernes vamos al cementerio.
steps.en: But not Friday morning. On Friday we go to the cemetery.

options.es: ¿A limpiar la tumba antes de irnos?
options.en: To clean the grave before we go?
options.feedback: You already knew. Cemetery in the morning, beach in the afternoon, and nobody in the country finds that a strange order.

options.es: Está bien, yo voy con vos.
options.en: All right, I will go with you.
options.feedback: Going is the whole thing. Knowing what is done there is the part you are still learning.

options.es: ¿Y eso qué tiene que ver con la playa?
options.en: And what has that got to do with the beach?
options.feedback: Nothing, and both happen on the same day every year. It is not a contradiction to anybody but you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Y llevá gorra, que el sol de esa semana está bravo.
steps.en: And take a cap, the sun that week is fierce.

options.es: Gorra, agua y sombra. Ya aprendí, negra.
options.en: Cap, water and shade. I have learned, negra.
options.feedback: March is the end of the dry season and the hottest week of the year. Listing it back is how you show her you are not going to be carried home red.

options.en: All right, I will take a cap.
options.feedback: Fine. She will pack the water anyway.

options.es: A mí el sol no me hace nada.
options.en: The sun does not affect me.
options.feedback: You are the palest person on that beach. Everybody there has watched a chele learn this once.

scenarios.title: El tope
scenarios.desc: August 1, and the whole city moves at once
scenarios.setting: Seven in the morning, thousands of people, and Marcos has told you twice not to let go of him.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: No te me soltés, vos. Aquí se pierde uno.
steps.en: Do not let go of me. People get lost here.

options.es: Dale. Si me pierdo, ¿dónde nos vemos?
options.en: Right. If I get lost, where do we meet?
options.feedback: Accepted and planned for the thing he just warned you about. Sensible without being nervous.

options.en: All right, I am right behind you.
options.feedback: Fine, and in that crowd behind lasts about forty seconds.

options.en: Do not worry, I know my way.
options.feedback: You have been to this city for four years and never to this. He has been coming since he was six.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Mirá aquel. Ese va pagando una promesa.
steps.en: Look at that one. He is paying a promise.

options.en: Is that why he is smeared in oil?
options.feedback: You noticed the thing that matters and asked. He has been waiting all morning for somebody to ask.

options.en: Ah, I see.
options.feedback: You do not see, and he knows it. Ask.

options.en: What a strange thing.
options.feedback: Said out loud in that crowd about a man paying for his child's health.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Se lo untan y caminan los diez días.
steps.en: They smear it on and walk the ten days.

options.es: Chocho. Diez días con eso encima.
options.en: Chocho. Ten days with that on.
options.feedback: The right word and the right amount of respect in it. That is somebody reacting, not observing.

options.en: That is a long time.
options.feedback: True. Flat where a reaction was called for.

options.es: Eso no puede ser bueno para la piel.
options.en: That cannot be good for the skin.
options.feedback: A health note in the middle of somebody's faith.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Y vos, tenés alguna promesa?
steps.en: And you, do you have a promise?

options.en: No, none. Do you?
options.feedback: Answered honestly and turned it back. In that crowd it is a real question and he may answer it.

options.es: No, yo no soy de eso.
options.en: No, I am not one for that.
options.feedback: Honest. It also closes the door he was opening.

options.en: I do not believe in promises.
options.feedback: Half the people around you are paying one. Save the position for another day.

scenarios.title: El enano en tu puerta
scenarios.desc: A giant woman, a big-headed boy and forty verses
scenarios.setting: December, seven at night, a drum coming down your street, and doña Carmen has just elbowed you.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ahí viene la Gigantona. Salí a verla.
steps.en: Here comes the Gigantona. Come out and see her.

options.en: Chocho, how big! Who is inside?
options.feedback: Reacted first and asked second, which is the right way round when something arrives at your door.

options.es: Ah, sí, ya la había visto.
options.en: Ah, yes, I had seen it before.
options.feedback: Perhaps. Saying so takes the moment away from the person showing you.

options.en: And what is that?
options.feedback: Fair on the first December. Doña Carmen just told you what it is.

steps.speaker: Enano
steps.es: Aquí está el Enano Cabezón, que viene de León...
steps.en: Here is the Big-Headed Dwarf, who comes from León...

options.en: (Listen without interrupting)
options.feedback: Nothing to say. He is eight and he has forty of these by heart. Let him finish.

options.en: (Take out the phone to film it)
options.feedback: Everybody does. It also puts a screen between you and the one boy performing at your gate.

options.en: I do not understand a word.
options.feedback: Said in the middle of the recital, to the reciter's face.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ya terminó. Ahora le toca a usted.
steps.en: He has finished. Now it is your turn.

options.en: Here you go, kid. That was good.
options.feedback: The coin and a word about the performance. He will remember the second part longer.

options.en: Take this, boy.
options.feedback: The coin goes across. He recited forty lines and got a transaction.

options.en: How much does one usually give?
options.feedback: Asking the price out loud in front of him.

steps.speaker: Enano
steps.es: Gracias, y hasta el otro año.
steps.en: Thank you, and until next year.

options.es: Hasta el otro año pues. Aquí lo espero.
options.en: Until next year then. I will be waiting here.
options.feedback: You have just told a boy he has a door to come back to. That is how the December round survives.

options.en: Goodbye.
options.feedback: Small, and after all that it lands smaller than you mean it.

options.en: That is enough for today.
options.feedback: He is leaving anyway. Now it sounds like you were waiting for him to go.

scenarios.title: Delroy
scenarios.desc: Half the country you had not accounted for
scenarios.setting: A new man on the afternoon shift takes a phone call in a language that sounds like English and is not.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: Sorry, that was my mother. She no speak Spanish.
steps.en: Sorry, that was my mother. She does not speak Spanish.

options.es: ¿De dónde sos vos? Nunca había oído eso.
options.en: Where are you from? I had never heard that.
options.feedback: Curious, direct, and vos. It treats him as a workmate rather than a curiosity.

options.en: Is that English?
options.feedback: Close, and a bit off. It sounds like English and it is not, and he gets asked that daily.

options.en: Are you from Jamaica?
options.feedback: He is Nicaraguan. That guess is the one he has been correcting since he arrived in Managua.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: De Bluefields. Es criollo, no inglés.
steps.en: From Bluefields. It is Creole, not English.

options.es: ¿Y allá el español es la segunda lengua?
options.en: And over there Spanish is the second language?
options.feedback: You got straight to the thing that actually surprises people from this side of the country.

options.en: Ah, how interesting.
options.feedback: Polite and finished. He would have kept going if you had asked anything.

options.en: But that is Nicaragua all the same, is it not?
options.feedback: It is, and phrased like that it sounds like you are correcting him about his own coast.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: La cuarta, a veces. Primero criollo, inglés y miskito.
steps.en: The fourth, sometimes. First Creole, English and Miskito.

options.es: Chocho, y yo pensaba que aquí era un solo idioma.
options.en: Chocho, and I thought there was one language here.
options.feedback: Admitting what you assumed, out loud, is the fastest way to be told the rest.

options.en: I did not know any of that.
options.feedback: True and fine. It stops just short of asking him for more.

options.es: Yo pensé que todos hablaban español.
options.en: I thought everybody spoke Spanish.
options.feedback: Almost the same sentence, said as a fact about the country rather than about you.

steps.speaker: Delroy
steps.es: Casi nadie de aquí ha ido para allá.
steps.en: Almost nobody from here has been over there.

options.es: Yo tampoco. Pero algún día quiero ir.
options.en: Nor have I. But some day I want to go.
options.feedback: You put yourself in the same sentence as everybody else and left a door open. Honest, and he will hold you to it.

options.en: It must be nice.
options.feedback: Warm and empty. He was telling you something about the country, not about scenery.

options.en: The thing is it is very far.
options.feedback: That is the excuse everybody here gives him. You have just become one more.

scenarios.title: El año viejo
scenarios.desc: Burning the year on the pavement at midnight
scenarios.setting: Roberto arrives at seven in the morning on the thirty-first with an armful of old clothes and a plan.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Hay que hacer el muñeco. ¿Tenés ropa vieja?
steps.en: We have to make the dummy. Have you got old clothes?

options.es: Debo tener algo. ¿De qué lo vamos a hacer?
options.en: I must have something. What are we going to make it out of?
options.feedback: You did not ask what a muñeco is, you asked what it is made of. That is somebody joining in rather than being told about it.

options.en: A dummy of what?
options.feedback: Fair question. He is going to look at you as though you were born yesterday, which he will anyway.

options.en: I have nothing to throw out.
options.feedback: You do. Lucía is already holding the shirt she has hated for two years.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Del año viejo. Se quema a medianoche.
steps.en: Of the old year. It gets burned at midnight.

options.en: And why is it burned? Tell me.
options.feedback: Asking for the reason instead of the instructions. He is seventeen and delighted to be the one who knows.

options.en: Ah, I understand now.
options.feedback: You do not, quite, and there is a good answer available for free.

options.en: That sounds dangerous.
options.feedback: Twenty fires on one dirt street. It is, and that is not the interesting part.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Todo lo malo del año se le mete adentro.
steps.en: Everything bad from the year gets stuffed inside it.

options.es: Entonces este año le vamos a meter bastante.
options.en: Then this year we are going to stuff plenty in.
options.feedback: You took the idea and made a joke of it that is also true. That is exactly the register of the thirty-first.

options.en: What a good idea.
options.feedback: Warm, and it treats a custom like a suggestion.

options.es: Yo no creo en esas cosas.
options.en: I do not believe in those things.
options.feedback: Nobody asked you to believe. They asked you to help stuff a shirt with newspaper.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: A las doce lo quemamos todos juntos.
steps.en: At twelve we all burn them together.

options.en: I will be there. Do we need matches?
options.feedback: Committed and thought one step ahead. That is somebody who is in it rather than watching it.

options.en: All right, see you there.
options.feedback: Accepted. Bringing something is what turns watching into taking part.

options.en: I will watch from inside.
options.feedback: From inside the house, on the one night when the whole street is outside.

scenarios.title: Padrino de las sillas
scenarios.desc: Being asked to pay for part of somebody’s quince
scenarios.setting: Marcos has been talking about his daughter's fifteenth for three months and has finally stopped talking.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Vos sabés que los quince salen caros.
steps.en: You know a quince works out expensive.

options.en: I can imagine. How are you putting it together?
options.feedback: You showed you understood and asked how, which is the opening he needs to name the padrinos.

options.en: Yes, they must be expensive.
options.feedback: Agreement. He is trying to get somewhere and you have not helped him.

options.en: And why do you all spend so much?
options.feedback: Judging the whole thing thirty seconds before he asks you to be part of it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Con padrinos. Uno del pastel, otro de la música.
steps.en: With godparents. One of the cake, another of the music.

options.en: Ah, right. And is one still missing?
options.feedback: You opened the door for him instead of making him push it. That is a kindness he will remember.

options.en: What a good way of doing it.
options.feedback: True. It appreciates the system and steps back from it.

options.en: We do not do that where I come from.
options.feedback: Possibly the least useful sentence available at that moment.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Faltan las sillas. Doscientas, alquiladas.
steps.en: The chairs are missing. Two hundred, rented.

options.es: Yo se las pongo. Contá con eso.
options.en: I will cover them. Count on it.
options.feedback: Said before he finished asking, and with a number in it. That is how a padrino answers.

options.en: And how much does that come to?
options.feedback: Fair, and asking the price first turns a padrinazgo into a quote.

options.es: Déjame ver cómo ando de plata.
options.en: Let me see how I am for money.
options.feedback: Honest. It will be heard as a no, and the chairs will fall to somebody else.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: De verdad, vos. Gracias.
steps.en: Honestly. Thank you.

options.es: Ideay, no es nada. Es tu hija.
options.en: Ideay, it is nothing. It is your daughter.
options.feedback: Waves off the thanks and names the reason. Between compadres that is the whole exchange.

options.en: No problem.
options.feedback: Fine. It answers the words and not the fact that he asked you and not his brother.

options.en: We will sort out the payment later.
options.feedback: There is no payment. You have just turned a gift into an invoice.

scenarios.title: La masa del sábado
scenarios.desc: Saturday night, fifty nacatamales, and an arm that stops working
scenarios.setting: It is nine at night, doña Chepa's kitchen is full of steam, and somebody has handed you a wooden spoon.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Venga, mijo. Batí esa masa un rato que a mí ya se me murió el brazo.
steps.en: Come here, love. Beat that dough a while, my arm is dead already.

options.es: Deme acá, doña. ¿Hasta cuándo la bato?
options.en: Give it here, doña. How long do I beat it for?
options.feedback: Take it and ask how you will know when it is done. The answer is by hand and by look, which is why she has to show you.

options.en: I do not know how to do that.
options.feedback: Nobody is asking you to know. You are being asked because there are fifty of these to make before morning.

options.en: And is there no machine for it?
options.feedback: There is, and hers is by hand, and that is the reason people buy hers. Say that in that kitchen and see how it lands.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Hasta que quede suave. Maíz molido, manteca y sal, nada más.
steps.en: Until it goes smooth. Ground maize, lard and salt, nothing else.

options.es: ¿Y por qué solo los domingos, doña?
options.en: And why only on Sundays, doña?
options.feedback: The right question while your arm is busy. A nacatamal is Sunday-morning food and nobody makes one on a Wednesday.

options.en: Smooth. I am getting there.
options.feedback: You are working, which is what the kitchen needs. She is in a talking mood and you are not using it.

options.es: Esto lleva un montón de trabajo.
options.en: This is an awful lot of work.
options.feedback: The work is the entire reason it means something. Say that in that kitchen and watch her face.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Porque es comida de domingo, pues. Y porque una no puede todos los días.
steps.en: Because it is Sunday food. And because a woman cannot do this every day.

options.es: Con razón la cuadra huele igual los domingos.
options.en: No wonder the whole block smells the same on Sundays.
options.feedback: You put two things together out loud. Three houses on this street are doing exactly this tonight and by nine tomorrow the smell is the same in all of them.

options.en: That makes sense, doña.
options.feedback: Fair. There was a better sentence in you about the smell of the street.

options.es: Podría hacerlos entre semana y vender más.
options.en: You could make them midweek and sell more.
options.feedback: Nobody would buy one. Advising a woman of sixty on her own business is a fast way to be handed back the spoon.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Mañana a las siete le guardo uno. Con su pedazo de cerdo.
steps.en: Tomorrow at seven I will keep one for you. With its piece of pork.

options.es: Ahí estoy a las siete, doña. Con gaseosa roja.
options.en: I will be there at seven, doña. With a red fizzy drink.
options.feedback: Seven in the morning, and the red gaseosa beside it. You have just described a Nicaraguan Sunday exactly as it is.

options.en: Thank you, doña. I will be there.
options.feedback: Fine. Naming the hour tells her you know it will be gone by nine.

options.es: ¿Me lo puede guardar para el mediodía?
options.en: Could you keep it for me until midday?
options.feedback: By midday there are none left anywhere in the barrio. That is the one rule of the nacatamal.

scenarios.title: A las doce en punto
scenarios.desc: Arriving on time, and being put to work for two hours
scenarios.setting: The invitation said twelve, it is twelve, and doña Carmen is in the patio with a broom and wet hair.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¡Ideay! ¿Ya vinieron? Si todavía no hay nada listo.
steps.en: Ideay! You are here already? There is nothing ready yet.

options.es: Llegamos temprano, doña. Póngame a hacer algo.
options.en: We came early, doña. Put me to work.
options.feedback: You are two hours early by local reckoning and there is only one way out of that: pick up a chair and start carrying.

options.es: La invitación decía a las doce.
options.en: The invitation said twelve.
options.feedback: It did, and twelve meant about two. Producing the evidence is the most foreign thing you could do standing in her patio.

options.en: Sorry, doña. Shall we come back later?
options.feedback: You will not be allowed to leave. Staying and helping is what happens next either way.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Ay, mijo, agarrá esas sillas y ponelas alrededor.
steps.en: Oh, love, grab those chairs and put them round.

options.en: Right then. How many shall I put out?
options.feedback: Punctuality has a price here and this is it. Two hours of work, and by the end you know where everything in her kitchen lives.

options.en: Coming.
options.feedback: Fine. You will put out the wrong number and carry them twice.

options.es: Lucía me dijo que era muy temprano.
options.en: Lucía told me it was too early.
options.feedback: She did, three times. Saying so now in front of everybody helps nobody, least of all you.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: El primer invitado llega a la una y media, vas a ver.
steps.en: The first guest will arrive at half past one, you will see.

options.es: Entonces la hora nica es la de verdad y la otra es la escrita.
options.en: So the real time is the Nica one and the other is the written one.
options.feedback: That is it exactly. Nobody is being rude and nobody is late, because everybody except you is reading the same clock.

options.en: I have noticed.
options.feedback: You have, at the cost of two hours of chairs.

options.es: Eso es una falta de respeto con usted.
options.en: That is disrespectful to you.
options.feedback: She does not think so and she would have been horrified if they had turned up at twelve, because nothing was ready.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Así es aquí, mijo. Pero ya sabés: para la otra, venite a la una.
steps.en: That is how it is here, love. But now you know: next time, come at one.

options.es: A la una y media, mejor. Con hambre.
options.en: Half past one, better. Hungry.
options.feedback: You went one better than she did, which is the joke she was fishing for. Arriving hungry is the other half of getting this right.

options.en: One o'clock then.
options.feedback: Agreed. She gave you the number, and by now you can work out the real one yourself.

options.en: I prefer to be on time.
options.feedback: You have just spent two hours carrying chairs for preferring to be on time. The lesson was free and you have refused it.

scenarios.title: Una birra
scenarios.desc: One beer, and the door that opens after eleven
scenarios.setting: Friday, plastic chairs on a corner, a cooler on the floor, and Marcos holding up one finger.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Una birra y nos vamos, vos.
steps.en: One beer and we are off.

options.en: Sure. Like when you say ahorita.
options.feedback: You caught the joke inside his promise. Nobody who has been here two years still believes the one beer.

options.en: All right, just one.
options.feedback: Agreed. He will order the second round and you will still be there at midnight.

options.en: I cannot stay long.
options.feedback: Announcing the exit before the first bottle is opened is a strange way to arrive.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¡Doña! Dos birras bien heladas.
steps.en: Doña! Two beers, good and cold.

options.en: This round is on me.
options.feedback: Getting in early on the rounds is how you stop being the one who never orders.

options.en: Thanks.
options.feedback: Fine tonight. Over a year, the man who only says gracias gets a name.

options.es: Yo pago la mía nada más.
options.en: I will pay for just mine.
options.feedback: Splitting it bottle by bottle is not how that cooler works.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: (llegando sin avisar) Ideay, ¿y no me llamaron?
steps.en: (arriving unannounced) Ideay, and nobody called me?

options.es: Vos siempre caés solo, no hay que llamarte.
options.en: You always turn up on your own, nobody needs to call you.
options.feedback: Given back with a smile. Nobody called him and everybody knew he was coming.

options.en: Sit down then.
options.feedback: Warm and correct. The joke was sitting there unclaimed.

options.en: We did not know you wanted to come.
options.feedback: Too careful. It sounds like he was left out, which now he half was.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: (a las once) Mi papá tenía una moto igualita.
steps.en: (at eleven) My father had a motorbike just like that.

options.en: (listen, and make no joke)
options.feedback: The tone changed. He has not talked about his father in nine years and the whole table just went quiet with him.

options.en: Tell me about him.
options.feedback: Kind, and it asks him to perform it. He will get there on his own.

options.es: Jaja, ¿y qué le pasó a la moto?
options.en: Ha, and what happened to the bike?
options.feedback: You answered the serious register with the joking one. Everybody heard it.

scenarios.title: Se me pasó la mano
scenarios.desc: One step past funny, in a patio that has gone quiet
scenarios.setting: You said something about Chino's new job and the six men in the patio have all stopped talking at once.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ideay, maje...
steps.en: Ideay, maje...

options.es: Se me pasó la mano. Perdoname, Chino.
options.en: I went too far. Forgive me, Chino.
options.feedback: Say it in the same ten seconds, to the man himself, by name. Se me pasó la mano is the exact phrase for having gone one step past the line.

options.en: It was a joke, man.
options.feedback: Everybody knows it was a joke. That is not what went wrong and saying it does not fix it.

options.en: What? Did I say something?
options.feedback: You did, everyone heard it, and pretending not to notice leaves it lying in the middle of the patio all afternoon.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: No, tranquilo. Si es verdad que del otro me botaron.
steps.en: No, it is fine. It is true they did sack me from the other one.

options.es: Igual estuvo de más. No debí decirlo.
options.en: It was still out of order. I should not have said it.
options.feedback: He let you off and you did not take it. Refusing the easy exit once is what makes the apology count.

options.en: All right, it is done.
options.feedback: You took the exit he offered. It closes the afternoon and it does not close the thing itself.

options.es: Ves, entonces no fue tan grave.
options.en: See, so it was not that bad.
options.feedback: He was being generous. Using his generosity as proof that you were right is worse than the joke was.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: El vacilón es del trabajo viejo, no del nuevo. Del nuevo no se toca.
steps.en: The teasing is about the old job, not the new one. You do not touch the new one.

options.es: Ya entendí. Lo que le duele hoy no se toca.
options.en: I understand. What still hurts today is off limits.
options.feedback: That is the line and nobody was ever going to explain it to you in advance. Everything is fair game except the thing that is still open.

options.es: Es difícil saber hasta dónde se puede.
options.en: It is hard to know where the line is.
options.feedback: It is, and you have just been told where it is for this table. That is as close to a rule as you will get.

options.en: You lot say worse things to each other.
options.feedback: They do, and they have twenty years of knowing what each other can take. You have four.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Ya, ya. Andá a traerme una birra y quedamos a mano.
steps.en: All right, all right. Go and get me a beer and we are even.

options.es: Dos te traigo. Y la otra me toca a mí aguantar.
options.en: I will bring you two. And next time it is my turn to take it.
options.feedback: The beer is the repair and offering yourself as the next target is the receipt. That is how it is finished here, not with a long conversation.

options.en: I will bring it right now.
options.feedback: Good enough. He has ended it and you are doing what he asked.

options.es: Traigo la birra, pero de verdad me quedé mal.
options.en: I will bring the beer, but I really do feel bad.
options.feedback: You already apologised twice. A third one asks him to keep forgiving you when he has said it is over.

scenarios.title: El chisme vuelve
scenarios.desc: Something you said in confidence comes back improved
scenarios.setting: Doña Chepa leans over the counter with news about you that you have not heard yet.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ideay, ¿y es cierto que se van del barrio?
steps.en: Ideay, is it true that you are leaving the barrio?

options.es: ¿Quién le dijo eso? Nosotros buscamos casa aquí cerca.
options.en: Who told you that? We are looking for a house near here.
options.feedback: Correcting it at the counter is the fastest way to correct it everywhere. This is where the barrio reads its news.

options.en: No, that is not true.
options.feedback: A denial with no replacement. The old version will keep travelling.

options.es: Eso no es asunto de nadie.
options.en: That is nobody's business.
options.feedback: In this barrio it already is, and now you have made an enemy of the printing press.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ah, entonces no se van lejos.
steps.en: Ah, so you are not going far.

options.es: Tres cuadras. Ni salimos del barrio.
options.en: Three blocks. We are not even leaving the barrio.
options.feedback: A number and a boundary. That is the version that will be repeated tonight, word for word.

options.en: No, just nearby.
options.feedback: Vague, and vague is what gossip fills in.

options.en: We do not know yet.
options.feedback: Uncertainty is the raw material. You have just given her more of it.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Es que me contaron que se iban para afuera.
steps.en: The thing is I was told you were going abroad.

options.es: Fijese que a doña Elena le llegó así y se puso a llorar.
options.en: The thing is, it reached doña Elena like that and she started crying.
options.feedback: Showing the cost, without blaming her, is the one thing that makes a barrio careful about a story.

options.en: Well, no, we are staying here.
options.feedback: Clear and correct. It corrects the fact without fixing the harm.

options.en: You are the one going around saying it.
options.feedback: Probably true. Saying it to her face ends a four-year relationship over a rumour.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ay, no. Yo le aviso a la gente entonces.
steps.en: Oh no. I will let people know, then.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Usted es la que sabe.
options.en: Thank you, doña. You are the one who knows.
options.feedback: You just turned the biggest gossip on the block into your correction service. That is the whole strategy.

options.en: Yes, please.
options.feedback: Fine. It accepts the offer without making her want to do it well.

options.es: Ojalá esta vez salga bien la historia.
options.en: Hopefully the story comes out right this time.
options.feedback: One small barb, and now the correction travels slower than the rumour did.

scenarios.title: No me hallo
scenarios.desc: A word for something you have been feeling for a year
scenarios.setting: You have left a party of thirty people to stand in the patio, and Lucía has come out to find you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Y vos qué hacés aquí afuera? ¿Estás bien?
steps.en: And what are you doing out here? Are you all right?

options.es: Sí, pero no me hallo. Así, de repente.
options.en: Yes, but I do not feel right. Just like that, suddenly.
options.feedback: No me hallo is the word and there is no clean English for it. It is not sadness and not anger, it is not finding your place in a room, and everybody here knows it.

options.en: I feel odd. I do not know.
options.feedback: Close, and it will do. Raro is what you say when you have not got the word yet.

options.en: I feel strange here.
options.feedback: Extraño is for a smell or a noise, and said about yourself in a house full of your wife's family it sounds like you feel foreign in it.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Ah, no te hallás. Eso le pasa a todo el mundo, gordo.
steps.en: Ah, you are not finding your place. That happens to everybody, gordo.

options.es: ¿A todo el mundo? Yo creía que era por ser de afuera.
options.en: To everybody? I thought it was from being a foreigner.
options.feedback: It is not. Nicaraguans say no me hallo about a new job, a new barrio, a party full of their own cousins. The word was never about you being foreign.

options.es: Qué bueno saber que no soy solo yo.
options.en: Good to know it is not just me.
options.feedback: True. Ask her when it happens to her and you will get the whole shape of the word.

options.es: A vos no te pasa, seguro.
options.en: It does not happen to you, surely.
options.feedback: It does. Deciding on her behalf that she has never felt it closes the conversation you came out here for.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Claro que sí. Yo no me hallaba en el trabajo nuevo por meses.
steps.en: Of course it does. I did not find my feet in the new job for months.

options.en: And what did you do? Did it go on its own?
options.feedback: Ask, because the answer is usually time and nothing else. Se me quitó is how you say a feeling left you, as though it had come by itself.

options.en: I did not know that about you.
options.feedback: Warm. There was a practical question sitting right there.

options.en: But that is different.
options.feedback: She just handed you her own version of it. Telling her it does not count is the wrong thing to do with that.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Se me fue solo. Entrá, que ya van a servir.
steps.en: It went on its own. Come in, they are about to serve.

options.es: Ya voy. Dame dos minutos y entro.
options.en: Coming. Give me two minutes and I will come in.
options.feedback: You are not being asked to be cured, only to come back in. Two minutes and the plate is the whole treatment.

options.en: All right, I am coming in.
options.feedback: Fine. Taking the two minutes you actually need is allowed.

options.es: Entrá vos, yo me quedo aquí.
options.en: You go in, I will stay here.
options.feedback: Standing alone in a patio while thirty people eat is how not finding your place turns into being outside it.

scenarios.title: Andate ya
scenarios.desc: Leaving a house, which takes forty minutes
scenarios.setting: Nine at night at doña Carmen's. You have work at six and you have just said the word bueno.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: ¿Ya se van? Pero si acaban de llegar.
steps.en: Are you going already? But you have only just got here.

options.es: Ya va siendo hora, doña. Mañana entro temprano.
options.en: It is getting to be time, doña. I start early tomorrow.
options.feedback: A reason that is not about her, said after the bueno rather than instead of it. The first stage, done properly.

options.en: Yes, we are going now.
options.feedback: Correct, and about thirty minutes early. Standing up now would be abrupt.

options.en: I am tired.
options.feedback: Honest and blunt. In her front room it lands as though the evening wore you out.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Quédense otro ratito. Ahorita hago más café.
steps.en: Stay a little longer. I will make more coffee in a minute.

options.es: Un ratito más entonces, pero sin café.
options.en: A little longer then, but no coffee.
options.feedback: She insisted once, which is obligatory, and you gave her half. Now you can leave in ten minutes without anybody losing.

options.en: All right, one more coffee.
options.feedback: Accepted the whole offer. That is another forty minutes and you have work at six.

options.es: No, de verdad ya nos vamos.
options.en: No, really, we are going now.
