options.feedback: Refusing the first insistence flatly is the one move that stings.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: (en el portón) Y dígale a Lucía que me llame.
steps.en: (at the gate) And tell Lucía to call me.

options.es: Yo le digo, doña. ¿Todo bien con usted?
options.en: I will tell her, doña. Is everything all right with you?
options.feedback: The gate is where the real thing gets said. You noticed and you asked.

options.en: Yes, I will let her know.
options.feedback: A message taken. The gate is where she would have told you why.

options.en: She has her own phone, doña.
options.feedback: True and cold, and it ends the one part of the evening that had something in it.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: Cuidate en el camino, mijo.
steps.en: Take care on the way, son.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Que pase buena noche.
options.en: Thank you, doña. Have a good night.
options.feedback: Warm, correct, and it lets both of you stop. Adiós was never an option.

options.en: Yes, goodbye.
options.feedback: Adiós from a gate you will be back at on Sunday is too big a word.

options.en: See you, I am off.
options.feedback: Ya me voy was thirty minutes ago. Saying it at the gate reopens the whole sequence.

scenarios.title: Depende
scenarios.desc: A yes-or-no question, and twenty minutes
scenarios.setting: You need to know whether the workshop opens on Saturday. That is the entire question.

steps.speaker: Jefe
steps.es: Depende.
steps.en: It depends.

options.en: What does it depend on, boss?
options.feedback: The follow-up that gets you the real answer. Depende is an opening, not a refusal.

options.en: Ah, all right.
options.feedback: You accepted a non-answer. Now you still do not know and you cannot ask again.

options.en: It is yes or no, boss.
options.feedback: It is not, here, and pushing for a flat answer makes him give you the flattest one available.

steps.speaker: Jefe
steps.es: De si llega el material. Y eso depende de la rastra.
steps.en: On whether the material arrives. And that depends on the lorry.

options.es: Entonces, ¿usted qué cree, más probable que sí?
options.en: So, what do you think, more likely yes?
options.feedback: Asking for his estimate rather than his commitment. That is a question he can actually answer.

options.en: I see, thank you.
options.feedback: Polite. You have collected the chain of reasons and none of the answer.

options.en: And who knows that, then?
options.feedback: It sounds like you are saying nobody in the building knows anything.

steps.speaker: Jefe
steps.es: Yo diría que sí. Casi seguro.
steps.en: I would say yes. Almost certain.

options.es: Va pues. Entonces aquí estoy a las siete.
options.en: Right then. So I will be here at seven.
options.feedback: You converted an almost into a plan, out loud, so he can correct it if it is wrong. Nobody has been pinned down.

options.en: Perfect, so you are opening.
options.feedback: He said almost. Repeating it back as certain is putting words in his mouth.

options.es: Entonces es sí. Ya lo dijo.
options.en: So it is a yes. You said it.
options.feedback: Quoting a man's hedge back at him as a promise is how you get a firm no next time.

steps.speaker: Jefe
steps.es: Si acaso no, yo le aviso el viernes.
steps.en: If not, I will let you know on Friday.

options.es: Dale. Y si no me avisa, yo llego.
options.en: Right. And if you do not tell me, I will come in.
options.feedback: You named what silence means, which is the one thing depende never says on its own.

options.en: All right, I will wait for your message.
options.feedback: Fine, and if the message never comes you will not know which way it went.

options.en: Hopefully this time you will actually tell me.
options.feedback: A complaint about the past dressed as a hope. He heard it.

scenarios.title: Tal vez después
scenarios.desc: A no you were given in March
scenarios.setting: You have invited Julio to the lake three times since March. It is August.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: Tal vez después, vos. Ahorita está complicado.
steps.en: Maybe later. Right now it is complicated.

options.es: Va pues. Cuando querrás, avisame vos.
options.en: Right then. Whenever you like, you let me know.
options.feedback: You heard the no and handed him the next move. Nothing is broken and nobody had to say it.

options.en: All right, another day then.
options.feedback: Fine. Otro día from you keeps the invitation alive slightly longer than it should be.

options.en: And next Sunday? And the one after?
options.feedback: Pushing past a soft no is the one thing it is designed to prevent.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: Es que en estos meses ando corto.
steps.en: The thing is these months I am short.

options.es: Ah, va. Si es por eso, yo pongo la gasolina.
options.en: Ah, right. If that is it, I will put in the petrol.
options.feedback: He gave you the real reason, indirectly. Answering it without naming it is exactly right.

options.en: Do not worry about that.
options.feedback: Kind and vague. He needs to know who is paying before he can say yes.

options.es: Pero si no cuesta casi nada.
options.en: But it hardly costs anything.
options.feedback: To him it does. That sentence tells him you have not understood the last four months.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: No, hombre, no es solo eso.
steps.en: No, man, it is not just that.

options.es: Está bien. No te estoy sacando nada.
options.en: All right. I am not trying to get anything out of you.
options.feedback: You let go of it cleanly. That sentence is what tells him the door stays open.

options.en: All right, when you can.
options.feedback: Fine. It leaves a small pull on him that he did not need.

options.en: Then tell me what it is.
options.feedback: He has now told you twice that he does not want to say. Asking a third time is the ofensa.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: Para el veintitrés sí puedo. Ese domingo sí.
steps.en: On the twenty-third I can. That Sunday, yes.

options.en: The twenty-third then. That is settled.
options.feedback: He named a date, which is the only signal that ever meant yes. You closed it immediately.

options.en: Perfect, we will see.
options.feedback: Ahí vemos on a date he finally named puts the vagueness back in.

options.en: Sure this time?
options.feedback: He gave you a date after five months. That is not the moment to doubt him out loud.

scenarios.title: Con todo respeto
scenarios.desc: Correcting a man of sixty-eight
scenarios.setting: Don Emilio's measurement is wrong. You are certain, and he has worked here since before you were born.

steps.speaker: Don Emilio
steps.es: ¿Sí?
steps.en: Yes?

options.es: Con todo respeto, don Emilio, ¿tiene un minuto?
options.en: With all respect, don Emilio, do you have a minute?
options.feedback: The permission comes before the problem. That phrase is what makes everything after it possible.

options.en: Don Emilio, I found a mistake.
options.feedback: The word error, in the first sentence, in a workshop where four people can hear.

options.en: This measurement is wrong.
options.feedback: No greeting, no permission, and the fault named out loud. He will not look at it now.

steps.speaker: Don Emilio
steps.es: Diga pues.
steps.en: Go ahead.

options.es: Yo debo estar equivocado, pero esta medida no me da.
options.en: I must be mistaken, but this measurement does not work out for me.
options.feedback: The mistake stays on your side of the bench until he chooses to pick it up. That is the whole technique.

options.es: Creo que hay un error en el número.
options.en: I think there is a mistake in the number.
options.feedback: Softened with creo, which helps. It still puts the error on his paper.

options.es: Usted puso ciento veinte y son ciento diez.
options.en: You put a hundred and twenty and it is a hundred and ten.
options.feedback: Correct, and it is a verdict delivered in front of the shop.

steps.speaker: Don Emilio
steps.es: (mira el papel treinta segundos) Ah.
steps.en: (looks at the paper for thirty seconds) Ah.

options.en: (wait without saying anything)
options.feedback: He is deciding whether to pick up the pencil. Anything you say in that gap takes the decision away from him.

options.en: Do you see what I mean?
options.feedback: Almost harmless. It also asks him to agree out loud that he was wrong.

options.es: Sí, yo sabía que estaba mal.
options.en: Yes, I knew it was wrong.
options.feedback: Everything you built with the first three sentences, undone in one.

steps.speaker: Don Emilio
steps.es: (cambia el número él mismo) Así sí le da.
steps.en: (changes the number himself) That way it works out.

options.en: Thank you, don Emilio.
options.feedback: Two words and back to work. Nobody mentions it again, which is the point.

options.en: Perfect, thank you.
options.feedback: Fine. Perfecto puts a small spotlight on the correction.

options.en: It is right now, then.
options.feedback: Summarising it out loud is the one thing that turns a private fix into a public one.

scenarios.title: Es que fíjese
scenarios.desc: A job that is not ready, and the man who talks first
scenarios.setting: You come back on Friday at four for welding that was promised for Friday at four.

steps.speaker: Dueño
steps.es: Es que fíjese, don, que se me enfermó el hijo.
steps.en: The thing is, sir, my son fell ill.

options.es: Ay, qué pena. ¿Y ya está mejor el chavalo?
options.en: Oh, I am sorry. And is the boy better now?
options.feedback: You went to the reason before the job. That is what the reason was offered for.

options.en: Ah, I see.
options.feedback: You received it. Asking after the boy is what turns it from an excuse into a relationship.

options.en: And my job?
options.feedback: He is telling you why. Cutting to the work makes the reason worthless and both of you smaller.

steps.speaker: Dueño
steps.es: Ya está mejor, gracias a Dios. Pero no avancé nada.
steps.en: He is better now, thank God. But I made no progress.

options.es: Se entiende. ¿Para cuándo me lo puede tener?
options.en: That is understandable. When can you have it for me?
options.feedback: Accepted, then asked for the new date. That date is the real commitment and it is yours to ask for.

options.en: All right, no problem.
options.feedback: Generous, and it walks out without a date. Now it is nobody's job.

options.en: I needed it today.
options.feedback: True. It also puts a sick child and your bracket on the same scale.

steps.speaker: Dueño
steps.es: El lunes sin falta. A las cuatro.
steps.en: Monday without fail. At four.

options.es: El lunes a las cuatro. Aquí estoy.
options.en: Monday at four. I will be here.
options.feedback: Repeated back, so it exists. That is how a new date stops being another maybe.

options.en: All right, Monday.
options.feedback: Accepted. Without the hour it can become Monday evening.

options.en: I hope so this time.
options.feedback: One line, and the whole thing you both just did carefully is undone.

steps.speaker: Dueño
steps.es: Y disculpe la molestia, de verdad.
steps.en: And I am sorry for the trouble, honestly.

options.es: No se preocupe. A cualquiera le pasa.
options.en: Do not worry about it. It happens to anybody.
options.feedback: Given back cleanly. He will remember that you did not make him pay for it twice.

options.en: All right.
options.feedback: Accepted. Slightly flat for a man who apologised properly.

options.es: Sí, es que me atrasó bastante.
options.en: Yes, it did set me back quite a bit.
options.feedback: He apologised and you invoiced him for it.

scenarios.title: Del norte
scenarios.desc: A country you thought had one accent
scenarios.setting: There is a new man at the workshop, he has said three sentences, and you have understood about half.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: Buenas. Yo soy Wilmer, vengo de Jinotega.
steps.en: Morning. I am Wilmer, I come from Jinotega.

options.es: Mucho gusto, Wilmer. ¿De Jinotega mismo o de por ahí?
options.en: Pleased to meet you, Wilmer. From Jinotega itself or from thereabouts?
options.feedback: Asking whether it is the town or the department is a local question, and it tells him you know the north is not one place.

options.es: Mucho gusto. Yo soy de aquí de Managua.
options.en: Pleased to meet you. I am from here in Managua.
options.feedback: A fair swap, and after four years you have earned de aquí. He will still hear where you started.

options.en: Jinotega? And is that in Nicaragua?
options.feedback: It is three hours away and it grows most of the coffee in the country. That question does not land as a joke.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: De un cafetal por allá arriba. Hablo despacio, dicen aquí.
steps.en: From a coffee farm a bit further up. I talk slowly, they say here.

options.es: Despacio sí, pero yo todavía le agarro poco. Tenga paciencia.
options.en: Slowly yes, but I still only catch a bit. Bear with me.
options.feedback: Honest and it puts you both on the same side. Slower and harder to follow at once is exactly what a different department sounds like.

options.en: I understand you fine.
options.feedback: You do not, yet. Saying so now means the next four sentences go past unrepaired.

options.en: It is that you talk oddly.
options.feedback: He talks like Jinotega. To him it is Managua that talks oddly, and he is being polite about it.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: Es que allá se habla distinto. Cada departamento tiene lo suyo.
steps.en: Up there they talk differently. Every department has its own.

options.es: Yo creía que era un solo acento en todo el país.
options.en: I thought there was one accent for the whole country.
options.feedback: Admit the wrong idea out loud. The country is small enough to cross three departments in a morning and they do not sound the same.

options.en: Yes, they had told me.
options.feedback: Fine. He was offering to explain the north to you and you said you already had it.

options.es: Managua es el acento correcto, pues.
options.en: Managua is the correct accent, though.
options.feedback: Said to a man from the north on his first morning, that is a poor start and it is not true either.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: Ideay, y usted no es de aquí tampoco, ¿verdad?
steps.en: Ideay, and you are not from here either, are you?

options.es: No, pero ya llevo cuatro años. Los dos venimos de afuera.
options.en: No, but I have been here four years now. We both come from somewhere else.
options.feedback: He has just put the two of you in the same boat on purpose. Taking it is worth more on a first morning than anything you could say about yourself.

options.es: No, yo vengo de más lejos que usted.
options.en: No, I come from much further away than you.
options.feedback: True, and it makes the distance the point. He was offering you something else.

options.en: Is it that obvious?
options.feedback: It is, and always will be a bit. He asked kindly and there was a warmer answer available.

scenarios.title: Los dos apellidos
scenarios.desc: A window, a form, and a surname you have not got
scenarios.setting: You are at a window applying for your residence cédula and the woman behind the glass has stopped writing.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Su segundo apellido.
steps.en: Your second surname.

options.es: Fíjese que yo solo tengo uno. Así es en mi país.
options.en: The thing is I only have one. That is how it is where I am from.
options.feedback: Fíjese que is the softener that buys you the next thirty seconds. The answer is still going to cause her a problem, and it will cause it politely.

options.en: I do not have a second surname.
options.feedback: True and flat. She is going to look at you as though you had said you have no mother.

options.en: Put anything.
options.feedback: It goes on the cédula, on every form after it, and on your children's papers. There is no anything.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: ¿Cómo que uno solo? ¿Y el de su mamá?
steps.en: What do you mean only one? And your mother's?

options.es: Mi mamá tiene el suyo, pero allá no se pone.
options.en: My mother has hers, but over there it does not go on.
options.feedback: Explain the system rather than yourself. Here the first surname is the father's and the second is the mother's, and it is the law of the registry, not a custom.

options.es: Es que allá se usa uno solo.
options.en: Over there only one is used.
options.feedback: Enough to move things along. She has never had to fill this box with nothing before.

options.es: Aquí es complicado con dos apellidos.
options.en: It is complicated here with two surnames.
options.feedback: It is not complicated, it is her entire filing system, and she has heard it from every foreigner who reaches that window.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Entonces le pongo solo el paterno. ¿Y su esposa?
steps.en: Then I will put only the paternal one. And your wife?

options.es: Lucía Mendoza Espinoza. Mendoza del papá, Espinoza de la mamá.
options.en: Lucía Mendoza Espinoza. Mendoza from her father, Espinoza from her mother.
options.feedback: Both, in order, and you named which is which. Knowing your wife's two surnames in the right order is not optional here.

options.en: Lucía Mendoza.
options.feedback: Half her name. She will ask you for the other half and you will look like a man who does not know it.

options.es: Ella se llama Lucía, como yo de apellido.
options.en: She is called Lucía, with my surname.
options.feedback: She does not take your surname here. A woman keeps both of hers for life, on every document she will ever sign.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Ah, Mendoza. ¿No será de los Mendoza de Masaya?
steps.en: Ah, Mendoza. She would not be one of the Mendoza family from Masaya?

options.es: Puede ser, quién sabe. Le voy a preguntar.
options.en: Could be, who knows. I will ask her.
options.feedback: Two surnames tell people where a family is from and who it might be. This is not small talk, it is her reading the name.

options.en: I do not think so.
options.feedback: Possibly not. You have no idea, and the honest answer keeps the conversation warm.

options.es: Eso no importa para el trámite.
options.en: That does not matter for the paperwork.
options.feedback: It does not, and she is the person stamping your paperwork. She was being friendly.

scenarios.title: El del billete
scenarios.desc: Four years of paying with his face and never once looking
scenarios.setting: You have handed Marcos a hundred-córdoba note and asked him who the man on it is.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: ¿Que quién es? Maje. Es Rubén Darío.
steps.en: Who is it? Maje. It is Rubén Darío.

options.es: Perdoname la ignorancia. ¿Y qué hizo él?
options.en: Forgive my ignorance. And what did he do?
options.feedback: Own it and ask. Everybody in this country learned him at school and nobody expects to have to explain who he is.

options.en: Ah, yes, I had heard something.
options.feedback: You had not. He can tell, and pretending costs you the explanation.

options.es: ¿Y por qué no ponen un presidente?
options.en: And why do they not put a president on it?
options.feedback: Because they put the poet instead, and that choice is the thing you are supposed to notice.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Es el poeta, maje. No un poeta. El poeta.
steps.en: He is the poet, maje. Not a poet. The poet.

options.es: Ya entendí la diferencia. ¿Y qué escribió?
options.en: I understand the difference. And what did he write?
options.feedback: The article was the whole correction. He is not one poet among several, he is the reason this country thinks of itself as a country of poets.

options.en: All right, the poet.
options.feedback: You repeated it back without asking anything. He is waiting to be asked.

options.es: En mi país nadie conoce poetas.
options.en: In my country nobody knows any poets.
options.feedback: That is exactly the thing not to say to a Nicaraguan holding a banknote with a poet on it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Vos preguntale a Lucía. Ella se sabe los versos de memoria.
steps.en: You ask Lucía. She knows the lines by heart.

options.es: ¿De memoria? ¿Se los enseñaron en la escuela?
options.en: By heart? Did they teach them at school?
options.feedback: They did, to everybody, and most people can still say four lines thirty years later. That is the part that is hard to believe from outside.

options.es: Le voy a preguntar en la noche.
options.en: I will ask her tonight.
options.feedback: Do. The surprise is not the poem, it is that she will not have to look it up.

options.es: Seguro se acuerda de una sola.
options.en: I bet she only remembers one.
options.feedback: She will recite you three and then be annoyed. This is not a small piece of the education here.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Cuatro años cargando su cara en la bolsa y ni sabías.
steps.en: Four years carrying his face in your pocket and you did not even know.

options.es: Cuatro años, sí. Ya me toca ponerle atención al billete.
options.en: Four years, yes. About time I paid attention to the note.
options.feedback: Take the ribbing. He is not really talking about money, he is telling you there is a whole layer of this place you have been walking past.

options.es: Es que nadie me lo había dicho.
options.en: Nobody had told me.
options.feedback: Nobody tells you what everybody knows. That is what makes it worth noticing yourself.

options.en: It is just a banknote, maje.
options.feedback: It is the biggest note in ordinary use and it has a man who wrote poems on it. That is not nothing here.

scenarios.title: De eso mejor no
scenarios.desc: A subject that closes without anybody refusing
scenarios.setting: Six people in the yard, beer, music, and you have just asked something that landed wrong.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: (contesta corto) Sí, está caro el arroz.
steps.en: (answers shortly) Yes, rice is expensive.

options.en: (let the subject go)
options.feedback: The short answer was the whole message. In this yard that is how a no is given.

options.es: Sí, pero yo preguntaba por otra cosa.
options.en: Yes, but I was asking about something else.
options.feedback: He knows what you were asking. Repeating it makes him refuse out loud.

options.en: No, seriously, what do you all think?
options.feedback: Now four people have to find a way out of a room you have closed the door of.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Ideay, subile a esa canción.
steps.en: Ideay, turn that song up.

options.en: Ideay, that song is good.
options.feedback: You took the exit he built and used it. That is the whole skill, and nobody will ever mention it.

options.en: (stay quiet)
options.feedback: Safe. Somebody still has to start the next subject and it might as well be you.

options.en: Turn it down, we are talking.
options.feedback: You have just dismantled the escape route in front of everybody.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Bueno, y de lo del primo de Chino, ¿qué pasó?
steps.en: Anyway, what happened with Chino's cousin?

options.en: Yes, tell me, did he end up going?
options.feedback: You joined the new subject immediately and with interest. The old one is now gone for good.

options.en: Ah, yes, that.
options.feedback: Joined, but limply. Somebody else has to carry it now.

options.en: I will come back to the other thing in a bit.
options.feedback: Announcing that you intend to reopen it is worse than reopening it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: (después, en el portón) De eso no se habla en grupo, vos.
steps.en: (later, at the gate) That is not talked about in a group.

options.es: Ya lo entendí. Gracias por decírmelo.
options.en: I understand now. Thank you for telling me.
options.feedback: He waited for the gate to tell you, which is a kindness, and you took it as one.

options.en: Yes, I realised.
options.feedback: Fine. It is a shade defensive for somebody doing you a favour.

options.en: But nobody said anything to me.
options.feedback: Nobody says anything. That is the thing he is explaining to you.

scenarios.title: El setenta y nueve
scenarios.desc: An old man tells you where he was, and stops before the end
scenarios.setting: Everybody else has gone inside and don Beto has stayed on the acera with you and half a queque.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Yo tenía veintisiete años en esa época.
steps.en: I was twenty-seven back then.

options.en: And where were you, don Beto?
options.feedback: He opened the door himself after four years, so walk through it slowly. Dónde estaba usted is the question people here ask about that year.

options.en: In seventy-nine?
options.feedback: You know which year he means and so does he. Asking him to confirm it makes him say it out loud, which he was avoiding.

options.en: Did you fight in the war?
options.feedback: He has not used that word and he is not going to. Putting it in his mouth is how this conversation ends early.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Aquí mismo. Trabajaba en una ferretería por el mercado oriental.
steps.en: Right here. I worked in a hardware shop over by the eastern market.

options.es: ¿Y cómo se puso la ciudad esos días?
options.en: And what was the city like in those days?
options.feedback: Esos días, la época, cuando pasó lo que pasó. Use his words back at him and he keeps talking; use yours and he stops.

options.en: And did you keep working?
options.feedback: A small question, and he will answer it. He is telling you something bigger than his job.

options.en: And which side were you on?
options.feedback: That is the question nobody asks in this country, and certainly not of a man of seventy-two on his own doorstep.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Rara. La gente joven no se veía de día. Aparecía de noche, en otras partes.
steps.en: Strange. You did not see the young people by day. They turned up at night, in other places.

options.en: I see.
options.feedback: One syllable and then nothing. He is telling the whole thing without a single big word and the only right answer is to let him.

options.en: And you were young too?
options.feedback: He said twenty-seven a minute ago. He is deciding how much more to say and a question moves him along faster than he wants to go.

options.es: Qué jodido lo que pasó aquí.
options.en: How terrible, what happened here.
options.feedback: It is his country and his year. A foreigner summing it up in one sentence closes the subject for good.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Bueno. Ya está bueno de eso. ¿Le sirvo más queque?
steps.en: Well. That is enough of that. Shall I give you more cake?

options.es: Sírvame, don Beto. Y gracias por contarme.
options.en: Go on then, don Beto. And thank you for telling me.
options.feedback: He changed the subject and you let him, and you thanked him for the part he did tell. Four years to get that far, and it ends when he says it ends.

options.en: Yes, thank you.
options.feedback: You took the exit with him, which is right. A word about what he told you would have cost nothing.

options.en: And what happened next, don Beto?
options.feedback: He just told you he is finished. Ya está bueno de eso is a full stop, not a pause.

scenarios.title: Uno nunca sabe
scenarios.desc: Saying I without saying I
scenarios.setting: Doña Elena has asked you something at the sink that you would rather answer sideways.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¿Y usted no piensa volver a su país algún día?
steps.en: And are you not thinking of going back to your country one day?

options.es: Uno nunca sabe, doña. Uno hace planes y después...
options.en: One never knows, doña. You make plans and then...
options.feedback: Uno is the most useful word in the language. It means I and it does not say I, and it leaves the sentence unfinished on purpose.

options.es: No sé, doña. La verdad no sé.
options.en: I do not know, doña. Honestly I do not know.
options.feedback: Honest and exposed. Uno would have said the same thing with a door still open.

options.en: No, never.
options.feedback: Nobody says never about that in this house. Half the family is abroad and the word costs more than you think.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Es que uno se queda pensando en esas cosas.
steps.en: It is that one is left thinking about those things.

options.es: Sí, doña. A uno le da vueltas y no lo dice.
options.en: Yes, doña. It goes round and round and you do not say it.
options.feedback: She used uno and you answered in uno. Both of you are talking about yourselves and neither of you has admitted it, which is exactly the arrangement.

options.en: The same happens to me.
options.feedback: Warm and it drops the cover. She was speaking about herself behind that word and you have just stepped out from behind it.

options.en: Are you thinking about your son, doña?
options.feedback: She was, and she was talking about him in the third person for a reason. Naming him out loud undoes the whole thing.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Y uno se acostumbra, pero no se olvida.
steps.en: And one gets used to it, but one does not forget.

options.en: That is how it is, doña.
options.feedback: Nothing else needed. She has said the hardest thing she is going to say and she said it about nobody in particular.

options.en: With time it passes.
options.feedback: She has just told you it does not. Telling a woman her own feeling will pass is not a comfort here.

options.es: Uno aprende a vivir con eso.
options.en: One learns to live with it.
options.feedback: Correct word, and you have just paraphrased her back at her. Silence would have carried more.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Bueno. ¿Me ayuda con esa cebolla, mijo?
steps.en: Well. Will you give me a hand with that onion, son?

options.en: I will give you a hand, doña.
options.feedback: She has closed it with the onion and you take the onion. Nobody in this kitchen is going to say another word about it.

options.en: Of course, doña.
options.feedback: Fine. Say the thing you are doing and the subject is properly buried.

options.es: ¿Y no quiere seguir hablando de eso?
options.en: And do you not want to keep talking about that?
options.feedback: No. The onion is the answer, and asking her to reopen it makes her say out loud that she does not want to.

scenarios.title: La indirecta
scenarios.desc: A leaking roof, mentioned like the weather
scenarios.setting: Doña Elena has been in your yard for an hour talking about the heat, the gas and her leg.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Y ahí el techo de la cocina goteando desde mayo.
steps.en: And there is the kitchen roof, leaking since May.

options.en: (hear it and not answer yet)
options.feedback: She has thrown it and changed the subject. Answering inside the same minute would tell her you heard a request, which is what she is avoiding.

options.en: What a shame, doña.
options.feedback: Sympathy, which is not what she came for. It leaves the hint on the floor.

options.en: Do you want me to fix it for you?
options.feedback: Naming it as a request forces her to admit she asked, which is the whole thing she was protecting.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Pero bueno. ¿Y el chavalito, cómo va?
steps.en: Anyway. And the boy, how is he?

options.es: Bien, ya camina. (y seguir con eso)
options.en: Well, he is walking now. (and go on with that)
options.feedback: You followed her off the subject. The roof stays where she left it, which is where it is supposed to stay.

options.es: Bien. Volviendo a lo del techo...
options.en: Well. Going back to the roof...
options.feedback: Dragging it back turns her hint into a negotiation.

options.en: Well. And how long has it been leaking?
options.feedback: Investigating the hint is the same as answering it out loud.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: (una hora después) Bueno, ya me voy.
steps.en: (an hour later) Right, I am off.

options.es: Doña, el domingo ando por allá. Llevo la escalera.
options.en: Doña, I am over your way on Sunday. I will bring the ladder.
options.feedback: Offered as your own idea, at the gate, an hour later. That is the answer to an indirecta and it is word-perfect.

options.es: Yo le puedo ayudar con el techo.
options.en: I can help you with the roof.
options.feedback: The right offer, said too plainly. It tells her the hint was received as a request.

options.es: Entonces el domingo le arreglo lo que me pidió.
options.en: So on Sunday I will fix what you asked me for.
options.feedback: She asked for nothing. Saying she did takes the whole thing apart.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Ay, no se moleste, mijo. Después.
steps.en: Oh, do not trouble yourself, son. Another time.

options.es: Si ya voy para allá, doña. Ahí le doy un vistazo.
options.en: I am going that way anyway, doña. I will take a look.
options.feedback: She refused once, which is obligatory. You insisted once, which is also obligatory. Now it is agreed.

options.en: All right, another time if you like.
options.feedback: You took the ritual refusal as a real one. The roof will still be leaking in October.

options.en: Whatever you say.
options.feedback: Same thing, with the door shut behind it.

scenarios.title: Ni modo
scenarios.desc: The drain is still blocked and the water is in the house
scenarios.setting: August, the second flood this year, and Lucía is sweeping water out of the back room.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Se mojó el colchón otra vez.
steps.en: The mattress got soaked again.

options.es: Ya lo saqué al patio. ¿Qué más agarro?
options.en: I have already taken it out to the yard. What else shall I grab?
options.feedback: Doing before saying. In the first ten minutes of a flood nobody wants an opinion.

options.en: How awful, again.
options.feedback: Agreement while she sweeps. Pick something up.

options.es: Es que la alcaldía no hace nada.
options.en: The thing is the town hall does nothing.
options.feedback: True, and there is water in the room. That conversation is for tomorrow.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: (sigue barriendo) Ni modo.
steps.en: (goes on sweeping) Ni modo.

options.es: Ni modo pues. Pasame la escoba grande.
options.en: Ni modo then. Pass me the big broom.
options.feedback: You took the word and got back to work with it. That is exactly what ni modo is for.

options.en: (go on carrying things out in silence)
options.feedback: Fine, and the word was an invitation to be in it together.

options.es: ¿Cómo que ni modo? Hay que reclamar.
options.en: What do you mean, ni modo? We have to complain.
options.feedback: Marcos went eleven times in six years. Ni modo is answer number twelve, not the first.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: (al día siguiente, con café) ¿Vamos el lunes a la alcaldía?
steps.en: (the next day, with coffee) Shall we go to the town hall on Monday?

options.es: Vamos los dos. Llevo las fotos del desagüe.
options.en: Let us both go. I will take the photos of the drain.
options.feedback: The anger has slept a night and now it has a plan and a piece of evidence. That is the other half of ni modo.

options.en: Yes, let us go.
options.feedback: Agreed. Turning up with nothing in your hand is the eleven trips Marcos already made.

options.es: ¿Para qué? No van a hacer nada.
options.en: What for? They will not do anything.
options.feedback: Yesterday you wanted to complain. Ni modo is not supposed to arrive the day after.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Puso música ayer con la casa mojada. ¿Te fijaste?
steps.en: You noticed I put music on yesterday with the house wet?

options.es: Me fijé. Creo que esa era la otra mitad.
options.en: I noticed. I think that was the other half of it.
options.feedback: You worked out that the song and the ni modo were the same thing. Almost nobody from outside gets that.

options.en: Yes, I thought it was odd.
options.feedback: Honest. It leaves her to explain something you nearly understood.

options.en: Yes, it was not the moment.
options.feedback: It was exactly the moment, and telling her so takes something from her.

scenarios.title: El chiste que no explicaron
scenarios.desc: Laughing in real time, or not at all
scenarios.setting: A birthday, thirty people, and Chino is three minutes into a joke you are following completely.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: ...y el cura le dice que ese pescado no era de él.
steps.en: ...and the priest tells him that fish was not his.

options.es: (reírse medio segundo antes que los demás)
options.en: (laugh half a second before the others)
options.feedback: That half second is the whole thing. It cannot be faked and everybody at that table knows it.

options.en: (laugh with the others)
options.feedback: Nobody will notice tonight. Over a year, laughing on the crowd is what marks somebody out.

options.es: ¿Y por qué era gracioso lo del pescado?
options.en: And why was the fish part funny?
options.feedback: Explaining a joke kills it in front of everybody, including the man who told it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Salud, vos.
steps.en: Cheers.

options.en: Cheers.
options.feedback: He raised his bottle and said one word. Answering with one word is the whole exchange; anything longer would spoil it.

options.en: (smile)
options.feedback: Fine. The bottle was worth a bottle back.

options.es: Sí, esta vez sí lo agarré.
options.en: Yes, this time I did get it.
options.feedback: Announcing that you understood is the same as admitting you usually do not.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Este ya se ríe a tiempo. ¿Qué le pasó?
steps.en: This one laughs on time now. What happened to him?

options.es: Cinco años oyéndote a vos. Ya era hora.
options.en: Five years listening to you. It was about time.
options.feedback: The credit goes to him and the joke goes back at him. Both halves right.

options.en: I am learning.
options.feedback: True, and it accepts a compliment where a return was available.

options.es: Siempre me he reído a tiempo.
options.en: I have always laughed on time.
options.feedback: Everybody at that table remembers the two years when you did not.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Bueno, y otro: ¿saben por qué el gallo cruzó la cancha?
steps.en: Right, another one: do you know why the rooster crossed the pitch?

options.en: That one was bad.
options.feedback: Telling a Nicaraguan his joke was bad, to his face, at his own table, is the compliment. It says you are inside.

options.en: (laugh anyway)
options.feedback: Kind. It is also the last thing anybody at that table needed.

options.en: (not laugh and stay serious)
options.feedback: Silence in the joking register reads as something being wrong, not as a verdict on the joke.

scenarios.title: Como decía mi abuela
scenarios.desc: Quoting the dead to end an argument
scenarios.setting: Two months of argument about the old house, and doña Elena has just started telling a story instead.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Mi mamá crió cinco hijos en esa casa.
steps.en: My mother raised five children in that house.

options.en: (listen to the end)
options.feedback: She has stopped arguing and started telling. The story is the argument now, and interrupting it loses it.

options.en: Yes, we knew that.
options.feedback: True, and it hurries a woman who has waited two months to say it.

options.es: Pero eso no cambia los números.
options.en: But that does not change the numbers.
options.feedback: It is about to change everything. You have just told the room you cannot hear it coming.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Como decía mi mamá, una casa no se vende.
steps.en: As my mother used to say, a house is not sold.

options.en: (say nothing at all)
options.feedback: Nobody argues with a dead grandmother. Silence here is agreement and everybody in the room understands it.

options.en: Well, that is true.
options.feedback: Agreement out loud. Slightly more than the moment needs, but harmless.

options.en: And did she really say that?
options.feedback: Asking whether the quote is real is the one question that cannot be asked.

steps.speaker: Julio
steps.es: Bueno, ¿y quién quiere más arroz?
steps.en: Anyway, who wants more rice?

options.en: I do, doña Elena.
options.feedback: The argument is over and Julio said so by asking about the rice. Taking the plate is how you agree.

options.en: (stay quiet at the table)
options.feedback: Fine. Somebody has to make the new subject work and it is easier with two.

options.en: So what did we decide?
options.feedback: It was decided. Asking makes her say it a second time.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: (en el carro) ¿Vos creés que la abuela dijo eso?
steps.en: (in the car) Do you think her grandmother said that?

options.es: Puede que sí o puede que no. Igual era lo que pensaba.
options.en: She may have or she may not. It was what she thought either way.
options.feedback: You understood that the quote finishes an idea the dead woman never put into a sentence. That is exactly how it works here.

options.en: No idea.
options.feedback: Honest. It sidesteps a question she was actually asking you.

options.en: She made it up, definitely.
options.feedback: Perhaps. Saying it out loud makes what happened smaller than it was.

scenarios.title: Ya en serio
scenarios.desc: The tone changes and you have to change with it
scenarios.setting: Friday, the corner, eleven o'clock, and something in Chino's face has just moved.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Bueno... la verdad es que las cosas en la casa están difíciles.
steps.en: Right... the truth is things at home are difficult.

options.es: (dejar de reírse y voltear a verlo)
options.en: (stop laughing and turn to look at him)
options.feedback: La verdad is the signal. Turning your body is how the table answers it, and you were not a beat behind.

options.en: Go on then.
options.feedback: Warm, and it asks him to perform it. He will get there without being asked.

options.en: Ha, and what have you done now?
options.feedback: Answering the serious register with the joking one. The table will go quiet and it will be your fault.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: Mi mujer se quiere ir donde su mamá.
steps.en: My wife wants to go to her mother's.

options.en: (say nothing and wait)
options.feedback: Nobody interrupts in this register. The silence is what lets him finish.

options.en: Damn. That is hard.
options.feedback: Human and correct. It is also a small interruption in a place where none is needed.

options.en: You can sort that out by talking.
options.feedback: Advice in the first thirty seconds. He is not asking for a solution.

steps.speaker: Chino
steps.es: (termina) Bueno. Ya. Eso era.
steps.en: (finishing) Right. That is it. That was it.

options.en: Thank you for telling it.
options.feedback: He gave you something. Saying so once, plainly, is the whole answer.

options.en: We are here.
options.feedback: Warm and true. It is what everybody says, which is fine.

options.en: And what are you going to do?
options.feedback: He has finished. That question puts him back in it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Otra birra, vos. ¿Cómo estuvo la semana?
steps.en: Another beer. How was your week?

options.es: (preguntarle a Chino aparte, en la puerta)
options.en: (ask Chino about it separately, at the door)
options.feedback: Serious things are said once at the table and looked after away from it. That is the rule and you have it.

options.en: (never mention it again)
options.feedback: Safe, and correct on the surface. Asking once, alone, is what makes the difference.

options.es: Chino, ¿cómo va lo de tu mujer?
options.en: Chino, how is the thing with your wife going?
options.feedback: Said at the table, in front of four people, in the joking register. That undoes the whole of last Friday.

scenarios.title: Béisbol o fútbol
scenarios.desc: An argument nobody wants to win
scenarios.setting: Four young men from the workshop, one bench, and don Emilio sitting behind not saying anything.

steps.speaker: Muchacho
steps.es: El béisbol ya pasó de moda. Eso es de viejos.
steps.en: Baseball is out of fashion. That is for old people.

options.es: Ah, de viejos. Decile eso a don Emilio, ahí está.
options.en: Ah, for old people. Say that to don Emilio, he is right there.
options.feedback: You hooked his own word and turned it round in one line. That is how you enter without pushing.

options.es: No es cierto, mucha gente juega.
options.en: That is not true, lots of people play.
options.feedback: A flat contradiction. It answers with facts, which is where this argument goes to die.

options.en: According to the statistics, baseball...
options.feedback: Numbers end the night. Nobody at that bench came for numbers.

steps.speaker: Muchacho
steps.es: Es que en el mundo entero se ve fútbol.
steps.en: The thing is the whole world watches football.

options.es: En el mundo entero, sí. Aquí no, aquí es otra cosa.
options.en: In the whole world, yes. Not here, here it is another thing.
options.feedback: You conceded the big half and kept the half that matters. Very hard to argue with.

options.en: Well, to each their own.
options.feedback: Agreement, which is the same as leaving the bench.

options.en: Football is boring.
options.feedback: A verdict where a story was called for. Now it is opinions against opinions.

steps.speaker: Muchacho
steps.es: ¿Y vos qué sabés? Si no sos de aquí.
steps.en: And what do you know? You are not even from here.

options.es: Fui al estadio con Marcos hace cuatro años. Contame vos.
options.en: I went to the stadium with Marcos four years ago. You tell me.
options.feedback: A memory beats a credential. It also invites him to keep going instead of shutting him down.

options.en: I have been here five years.
options.feedback: True, and it argues about your right to be in the conversation rather than about baseball.

options.en: More than you, certainly.
options.feedback: Now the argument is about the two of you, which is the one thing it was never about.

steps.speaker: Don Emilio
steps.es: (al pasar, le pone la mano en el hombro) Buen juego el domingo.
steps.en: (passing, he puts a hand on your shoulder) A good game on Sunday.

options.en: I will be there, don Emilio.
options.feedback: He ended the argument with a hand and a half-sentence. You answered the half-sentence and left the hand alone.

options.en: Thank you, don Emilio.
options.feedback: Warm. It is also a shade louder than the gesture.

options.en: I am right, am I not, don Emilio?
options.feedback: Recruiting him into the argument after he had ended it with one hand.

scenarios.title: La bulla
scenarios.desc: A speaker on the pavement at one in the morning
scenarios.setting: The neighbour's music has been going since nine and you have come out to the acera, where doña Chepa is already sitting.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ideay, ¿y usted despierto a esta hora?
steps.en: Ideay, and you awake at this hour?

options.en: With that racket, doña, who is sleeping?
options.feedback: Bulla is not a complaint word here, it is a weather word. Saying it like that puts you on the pavement with her instead of above it.

options.es: No puedo dormir con ese ruido.
options.en: I cannot sleep with that noise.
options.feedback: True, and ruido is the neutral word. Bulla is the one this street uses and it carries no accusation.

options.en: That ought to be banned.
options.feedback: You are five years in and proposing a law about the neighbour's speaker. Doña Chepa will remember that sentence.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Es el cumpleaños de la nieta. Una vez al año, pues.
steps.en: It is the granddaughter's birthday. Once a year, after all.

options.es: Ah, con razón. Entonces que la pasen bien.
options.en: Ah, that explains it. Let them enjoy it, then.
options.feedback: The reason changes everything and it always exists. Once you have it, the noise stops being an offence and becomes somebody's party.

options.es: No sabía. Ya al menos entiendo.
options.en: I did not know. At least now I understand.
options.feedback: Fair. Half a step short of wishing them well, which is the part that gets repeated tomorrow.

options.es: Una vez al año hasta las tres de la mañana.
options.en: Once a year until three in the morning.
options.feedback: She gave you the reason so that you would let it go. Answering with the hour tells her you have not.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Mi hija dice que a las doce lo bajan. Vamos a ver.
steps.en: My daughter says they will turn it down at twelve. We will see.

options.es: Vamos a ver, doña. Aquí me quedo un rato con usted.
options.en: We will see, doña. I will sit out here with you a while.
options.feedback: Vamos a ver means it is not happening and both of you know it. Sitting down instead of going in is the only real solution anybody has found.

options.en: Let us hope so.
options.feedback: Kind. It will not go down at twelve and she was warning you rather than promising.

options.es: ¿Y si les pedimos que le bajen?
options.en: And what if we ask them to turn it down?
options.feedback: Nobody asks. It is a fifteen-year-old's birthday and asking makes an enemy on a street you will live on for another twenty years.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Al principio usted no aguantaba nada de bulla. ¿Se acuerda?
steps.en: At the start you could not stand any noise at all. Do you remember?

options.es: La primera noche no dormí nada, doña. Ya ni la oigo.
options.en: The first night I did not sleep at all, doña. Now I do not even hear it.
options.feedback: That is the whole five years in one sentence. The noise was the first thing that nearly sent you home, and you stopped noticing it some year you cannot name.

options.en: Yes, I got used to it.
options.feedback: True. She asked because she has been watching it happen and wanted to hear you say it.

options.es: Todavía no me acostumbro del todo.
options.en: I am still not entirely used to it.
options.feedback: Honest, and you are sitting on a pavement at one in the morning talking to a neighbour instead of lying awake being angry. That is used to it.

scenarios.title: ¿Y usted de dónde es?
scenarios.desc: The same question as always, answered in a different order
scenarios.setting: Somebody you have never met has sat down beside you at a lunch and asked the question everybody asks.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: ¿Y usted de dónde es?
steps.en: And where are you from?

options.es: Vivo aquí, en el barrio de abajo. Vine de afuera hace cinco años.
options.en: I live here, in the barrio down the road. I came from abroad five years ago.
options.feedback: That order is the whole trick. Where you live first, where you came from second, and the conversation goes somewhere instead of stopping to look at you.

options.es: Yo soy de afuera, pero vivo aquí.
options.en: I am from abroad, but I live here.
options.feedback: The same two facts the other way round, and now the next four questions are about your country.

options.en: From very far away.
options.feedback: It sounds mysterious and it makes him work. He asked the first friendly question anybody asks in this country.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: Ah, ¿del barrio de abajo? ¿Y por dónde vive exactamente?
steps.en: Ah, the barrio down the road? And whereabouts exactly do you live?

options.es: De la iglesia dos cuadras al lago y media abajo.
options.en: From the church two blocks towards the lake and half a block down.
options.feedback: Landmark, blocks, direction. Five years ago that sentence was a puzzle and now it comes out of you without thinking.

options.en: Near the church.
options.feedback: He will nod and he will not know where you live. The full address takes six words more.

options.en: I can send you a map.
options.feedback: Nobody sends a pin at a lunch table. He was placing you in the city, not trying to find your gate.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: ¡Ideay! Yo tengo una hermana por ahí. ¿Conoce a los Espinoza?
steps.en: Ideay! I have a sister over there. Do you know the Espinoza family?

options.es: Espinoza es el apellido de mi suegra. Vaya a saber si son.
options.en: Espinoza is my mother-in-law's surname. Who knows if they are the same lot.
options.feedback: This is what surnames are for. Two people who have never met can place each other in about four moves, and you have just made yours.

options.en: No, I do not know them.
options.feedback: Probably true. Espinoza is also your mother-in-law's name, which was worth mentioning.

options.en: That is a very common surname, is it not?
options.feedback: It is, and that is not the game. He is trying to find the person you both know and you have just closed the search.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: Puede ser, puede ser. ¿Y hace cuánto me dijo que vino?
steps.en: Could be, could be. And how long did you say you have been here?

options.es: Cinco años ya. Aunque a veces se siente que más.
options.en: Five years now. Though sometimes it feels like more.
options.feedback: Short and it opens a door without leaning on it. He has stopped asking about your country entirely, which is what the reordering was for.

options.en: Five years.
options.feedback: Accurate. Half a sentence more and he would have had something to answer.

options.es: Cinco años, pero todavía me falta mucho.
options.en: Five years, but I still have a long way to go.
options.feedback: Modest, and it puts you back outside. He had already stopped treating you as a visitor.

scenarios.title: Ideay, y vos qué
scenarios.desc: Five years before anybody asks you what you actually think
scenarios.setting: You are on the corner with Marcos, he has been talking about a cousin who wants to leave, and he has turned to face you.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ideay, ¿y vos qué? ¿Vos qué pensás de este país?
steps.en: Ideay, and you? What do you think of this country?

options.en: Do you really want me to tell you?
options.feedback: Check first, because for five years that question has meant do you like the lake. This time it does not, and he will say so.

options.en: I like it a lot, honestly.
options.feedback: That is the tourist answer and he has heard you give it two hundred times. He asked a different question tonight.

options.en: That is a big question, maje.
options.feedback: It is, and he knows. Buying a second does no harm as long as you then answer it.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Sí, hombre. De verdad. Ya llevás cinco años aquí.
steps.en: Yes, man. Really. You have been here five years now.

options.es: Que es el país más difícil que conozco y no me quiero ir.
options.en: That it is the hardest country I know and I do not want to leave.
options.feedback: Both halves in one sentence. Anything that is only praise or only complaint tells him you are still outside it.

options.es: Que la gente es lo mejor que tiene.
options.en: That the people are the best thing about it.
options.feedback: True and it is what every visitor says. He is standing there waiting for the other half.

options.en: That it still has a long way to go.
options.feedback: A verdict on somebody else's country delivered from the corner. Even when it is true, that sentence needs to be his, not yours.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Difícil por qué. Contame.
steps.en: Hard why. Tell me.

options.es: Por lo que le pasa a tu primo. Por eso se va.
options.en: Because of what is happening to your cousin. That is why he is going.
options.feedback: You answered with the thing he was already talking about instead of a general opinion. That is arguing about a country from inside it.

options.en: Because of the money, above all.
options.feedback: Right and broad. Naming his cousin would have made it a conversation instead of an assessment.

options.es: Por muchas cosas que mejor no digo.
options.en: For a lot of reasons I had better not say.
options.feedback: He asked you straight after five years of not asking. Hiding behind mejor no digo wastes the one time it was a real question.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ideay. Y aun así te quedás.
steps.en: Ideay. And even so you stay.

options.es: Aquí está mi mujer, mi hijo y vos. ¿Para dónde me voy a ir?
options.en: My wife is here, my son is here and so are you. Where would I go?
options.feedback: The answer is a list of people, which is the only answer that means anything on that corner.

options.en: I am staying, yes.
options.feedback: Enough. He gave you the whole opening and you used four words of it.

options.en: For now, we will see later.
options.feedback: Said to a man whose cousin is leaving next month, por ahora sounds like one foot already out of the door.

scenarios.title: Confianza
scenarios.desc: Explaining a word to somebody who arrived last week
scenarios.setting: Tom got here nine days ago, he has a notebook, and he has just asked you what confianza means.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: ¿Qué es eso de confianza? Yo lo entiendo como confiar, ¿verdad?
steps.en: What is this confianza thing? I take it as confiar, right?

options.es: Más o menos, pero no. Es un permiso que se gana con años.
options.en: More or less, but no. It is a permission you earn over years.
options.feedback: Confiar is what a bank does. Confianza is being able to walk in without knocking, and there is no word for that on the other side.

options.es: Sí, es más o menos eso.
options.en: Yes, it is more or less that.
options.feedback: It is not, and he will spend a year using it wrong because you did not want to complicate his ninth day.

options.en: It cannot be translated.
options.feedback: True and useless. It cannot be translated, so explain it in Spanish, which is what you now know how to do.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: ¿Un permiso para qué?
steps.en: A permission for what?

options.es: Para entrar sin tocar. Para agarrar un vaso sin pedirlo.
options.en: To walk in without knocking. To take a glass without asking for it.
options.feedback: Two concrete pictures beat any definition. That is how you explain a word inside the language instead of around it.

options.es: Para tratar a alguien sin tanto cuidado.
options.en: To deal with somebody less carefully.
options.feedback: Accurate and abstract. Nine days in, he needs the door and the glass.

options.es: Ya lo vas a ir sintiendo.
options.en: You will get a feel for it.
options.feedback: He will, in about two years. He asked now and you have the answer now.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: ¿Y cómo sé si alguien me tiene confianza?
steps.en: And how do I know if somebody has confianza with me?

options.es: Cuando te empiecen a corregir. A la visita no se le corrige.
options.en: When they start correcting you. You do not correct a guest.
options.feedback: That is the test and somebody had to tell you it too. Being corrected is the promotion, and until then everything you do wrong is politely absorbed.

options.es: Cuando te inviten a comer sin avisar.
options.en: When they feed you without warning you.
options.feedback: A good sign and it happens on day one, to everybody. The correction is the one that only happens later.

options.es: Cuando te digan que sí a todo.
options.en: When they say yes to everything.
options.feedback: That is the opposite. Yes to everything is what people say to somebody they are still being careful with.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: Ideay. Voy a apuntar eso.
steps.en: Ideay. I am going to write that down.

options.es: Apuntalo, sí. Yo tenía un cuaderno igual.
options.en: Write it down, yes. I had a notebook just like that.
options.feedback: You had one, you filled it, and somebody stood on a corner explaining words to you. This is the same afternoon from the other side.

options.en: Go on, write it down.
options.feedback: Fine. Telling him you had the same notebook is worth more to him than the definition was.

options.en: There is no need to write that down.
options.feedback: There is. It took you three years to work out and he can have it on his ninth day.

scenarios.title: Otro chele
scenarios.desc: Somebody arrives with the notebook you used to have
scenarios.setting: Tom has been in the country three months, speaks careful Spanish, and has just said tú to don Emilio.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: Le dije tú y él se dio la vuelta. ¿Hice algo mal?
steps.en: I said tú to him and he turned away. Did I do something wrong?

options.es: Aquí es vos, o usted. El tú suena a telenovela.
options.en: Here it is vos, or usted. Tú sounds like a soap opera.
options.feedback: The rule and the reason it matters, in one line he will remember.

options.en: Yes, here you say vos.
options.feedback: Correct and thin. He will use vos with the boss tomorrow.

options.es: No te preocupés, ya se le pasa.
options.en: Do not worry, he will get over it.
options.feedback: He will. Tom will also do it again on Thursday.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: ¿Y cuál es la regla de cuándo va cada uno?
steps.en: And what is the rule for when each one goes?

options.es: No hay una regla. Hay como veinte y se aprenden oyendo.
options.en: There is no rule. There are about twenty and you learn them by listening.
options.feedback: Honest, and it is the answer you were given. Inventing a rule would send him in the wrong direction for a year.

options.es: A los viejos usted, a los del taller vos.
options.en: Usted to old people, vos to the workshop men.
options.feedback: A useful first approximation that will fail him in about six places.

options.es: Con el tiempo te sale solo.
options.en: With time it comes out on its own.
options.feedback: True and useless today. Give him the two he needs this week.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: Entonces el cuaderno no me sirve de nada.
steps.en: So the notebook is no use to me at all.

options.es: Sirve. A mí me sirvió. Pero lo otro se agarra estando.
options.en: It is of use. It was to me. But the rest is picked up by being here.
options.feedback: You did not take his method away from him. You put it in its place, which is what somebody did for you.

options.en: Not much, honestly.
options.feedback: Blunt. He has three months invested in that notebook.

options.en: Throw it away. That is no use.
options.feedback: You wrote refranes in one for a month. Do not tell him that.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: (en diciembre, en tu portón) Gracias.
steps.en: (in December, at your gate) Thank you.

options.es: (quedarse hablando en el portón veinte minutos)
options.en: (stay talking at the gate for twenty minutes)
options.feedback: He said thank you and did not leave, which means he is waiting for the goodbye to take its proper length. You are teaching him without saying a word.

options.es: De nada. Nos vemos el lunes.
options.en: You are welcome. See you Monday.
options.feedback: Kind and quick. Quick is the one thing a Nicaraguan goodbye is not.

options.en: Right then, take care.
options.feedback: The right words, thirty minutes early. He will learn to leave like a foreigner.

scenarios.title: Nadie preguntó
scenarios.desc: Ten minutes at a bus stop
scenarios.setting: A stop in the centre, Tuesday afternoon, savage heat, and a man of about fifty starts talking to you.

steps.speaker: Señor
steps.es: Está bravo el calor este año, ¿verdad?
steps.en: The heat is fierce this year, is it not?

options.es: Peor que el año pasado. Y todavía falta agosto.
options.en: Worse than last year. And August is still to come.
options.feedback: You agreed and added to it. That is a conversation starting rather than a question being answered.

options.en: Yes, very hot.
options.feedback: Correct, and it stops. He opened a door and you stood in it.

options.en: Yes, very hot here.
options.feedback: One word of the other language and the next ten minutes are about where you are from.

steps.speaker: Señor
steps.es: A mí se me metió el agua en agosto pasado.
steps.en: The water got into my place last August.

options.es: A mí también, y el desagüe de mi cuadra sigue tapado.
options.en: Mine too, and the drain on my block is still blocked.
options.feedback: Your own story, in the same register, with a complaint everybody in this city shares. Nothing about you is foreign in that sentence.

options.en: How awful. I am sorry.
options.feedback: Sympathy from outside. It is the register of a visitor.

options.en: And did you not complain to the town hall?
options.feedback: Advice. He has lived here fifty years and knows what the town hall does.

steps.speaker: Señor
steps.es: Uno reclama y nada. Ni modo.
steps.en: One complains and nothing. Ni modo.

options.en: Ni modo, then.
options.feedback: Two words, and they are the two words a stranger at a bus stop expects back. Nothing at all remarkable happened.

options.en: Yes, that is how it is.
options.feedback: True. It agrees without joining him.

options.en: One has to insist more.
options.feedback: Advice again, and it is the sentence somebody who has not lived it says.

steps.speaker: Señor
steps.es: (subiendo al bus) Que le vaya bien, joven.
steps.en: (getting on the bus) All the best, young man.

options.en: Likewise, sir. Good afternoon.
options.feedback: Ordinary, warm and finished. He never asked where you are from, and it only counts because you did not notice while it was happening.

options.en: Thanks, likewise.
options.feedback: Correct, and a shade clipped for ten minutes of company.

options.en: Thanks. And sorry about the accent.
options.feedback: He did not mention it once in ten minutes. Bringing it up throws away the only thing that happened.

scenarios.title: Ya sos nica
scenarios.desc: An ordinary Saturday, and somebody says it out loud
scenarios.setting: It is eleven thirty on a Saturday at doña Elena's, there are twenty people between the patio and the kitchen, and nothing is being celebrated.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: Póngale sal a esa olla, mijo. Usted ya sabe cuánto.
steps.en: Put salt in that pot, son. You know how much by now.

options.en: Three fingers, like you.
options.feedback: She stopped measuring years ago and so have you. Nobody in that kitchen is going to remark on it, which is the point.

options.en: About how much, doña?
options.feedback: You know. Asking hands the decision back to her when she has just handed it to you.

options.en: Better if you put it in.
options.feedback: She asked because it does not matter any more who does it. Handing the pot back puts you two years into the past.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Ideay, ¿y este a qué hora llegó?
steps.en: Ideay, and what time did this one get here?

options.es: A las once y media, don Beto. La hora buena.
options.en: Half past eleven, don Beto. The right hour.
options.feedback: They said eleven. You came at half past, which is the hour the invitation actually meant, and saying so out loud is the joke he was setting up.

options.en: A little while ago.
options.feedback: Fine. The half hour is the funny part and you left it out.

options.en: At eleven, like they said.
options.feedback: You did not, and everybody saw you arrive. Five years ago you would have, and that is the joke.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Miren a este. Ya sos nica, vos.
steps.en: Look at this one. You are a nica now, you are.

options.en: An adopted nica, don Beto.
options.feedback: Take it and hand a bit of it back. Claiming it whole would be too much and refusing it would be worse, and adoptivo is the word people use.

options.en: Thank you, don Beto. Truly.
options.feedback: Warm, and it treats it as a compliment. It is more like a decision the room has made.

options.en: Not yet, don Beto.
options.feedback: He said it in front of twenty people, which is how these things are made official here. Arguing with it argues with all of them.

steps.speaker: Doña Elena
steps.es: ¿Y ese chavalo suyo dónde anda? Que venga a comer.
steps.en: And where is that boy of yours? Tell him to come and eat.

options.es: Ahí anda con los primos. Ya lo llamo, doña.
options.en: He is off with his cousins. I will call him, doña.
options.feedback: Your son is somewhere in a house full of people who are all his family. Nobody has explained anything to you in about two years and you did not need it.

options.en: He is playing outside.
options.feedback: True. Con los primos is the part that says where he actually belongs.

options.en: He ate at home.
options.feedback: That has never once been an acceptable answer in this kitchen, and you learned it in your first month.

emergency.title: If you are hurt or ill

phrases.es: ¿Me puede ayudar a llamar a alguien?
phrases.en: Can you help me call someone?

phrases.es: No entiendo. Más despacio, por favor.
Lléveme a esta dirección, por favor.
phrases.en: Take me to this address, please.
No thank you. Leave me alone.

phrases.es: Voy a llamar a la policía.
phrases.en: I'm going to call the police.
